children.translated_text:
<s>Śrī</s>.
<s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s> (The Mirror of Literary Composition).
Verses (<s>kārikā</s>) only.

(1)
First Section (<s>Prakāśa</s>).

children.text: śarad-indu-sundara-ruciś cetasi sā me girāṃ devī /
children.translated_text: May the Goddess of Speech, whose beauty is like the autumn moon, in my mind,

children.text: apahṛtya tamaḥ santatam arthān akhilān prakāśayatu // VisSd_1.1 //
children.translated_text: having removed darkness, constantly illuminate all objects. ||1||
Since even persons of little intellect can easily obtain the fruits of the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>)

children.text: kāvyād eva yatas tena tat-svarūpaṃ nirūpyate // VisSd_1.2 //
children.translated_text: from <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) alone, therefore its essential nature is being ascertained. ||2||
<s>Kāvya</s> is that which has <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) as its soul; <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are what diminish it;
<s>guṇas</s> (qualities), <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), and <s>rītis</s> (styles) are declared to be the causes of its excellence. ||3||

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe kāvya-svarūpa-nirūpaṇo nāma
prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter (<s>pariccheda</s>) in the <s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s>, entitled 'The Ascertainment of the Nature of <s>Kāvya</s>.'

(2)
Second Section (<s>Prakāśa</s>).
A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a collection of words possessing fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>), expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), and contiguity (<s>sannidhi</s>);

children.text: vākyoccayo mahā-vākyam itthaṃ vākyaṃ dvidhā matam // VisSd_2.1 //
children.translated_text: a collection of sentences is a great sentence (<s>mahāvākya</s>) — thus the sentence is regarded as twofold. ||1||
Phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) fit for use and conveying a single connected meaning constitute a word (<s>pada</s>);

children.text: artho vācyaś ca lakṣyaś ca vyaṅgaś ceti tridhā matā // VisSd_2.2 //
children.translated_text: meaning is regarded as threefold: expressed (<s>vācya</s>), indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>), and suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). ||2||
The expressed meaning is understood through denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>); the indicated meaning through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>);

children.text: vyaṅgyo vyañjanayā tāḥ syus tisraḥ śabdasya śaktayaḥ // VisSd_2.3 //
children.translated_text: the suggested through suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>) — these are the three powers of a word. ||3||
Among these, the first [denotation] is considered [primary] because it makes known the conventionally signified meaning;

children.text: saṅketo gṛhyate jātau guṇa-dravya-kriyāsu ca // VisSd_2.4 //
children.translated_text: convention is grasped with respect to genus (<s>jāti</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), substance (<s>dravya</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>). ||4||
When the primary meaning is obstructed, the power called <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is assigned,

children.text: rūḍheḥ prayojanād vāpi lakṣaṇā śaktir arpitā // VisSd_2.5 //
children.translated_text: by which, in connection with that [primary meaning], another meaning is apprehended — either through convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) or through purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). ||5||
The setting aside of the primary meaning in favor of another, for the establishment of the sentence-meaning,
through the adoption of oneself [i.e., the primary meaning] — this is called <s>upādāna-lakṣaṇā</s> (inclusion-indication). ||6||
The dedication of oneself to the sentence-meaning for the establishment of another's connection,
through being the ground of a secondary designation — this is called <s>lakṣaṇā-lakṣaṇā</s> (indicatory indication). ||7||
Through superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) and determination (<s>adhyavasāna</s>) respectively, these too are each twofold:
that which produces the cognition of identity of the subject whose [own nature] is not absorbed with another
is the <s>sāropā</s> (superimpositive) type; that of the absorbed [subject] is regarded as <s>sādhyavasānikā</s> (determinative);

children.text: sādṛśyetara-saṃbandhāḥ śuddhās tāḥ sakalā api // VisSd_2.9 //
children.translated_text: those based on relations other than similarity, and the pure ones — all of these ||8-9||

children.text: sādṛśyāt tu matā gauṇyas tena ṣoḍaśa-bhedikā /
children.translated_text: and those based on similarity are regarded as <s>gauṇī</s> (secondary) — thus [lakṣaṇā is] of sixteen varieties;

children.text: vyaṅgyasya gūḍhāgūḍhatvād dvidhā syuḥ phala-lakṣaṇā // VisSd_2.10 //
children.translated_text: through the concealed and unconcealed nature of the suggested meaning, they become twofold in their function. ||10||
Through the function pertaining to the qualified (<s>dharmin</s>) and the qualifier (<s>dharma</s>), these too are each twofold;

children.text: tad evaṃ lakṣaṇābhedāś catvāriṃśan matā budhaiḥ // VisSd_2.11 //
children.translated_text: thus the varieties of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> are considered by the wise to be forty. ||11||
Through being at the level of the word (<s>pada</s>) or the sentence (<s>vākya</s>), each of these too is twofold;
when denotation and the rest have ceased, another meaning is made known — ||12||

children.text: sā vṛttir vyañjanā nāma śabdasyārthādikasya ca /
children.translated_text: that function is called <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion), of both the word and the meaning and the rest;
the <s>vyañjanā</s> of a word is twofold: based on denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>) and based on indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). ||13||
When a word having multiple meanings is restricted to one meaning by association and other [factors],
the [function] that causes the cognition of another [meaning] is <s>vyañjanā</s> based on denotation. ||14||

children.text: lakṣaṇopāsyate yasya kṛte tat tu prayojanam /
children.translated_text: That for whose sake indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is employed — that [meaning] is its purpose;

children.text: yayā pratyākhyāyate sā syād vyañjanā lakṣaṇāśrayā // VisSd_2.15 //
children.translated_text: the [function] by which it is communicated — that is <s>vyañjanā</s> based on indication. ||15||
Through the distinctiveness of the speaker, the person to be informed, the sentences, the proximity of others, the expressed meaning,
the occasion, place, time, tone of voice, gesture, and the like — ||16||

children.text: vaiśiṣṭyād anyam arthaṃ yā bodhayet sārtha-saṃbhavā /
children.translated_text: that which makes known another meaning, arising from the meaning [of words] —

children.text: traividhyād iyam arthānāṃ pratyekaṃ trividhā matā // VisSd_2.17 //
children.translated_text: this [vyañjanā of meaning], through the threefold [nature] of meanings, is regarded as threefold for each. ||17||
The meaning known through words suggests [further]; the word too, depending on another meaning, [suggests];

children.text: ekasya vyañjakatve tad anyasya sahakāritā // VisSd_2.18 //
children.translated_text: when one is the suggester, the other functions as an auxiliary. ||18||
Through the distinctiveness of the three conditions — denotation, indication, and suggestion —

children.text: śabdo 'pi vācakas tadval lakṣako vyañjakas tathā // VisSd_2.19 //
children.translated_text: the word too is regarded as threefold: denotative, indicative, and suggestive. ||19||
The function called <s>tātparya</s> (purport) is said [to operate] in the cognition of the connection of word-meanings;

children.text: tātparyārthaṃ tad-arthaṃ ca vākyaṃ tad-bodhakaṃ pare // VisSd_2.20 //
children.translated_text: its meaning is the purported meaning; others [say] the sentence that conveys it [is called <s>tātparya</s>]. ||20||

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe vākya-svarūpa-nirūpaṇo nāma
dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter in the <s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s>, entitled 'The Ascertainment of the Nature of the Sentence.'

(3)
Third Chapter (<s>Pariccheda</s>).
When manifested by <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant), <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent), and <s>sañcārin</s> (transitory state),

children.text: rasatām eti ratyādiḥ sthāyī bhāvaḥ sa-cetasām // VisSd_3.1 //
children.translated_text: the permanent mental state (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) such as love (<s>rati</s>) and the rest attains the status of <s>rasa</s> in persons of refined sensibility. ||1||
Through the predominance of <s>sattva</s> (pure being), [it is] of the nature of undivided, self-luminous bliss and consciousness,
devoid of contact with any other object of knowledge, akin to the relishing of <s>Brahman</s>; ||2||
whose life-breath is an extraordinary aesthetic rapture (<s>camatkāra</s>) — by certain percipients
this <s>rasa</s> is savored as non-different from their own form. ||3||

children.text: karuṇādāv api rase jāyate yatparaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: That supreme pleasure which arises even in <s>rasas</s> such as the compassionate (<s>karuṇa</s>) and the rest —

children.text: sacetasām anubhavaḥ pramāṇaṃ tatra kevalam // VisSd_3.4 //
children.translated_text: the direct experience of persons of refined sensibility is the sole authority for that. ||4||

children.text: kiṃ ca teṣu yadā duḥkhaṃ na ko 'pi syāt tad-unmukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if there were suffering in those [rasas], no one would turn toward them;
and the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and other [works] would then become causes of suffering. ||5||
The causation of grief, joy, and the like — for those who have become worldly through worldly association —

children.text: śoka-harṣādayo loke jāyantāṃ nāma laukikāḥ // VisSd_3.6 //
children.translated_text: let grief, joy, and the like arise in the world — let them indeed be worldly. ||6||
For those who have attained the status of unworldly <s>vibhāvas</s> through literary association,

children.text: sukhaṃ sañjāyate tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo 'pīti kā kṣatiḥ // VisSd_3.7 //
children.translated_text: pleasure arises from all of them — so what loss is there? ||7||
Shedding of tears and the like are similarly regarded as due to the melting of the mind;

children.text: na jāyate tad-āsvādo vinā raty-ādi-vāsanām // VisSd_3.8 //
children.translated_text: the relishing of that [rasa] does not arise without the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of love (<s>rati</s>) and the rest. ||8||
The function of the <s>vibhāva</s> and the rest is called <s>sādhāraṇīkṛti</s> (universalization);
through its power, those for whom the crossing of oceans and the like [was impossible] ||9||
the percipient apprehends himself as non-different from that [character];
the awakening of festival and the like [emotions results] from the identification with universality. ||10||
In the leaping of oceans and the like, there is no fault even for ordinary men;

children.text: sādhāraṇyena raty-ādir api tadvat pratīyate // VisSd_3.11 //
children.translated_text: through universalization, love and the rest are similarly apprehended. ||11||

children.text: parasya na parasyeti mameti na mameti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Another's, not another's; mine, not mine' —

children.text: tad-āsvāde vibhāvādeḥ paricchedo na vidyate // VisSd_3.12 //
children.translated_text: in the relishing of that [rasa], no determination of the <s>vibhāva</s> and the rest [as belonging to specific persons] is found. ||12||
For those who have attained the unworldly function of universalization and the rest,

children.text: alaukikatvam eteṣāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ na tu dūṣaṇam // VisSd_3.13 //
children.translated_text: the unworldliness of these is an ornament, not a fault. ||13||
Though in the world [they are] in the form of cause, effect, and transitory [state],

children.text: rasodbodhe vibhāvādyāḥ kāraṇāny eva te matāḥ // VisSd_3.14 //
children.translated_text: in the awakening of <s>rasa</s>, the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest are regarded as causes alone. ||14||
Being apprehended first, each is called a cause;

children.text: tataḥ saṃvalitaḥ sarvo vibhāvādiḥ sa-cetasām // VisSd_3.15 //
children.translated_text: then, combined together, all the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest [function] for persons of refined sensibility. ||15||
By the analogy of the drink-and-relish method (<s>prapāṇaka-rasa-nyāya</s>), when savored, <s>rasa</s> comes about;

children.text: sad-bhāvaś ced vibhāvāder dvayor ekasya vā bhavet // VisSd_3.16 //
children.translated_text: if the <s>vibhāva</s> and the rest are present — either both or even one — ||16||

children.text: jhaṭity anyasam ākṣepe tadā doṣo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: when the other is quickly implied, then there is no fault;
because of its limitation, worldliness, and [consequent] obstruction, ||17||

children.text: anukāryasya ratyāder udbodho na raso bhavet /
children.translated_text: the awakening of love and the rest of the character being imitated does not become <s>rasa</s>;
a dancer who merely displays the form of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) and the like through training and practice ||18||
does not become a relisher of <s>rasa</s>;
but through the apprehension of the literary meaning, he too attains the status of a cultured spectator (<s>sabhya</s>). ||19||
This [rasa] need not be proved in its own existence, because of the invariability of [its] cognition;
since it has the nature of depending upon the aggregate of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest. ||20||

children.text: tasmān na kāryaḥ no nityaḥ pūrva-saṃvedanojjhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is neither an effect, nor eternal, nor devoid of prior experience;

children.text: asaṃvedana-kāle hi na bhāvo 'py asya vidyate // VisSd_3.21 //
children.translated_text: for at the time of non-experience, its existence is not found. ||21||
Nor is it a future [entity]; because of being of the nature of self-luminous bliss and consciousness,
unlike effects and objects to be known — nor is it a present [entity] either. ||22||
Because it is the object of the contemplation of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest for persons of refined sensibility,
and because it is clearly experienced as supremely blissful — ||23||

children.text: na nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ tasya grāhakam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: indeterminate cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka jñāna</s>) is not accepted as its apprehender;
and because of the absence of fitness for verbal expression — nor ||24||
is it apprehended by determinate cognition; nor [is it apprehended] by direct perception (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>);
it is not indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>), nor is its manifestation non-indirect (<s>aparokṣa</s>) — because of its arising from words. ||25||

children.text: tasmād alaukikaḥ satyaṃ vedyaḥ sahṛdayair ayam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, truly, this is an unworldly entity to be known by persons of refined sensibility;

children.text: pramāṇaṃ carvaṇaivātra svābhinne viduṣāṃ matam // VisSd_3.26 //
children.translated_text: the authority here is savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) alone, in the view of the wise who are non-different [from the rasa]. ||26||
Through the accomplishment of this savoring, [rasa's] accomplishment is figurative (<s>upacāra</s>);
its inexpressibility and the like I shall state in the section on suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>). ||27||
Since <s>rasa</s> arises precisely from the identity with the cognition of love (<s>rati</s>) and the rest,

children.text: ato 'sya sva-prakāśatvam akhaṇḍatvaṃ ca sidhyati // VisSd_3.28 //
children.translated_text: therefore its self-luminousness and undividedness are established. ||28||
Those that in the world awaken love and the rest — [they are] <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) in <s>kāvya</s> and <s>nāṭya</s> (drama);
two types of these are remembered: <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulant);

children.text: ālambanaṃ nāyakādis tam ālambya rasodgamāt // VisSd_3.29 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ālambana</s> is the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) and the like, since <s>rasa</s> arises by depending on him. ||29||
The hero (<s>netā</s>) is generous, skilled, well-born, endowed with beauty, form, youthfulness, and enthusiasm,
dexterous, beloved of the people, radiant, clever, and virtuous. ||30||
<s>Dhīrodātta</s> (the self-controlled and exalted), <s>dhīroddhata</s> (the self-controlled and vehement), <s>dhīra-lalita</s> (the self-controlled and amorous),

children.text: dhīra-praśānta ity ayam uktaḥ prathamaś caturbhedaḥ // VisSd_3.31 //
children.translated_text: and <s>dhīra-praśānta</s> (the self-controlled and tranquil) — thus the first [hero] is described as fourfold. ||31||
Not boastful, forbearing, exceedingly grave, of great fortitude,

children.text: stheyān nigūḍhamāno dhīrodātto dṛḍha-vrataḥ kathitaḥ // VisSd_3.32 //
children.translated_text: steadfast, of concealed pride — thus is described the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (self-controlled and exalted) hero, of firm vows. ||32||
Given to deception, fierce, fickle, predominantly possessed of ego and arrogance,
delighting in self-praise — thus is the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (self-controlled and vehement) hero described by the wise. ||33||

children.text: niścinto mṛdur aniśaṃ kalā-paro dhīra-lalitaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Carefree, gentle, constantly devoted to the arts — thus would be the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> (self-controlled and amorous);

children.text: sāmānya-guṇair bhūyān divjādiko dhīra-praśāntaḥ syāt // VisSd_3.34 //
children.translated_text: possessing the general qualities in abundance, a twice-born and the like — thus would be the <s>dhīra-praśānta</s> (self-controlled and tranquil). ||34||
With these [four types combined with] the faithful (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>), bold (<s>dhṛṣṭa</s>), devoted (<s>anukūla</s>), and deceitful (<s>śaṭha</s>) — [there are] sixteen;

children.text: eṣu tv aneka-mahilāsu samarāgo dakṣiṇaḥ kathitaḥ // VisSd_3.35 //
children.translated_text: among these, the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (faithful) is described as one who is equally attached to many women. ||35||

children.text: kṛtāgā api niḥśaṅkas tarjito 'pi na lajjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though having committed an offense, fearless; though rebuked, not ashamed;
though his faults are seen, one who churns out falsehoods — he is the bold (<s>dhṛṣṭa</s>) hero. ||36||

children.text: anukūla eka-nirataḥ śaṭho 'yam ekatra baddha-bhāvo yaḥ /
children.translated_text: The devoted (<s>anukūla</s>) is attached to one alone; the deceitful (<s>śaṭha</s>) is one who, though attached to one,

children.text: darśita-bahir-anurāgo vipriyam anyatra gūḍham ācarati // VisSd_3.37 //
children.translated_text: displays outward affection but secretly acts displeasing toward others. ||37||
Through the threefold [classification] of these — as superior, middling, and inferior —

children.text: uktā nāyaka-bhedāś catvāriṃśat tathāṣṭau ca // VisSd_3.38 //
children.translated_text: the types of heroes are declared to be forty-eight. ||38||
The <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (companion) should be in the distant retinue of the hero; in the account of his incidental affairs,

children.text: kiñcit tad-guṇa-hīnaḥ sahāya evāsya pīṭha-mardākhyaḥ // VisSd_3.39 //
children.translated_text: he is slightly inferior in those qualities; he is indeed the hero's assistant, called <s>pīṭhamarda</s>. ||39||
The assistants of the hero in the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) are the <s>viṭa</s> (libertine), <s>ceṭa</s> (servant), <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester), and others;

children.text: bhaktā narmasu nipuṇāḥ kupita-vadhū-māna-bhañjanāḥ śuddhāḥ // VisSd_3.40 //
children.translated_text: devoted, skilled in humor, capable of dispelling the pride of an angry wife — [these are] the pure [assistants]. ||40||
The <s>viṭa</s> (libertine) lacks the resources for enjoyment; he is clever, knows some portion of the arts,

children.text: veśopacāra-kuśalo vāgmī madhuro 'tha bahu-mato goṣṭhyām // VisSd_3.41 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the manners of courtesans, eloquent, sweet-spoken, and highly esteemed in assemblies. ||41||
Called by names such as <s>Kusuma</s> (Flower), <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), and the like; through his actions, appearance, dress, speech, and the rest

children.text: hāsya-karaḥ kalaha-ratir vidūṣakaḥ syāt sva-karma-jñaḥ // VisSd_3.42 //
children.translated_text: he is a cause of laughter; fond of quarrels — the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) should be one who knows his own role. ||42||

children.text: mantrī syād arthānāṃ cintāyāṃ tadvad avarodhe /
children.translated_text: The counselor (<s>mantrī</s>) should be in the deliberation of affairs, and similarly in the inner quarters;
the <s>Vāmana</s> (dwarf), <s>Ṣaṇḍa</s> (eunuch), <s>Kirāta</s> (tribal), <s>Mleccha</s> (barbarian), <s>Ābhīra</s> (cowherd), <s>Śakāra</s>, <s>Kubja</s> (hunchback), and the like — ||43||
intoxicated, foolish, full of self-conceit, endowed with both low birth and lordship —

children.text: so 'yam anūḍha-bhrātā rājñaḥ śyālaḥ śakāra ity uktaḥ // VisSd_3.44 //
children.translated_text: this one, the unmarried brother or the king's brother-in-law, is called <s>Śakāra</s>. ||44||
In the sphere of punishment: the friend, the prince, the forest-dweller, the feudatory, the soldier, and the rest;

children.text: ṛtvik-purodhasaḥ syur brahma-vidas tāpasās tathā dharme // VisSd_3.45 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ṛtvik</s> (sacrificial priest) and the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) should be knowers of <s>Brahman</s>; likewise, ascetics (<s>tāpasa</s>) in the sphere of <s>dharma</s>. ||45||
The <s>pīṭhamarda</s> and the like are superior; the <s>viṭa</s> and <s>vidūṣaka</s> are middling;
and the <s>Śakāra</s>, <s>ceṭa</s>, and the like are declared to be inferior. ||46||
The <s>nisṛṣṭārtha</s> (one with full authority), the <s>mitārtha</s> (one with limited authority), and likewise the <s>sandeśahāraka</s> (mere message-bearer) —

children.text: kārya-preṣyas tridhā dūto dūtyaś cāpi tathāvidhāḥ // VisSd_3.47 //
children.translated_text: the messenger dispatched for a purpose is of three kinds; and the female messengers (<s>dūtī</s>) are likewise. ||3.47||

children.text: ubhayor bhāvam unnīya svayaṃ vadati cottaram /
children.translated_text: He who, drawing out the sentiments of both parties, himself gives the reply

children.text: suśliṣṭaṃ kurute kāryaṃ nisṛṣṭārthas tu sa smṛtaḥ // VisSd_3.48 //
children.translated_text: and brings about the affair with skill — he is known as the <s>nisṛṣṭārtha</s> (one with full authority). ||3.48||
He who speaks in measured terms about the matter and effects its accomplishment is the <s>mitārtha</s> (one with limited authority).
He who merely conveys the message as spoken is the <s>sandeśahāraka</s> (message-bearer). ||3.49||
<s>Śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>vilāsa</s> (grace), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (depth), <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness), <s>tejas</s> (brilliance),

children.text: lalitaudāryam ity aṣṭau sattvajāḥ pauruṣā guṇāḥ // VisSd_3.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>lalita</s> (delicacy), and <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity) — these eight are the innate (<s>sattvaja</s>) masculine qualities. ||3.50||
Valor, skill, truthfulness, great enthusiasm, devotion,

children.text: nīce ghūṇādhike spardhā yataḥ śobheti tāṃ viduḥ // VisSd_3.51 //
children.translated_text: disdain toward inferiors, and rivalry with superiors — from which <s>śobhā</s> (splendor) [arises], so the learned know it. ||3.51||

children.text: dhīrā dṛṣṭir gatiś citrā vilāse sasmitaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: A steady gaze, a striking gait — in <s>vilāsa</s> (grace), speech with a smile,

children.text: sāṅkṣobheṣv apy anudvego mādhuryaṃ parikīrtitam // VisSd_3.52 //
children.translated_text: and absence of agitation even in disturbances — this is declared as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). ||3.52||
<s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (depth) is freedom from disturbance by fear, grief, anger, joy, and the like.

children.text: vyavasāyād acalanaṃ dhairyaṃ vighne mahaty api // VisSd_3.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhairya</s> (steadfastness) is not wavering from one's resolve even in the face of great obstacles. ||3.53||
When abuse, insult, and the like are inflicted by another,
the inability to endure them even at the cost of life — that is declared to be <s>tejas</s> (brilliance). ||3.54||
Sweetness of speech and dress, and likewise amorous behavior is <s>lalita</s> (delicacy).

children.text: dānaṃ sa-priya-bhāṣaṇam audāryaṃ śatru-mitrayoḥ samatā // VisSd_3.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity) is giving with pleasant words, and equanimity toward enemy and friend alike. ||3.55||

children.text: atha nāyikā tri-bhedā svānyā sādhāraṇā strīti /
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) is of three kinds: <s>svā</s> (one's own), <s>anyā</s> (another's), and <s>sādhāraṇā</s> (common).
She is endowed with the general qualities of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero), as appropriate. ||3.56||
Endowed with modesty, straightforwardness, and the like, devoted to household duties, faithful to her husband — she is <s>svīyā</s> (one's own).

children.text: sāpi kathitā tribhedā mugdhā madhyā pragalbheti // VisSd_3.57 //
children.translated_text: She too is said to be of three kinds: <s>mugdhā</s> (innocent), <s>madhyā</s> (moderate), and <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold). ||3.57||
She whose youthful passion has just arisen, who is reluctant (<s>vāmā</s>) in amorous sport,

children.text: kathitā mṛduś ca māne samadhika-lajjāvatī mugdhā // VisSd_3.58 //
children.translated_text: gentle in love-quarrels, and surpassingly bashful — she is called <s>mugdhā</s> (the innocent one). ||3.58||
The <s>madhyā</s> (moderate one) is skilled in varied love-play, with love and youth fully developed,
slightly bold in speech, and of moderate bashfulness. ||3.59||
Blinded by desire, in the fullness of youth, accomplished in all arts of love,
with elevated emotions and slight bashfulness — the <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold one) dominates the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero). ||3.60||

children.text: te dhīrā cāpy adhīrā ca dhīrādhīreti ṣaḍ-vidhe /
children.translated_text: Each of these [madhyā and pragalbhā] is of three kinds: <s>dhīrā</s> (restrained), <s>adhīrā</s> (unrestrained), and <s>dhīrādhīrā</s> (mixed) — thus sixfold.

children.text: priyaṃ sotprāsa-vakroktyā madhyā dhīrā dahed ruṣā // VisSd_3.61 //
children.translated_text: If the <s>madhyā</s> is <s>dhīrā</s>, she addresses her beloved with sarcastic and crooked words, and burns [him] with anger. ||3.61||
The <s>dhīrādhīrā</s> [madhyā responds] with weeping; the <s>adhīrā</s> with masculine words [i.e., direct verbal attacks].

children.text: pragalbhā yadi dhīrā syāc channa-kopākṛtis tadā // VisSd_3.62 //
children.translated_text: If the <s>pragalbhā</s> is <s>dhīrā</s>, her anger is concealed in form. ||3.62||

children.text: udāste surate tatra darśayanty ādarān bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: She remains indifferent in love-making, while showing courtesy outwardly.

children.text: dhīrādhīrā tu solluṇṭha-bhāṣitaiḥ khedayaty amum // VisSd_3.63 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhīrādhīrā</s> [pragalbhā] distresses him with insolent speech. ||3.63||

children.text: tarjayet tāḍayed anyā pratyekaṃ tā api dvidhā /
children.translated_text: The other [<s>adhīrā pragalbhā</s>] would threaten and even strike [him]. Each of these too is of two kinds,
according to being the junior or senior wife, with respect to the beloved's affection. ||3.64||
Therefore, the varieties of <s>madhyā</s> and <s>pragalbhā</s> are twelve.

children.text: mugdhā tv ekaiva tena syuḥ svīyābhedās trayodaśā // VisSd_3.65 //
children.translated_text: But <s>mugdhā</s> is only one; hence the varieties of <s>svīyā</s> are thirteen. ||3.65||

children.text: parakīyā dvidhā proktā paroḍhā kanyakā tathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>parakīyā</s> (another's woman) is said to be of two kinds: <s>paroḍhā</s> (another's wife) and <s>kanyakā</s> (an unmarried girl).
A <s>paroḍhā</s> whose husband is away on a journey or the like is a <s>kulaṭā</s> (an unchaste woman) devoid of shame. ||3.66||
A <s>kanyā</s> (maiden) is one who has not yet been married, who is bashful and newly youthful.
The <s>sāmānya nāyikā</s> (common heroine), who is bold and skilled in arts, is the courtesan (<s>veśyā</s>). ||3.67||

children.text: nirguṇān api na dveṣṭi na rajyati guṇiṣv api /
children.translated_text: She does not dislike even those without virtues, nor is she attached to those with virtues.

children.text: vitta-mātraṃ samālokya sā rāgaṃ darśayed bahiḥ // VisSd_3.68 //
children.translated_text: Looking only at wealth, she displays affection outwardly. ||3.68||
Even a man she has accepted, when his wealth is depleted,
she, through her mother, would eject him, in expectation of future reunion. ||3.69||
Thieves, eunuchs, fools, those who easily obtain wealth,

children.text: liṅginaś channa-kāmādyā asyāḥ prāyeṇa vallabhāḥ // VisSd_3.70 //
children.translated_text: ascetics with concealed desires, and the like — these are usually her lovers. ||3.70||
Even she, when overpowered by passion, is sometimes truly in love.

children.text: raktāyāṃ vā viraktāyāṃ ratam asyāṃ satyānurāgiṇī // VisSd_3.71 //
children.translated_text: Whether she is attached or detached, the one who truly loves her is the <s>satyānurāgiṇī</s> (one of true attachment). ||3.71||
By their states, these [heroines] become eight, with sixteen varieties:
<s>Svādhīnabhartṛkā</s> (she whose husband is under her control), likewise <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the offended one), and <s>abhisārikā</s> (she who goes to meet her lover); ||3.72||
<s>Kalahāntaritā</s> (she who is separated by a quarrel), <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one), <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s> (she whose husband is abroad),

children.text: anyā vāsaka-sajjā syād virahotkaṇṭhitā tathā // VisSd_3.73 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (she who has prepared the bower), and likewise <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (she who is anxious in separation). ||3.73||
She whose beloved, drawn by the qualities of love-making, does not leave her side,
she who is devoted to various amorous gestures — she is the <s>svādhīnabhartṛkā</s>. ||3.74||
She whose beloved comes to her side bearing the marks of union with another woman,

children.text: sā khaṇḍiteti kathitā dhīrair īrṣyā-kaṣāyitā // VisSd_3.75 //
children.translated_text: she is called <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the offended one) by the learned — stained with jealousy. ||3.75||
She who sends for her beloved, being subject to the power of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love),

children.text: svayaṃ vābhisaraty eṣā dhīrair uktābhisārikā // VisSd_3.76 //
children.translated_text: or who herself goes forth to meet him — she is called <s>abhisārikā</s> by the learned. ||3.76||
If a woman of good family goes forth — shrunk into her own limbs, with ornaments silenced,
covered with a veil — [she is one type of <s>abhisārikā</s>]. ||3.77||
But if a courtesan goes forth — in brilliant and splendid attire, with jingling anklets and bracelets,
with a face beaming with delight — [she is another type]. ||3.78||
If a maidservant goes forth — with speech faltering from intoxication, with eyes wide open from excitement,
with a swaying, undulating gait — [she is yet another type]. ||3.79||
A field, a garden, a ruined temple, a go-between's house, a forest,

children.text: mālā-pañcaḥ śmaśānaṃ ca nadyādīnāṃ taṭī tathā // VisSd_3.80 //
children.translated_text: a garland-maker's [shop], a cremation ground, and the bank of a river and the like — ||3.80||
these are the eight places for the dalliance of women who have thus gone forth

children.text: sthānāny aṣṭau tathā dhvānta-cchanne kutracid āśraye // VisSd_3.81 //
children.translated_text: to meet their lovers, as well as any spot concealed by darkness. ||3.81||

children.text: cāṭukāram api prāṇa-nāthaṃ roṣād apāsya yā /
children.translated_text: She who, out of anger, rejects her lord of life even when he flatters her,

children.text: paścāt tāpam avāpnoti kalahāntaritā tu sā // VisSd_3.82 //
children.translated_text: and afterward suffers remorse — she is the <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (separated by a quarrel). ||3.82||

children.text: priyaḥ kṛtvāpi saṅketaṃ yasyā nāyāti saṃnidhim /
children.translated_text: She whose beloved, though having made an assignation, does not come into her presence —

children.text: vipralabdhā tu sā jñeyā nitāntam avamānitā // VisSd_3.83 //
children.translated_text: she is to be known as the <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one), utterly humiliated. ||3.83||
She whose husband has gone to a distant land due to various duties —
she, afflicted by the sorrow of desire, is the <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s> (she whose husband is abroad). ||3.84||
She who adorns herself while the bower-chamber is prepared,

children.text: sā tu vāsaka-sajjā syād vidita-priya-saṅgamā // VisSd_3.85 //
children.translated_text: she is the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (she who has prepared the bower), knowing of the coming union with her beloved. ||3.85||

children.text: āgantuṃ kṛta-citto 'pi daivān nāyāti yat priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the beloved, though minded to come, does not come by fate,
she who is afflicted by the sorrow of his non-arrival is the <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (anxious in separation). ||3.86||
Thus one hundred and twenty-eight, in the forms of superior, middling, and inferior —
three hundred and eighty-four are the varieties of <s>nāyikā</s> (heroines). ||3.87||
In the illustrative examples [of these], a mingling of one with another is sometimes seen.

children.text: itarā apy asaṅkhyās tā noktā vistara-śaṅkayā // VisSd_3.88 //
children.translated_text: The others too are innumerable — they are not stated for fear of prolixity. ||3.88||
In youth, the innate (<s>sattvaja</s>) [ornaments] of these [heroines] number twenty-eight;
among them, <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), <s>hāva</s> (gesture), and <s>helā</s> (coquetry) — three are bodily. ||3.89||

children.text: śobhā kāntiś ca dīptiś ca m ādhuryaṃ ca pragalbhatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>kānti</s> (radiance), <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>pragalbhatā</s> (boldness),

children.text: audāryaṃ dhairyam ity ete saptaiva syur ayatnajāḥ // VisSd_3.90 //
children.translated_text: <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity), and <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness) — these seven alone are effortless [natural qualities]. ||3.90||
<s>Līlā</s> (playfulness), <s>vilāsa</s> (grace), <s>vicchitti</s> (elegance), <s>bibboka</s> (affectation), <s>kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotion),

children.text: moṭṭāyitaṃ kuṭṭamitaṃ vibhramo lalitaṃ madaḥ // VisSd_3.91 //
children.translated_text: <s>moṭṭāyita</s> (thrilled response), <s>kuṭṭamita</s> (apparent resistance), <s>vibhrama</s> (confusion), <s>lalita</s> (delicacy), <s>mada</s> (pride), ||3.91||

children.text: vihṛtaṃ tapanaṃ maugdhyaṃ vikṣepaś ca kutūhalam /
children.translated_text: <s>vihṛta</s> (bashful silence), <s>tapana</s> (burning in separation), <s>maugdhya</s> (feigned innocence), <s>vikṣepa</s> (distraction), <s>kutūhala</s> (curiosity),

children.text: hasitaṃ cakitaṃ kelir ity aṣṭādaśa-saṅkhyakāḥ // VisSd_3.92 //
children.translated_text: <s>hasita</s> (laughter), <s>cakita</s> (alarm), and <s>keli</s> (sport) — thus [they are] eighteen in number. ||3.92||

children.text: svabhāvājāś ca bhāvādyā daśa puṃsāṃ bhavanty api /
children.translated_text: The natural ones, beginning with <s>bhāva</s> — ten of these occur in men as well.
<s>Bhāva</s> (emotion) is the first disturbance in an otherwise undisturbed mind. ||3.93||
Through the changes of eyebrows, eyes, and the like, which manifest the desire for union —
<s>bhāva</s> itself, when its change is only slightly perceptible, is called <s>hāva</s> (gesture). ||3.94||
<s>Helā</s> (coquetry) is that very [bhāva] when its change is extremely perceptible.
<s>Śobhā</s> (splendor) is the adornment of the body through beauty, youth, grace, enjoyment, and the like. ||3.95||
<s>Kānti</s> (radiance) is the same [śobhā], whose luster is nourished by the god of love.

children.text: kāntir evātivistīrṇā dīptir ity abhidhīyate // VisSd_3.96 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s> itself, when greatly expanded, is called <s>dīpti</s> (brilliance). ||3.96||
<s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) is loveliness in all particular states.

children.text: niḥsādhvasatvaṃ prāgalbhyam audāryaṃ vinayaḥ sadā // VisSd_3.97 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāgalbhya</s> (boldness) is fearlessness. <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity) is constant modesty. ||3.97||
<s>Dhairya</s> (steadfastness) is freedom from self-praise, and an unwavering mental disposition.

children.text: aṅgair veṣair alaṅkāraiḥ premibhir vacanair api // VisSd_3.98 //
children.translated_text: Through limbs, attire, ornaments, loving words, and
gestures prompted by affection — the imitation of the beloved's [behavior] is known as <s>līlā</s> (playfulness). ||3.99||
A distinctive quality in walking, standing, sitting, and the like, and in the actions of the face, eyes, and the rest —
<s>vilāsa</s> (grace) arises from seeing the beloved and the like.
<s>Vicchitti</s> (elegance) is even a slight arrangement of adornment that enhances radiance. ||3.100||
The mingling of a smile, dry weeping, laughter, fear, anger, fatigue, and the like —
that is <s>kilakiñcita</s>, born of joy from the meeting with the most beloved, and so forth. ||3.101||
When the mind is pervaded by his feelings, in narratives and the like about the beloved —
<s>moṭṭāyita</s> is said [to be manifested] through scratching the ear and such [gestures]. ||3.102||
When the hair, breasts, lower lip, and the like are seized, even though delighted, out of flurry —
<s>kuṭṭamita</s> is said to be the shaking of the head and hands. ||3.103||
Due to the haste of joy, passion, and the like in the approach of the beloved and similar [occasions],

children.text: asthāne vibhramādīnāṃ vinyāso vibhramo mataḥ // VisSd_3.104 //
children.translated_text: <s>vibhrama</s> (confusion) is considered to be the inappropriate placement of [gestures like] confusion and the rest. ||3.104||
<s>Lalita</s> (delicacy) is the arrangement of the limbs with tenderness.
<s>Mada</s> (pride) is the alteration [of behavior] born of the conceit of beauty, youth, and the like. ||3.105||
<s>Vihṛta</s> (bashful silence) is considered to be speechlessness even when one should speak, out of bashfulness.
<s>Tapana</s> (burning) is the activity born of the force of desire in separation from the beloved. ||3.106||

children.text: ajñānād iva yā pṛcchā pratītasyāpi vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: An inquiry, as if from ignorance, about a thing that is already known,

children.text: vallabhasya puraḥ proktaṃ maugdhyaṃ tat-tattva-vedibhiḥ // VisSd_3.107 //
children.translated_text: in the presence of the beloved — that is called <s>maugdhya</s> (feigned innocence) by those who know its nature. ||3.107||
Half-completing the arrangement of ornaments, gazing about aimlessly,

children.text: rahasyākhyānam īṣāc ca vikṣepo dayitāntike // VisSd_3.108 //
children.translated_text: telling secrets, and slight <s>vikṣepa</s> (distraction) near the beloved — ||3.108||
<s>Kutūhala</s> (curiosity) is the eagerness in gazing at a charming object.
<s>Hasita</s> (laughter) is causeless laughter, arising from the bursting forth of youth. ||3.109||
<s>Cakita</s> (alarm) is a flurry of fear from some [perceived cause], in the presence of the beloved.

children.text: vihāre saha kāntena krīḍitaṃ kelir ucyate // VisSd_3.110 //
children.translated_text: Play together with the beloved in amorous sport is called <s>keli</s> (sport). ||3.110||

children.text: dṛṣṭvā darśayati vrīḍāṃ saṃmukhaṃ naiva paśyati /
children.translated_text: Seeing [the beloved], she shows bashfulness; she does not look at him directly.

children.text: pracchannaṃ vā bhramantaṃ vā-(a)tikrāntaṃ paśyati priyam // VisSd_3.111 //
children.translated_text: She looks at her beloved either secretly, or when he passes by. ||3.111||
Even when questioned many times, slowly, with face downcast,

children.text: sagadgada-svaraṃ kiñcit priyaṃ prāyeṇa bhāṣate // VisSd_3.112 //
children.translated_text: with a slightly faltering voice, she generally speaks [only] pleasant words. ||3.112||

children.text: anyaiḥ pravartitāṃ śaśvat sāvadhānā ca tat-kathām /
children.translated_text: She listens with great attention to talk about him, always, when initiated by others,

children.text: śṛṇoty anyatra dattākṣī priye bālānurāgiṇī // VisSd_3.113 //
children.translated_text: while casting her eyes elsewhere — the girl who is newly in love. ||3.113||

children.text: cirāya savidhe sthānaṃ priyasya bahu manyate /
children.translated_text: She greatly values standing near the beloved for a long time.

children.text: vilocana-pathaṃ cāsya na gacchaty analaṅkṛtā // VisSd_3.114 //
children.translated_text: And she does not come into his line of sight without being adorned. ||3.114||
Somewhere, on the pretext of arranging and tying up her tresses,

children.text: bāhu-mūlaṃ stanau nābhi-paṅkajaṃ darśayet sphuṭam // VisSd_3.115 //
children.translated_text: she clearly reveals the armpits, breasts, and the lotus of her navel. ||3.115||
She conceals [her feelings] through words and the like before the beloved's attendants.

children.text: viśvasity asya mitreṣu bahu-mānaṃ karoti ca // VisSd_3.116 //
children.translated_text: She trusts his friends and shows them great respect. ||3.116||

children.text: sakhī-madhye guṇān brūte sva-dhanaṃ pradadāti ca /
children.translated_text: Among her companions, she speaks of his virtues and gives him her own wealth.

children.text: supte svapiti duḥkhe 'sya duḥkhaṃ dhatte sukhe sukham // VisSd_3.117 //
children.translated_text: When he sleeps, she sleeps; in his sorrow she grieves; in his happiness, she is happy. ||3.117||
Standing always in his line of sight, when the beloved looks from afar,
she addresses [his] retinue directly, revealing amorous agitation. ||3.118||

children.text: yat kiñcid api saṃvīkṣya kurute hasitaṃ mudhā /
children.translated_text: Seeing anything at all, she laughs without cause.
likewise scratching the ear, and loosening and binding the braid of hair.

children.text: jṛmbhate sphoṭayaty aṅgaṃ bālam āśliṣya cumbati /
children.translated_text: She yawns, stretches her limbs, embraces and kisses a child,

children.text: bhāle tathā vayasyāyā racayet tilaka-kriyām // VisSd_3.120 //
children.translated_text: and draws a <s>tilaka</s> mark on the forehead of her friend.
She draws on the ground with the tip of her thumb, looks with sidelong glances,

children.text: daśati svādharaṃ cāpi brūte priyam adhomukhī // VisSd_3.121 //
children.translated_text: bites her own lower lip, and speaks sweet words with her face turned down.

children.text: na muñcati ca taṃ deśaṃ nāyako yatra dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: She does not leave the place where the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) is seen,

children.text: āgacchati gṛhaṃ tasya kārya-vyājena kenacit // VisSd_3.122 //
children.translated_text: and she goes to his house on the pretext of some errand.

children.text: dattaṃ kim api kāntena dhṛtvāṅge muhur īkṣate /
children.translated_text: She repeatedly gazes at whatever her beloved has given her, holding it on her body;

children.text: nityaṃ hṛṣyati tad-yoge viyoge malinā kṛśā // VisSd_3.123 //
children.translated_text: she is always joyful in his company, and pale and emaciated in separation.

children.text: manyate bahu tac-chīlaṃ tat-priyaṃ manyate priyam /
children.translated_text: She greatly values his character; she considers what is dear to him as dear;

children.text: prārthayaty alpa-mūlyāni suptā na parivartate // VisSd_3.124 //
children.translated_text: she requests things of small value; and when asleep, she does not toss and turn.
When face to face, she does not exhibit <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary) changes;

children.text: bhāṣate sūnṛtaṃ snigdhām anuraktā nitambinī // VisSd_3.125 //
children.translated_text: she speaks truthfully and gently — [such is] the woman attached [to her beloved], the full-hipped one.
Among these, a newly-wed woman (<s>nava-strī</s>) performs actions with excessive modesty;
a middling woman with moderate bashfulness; and one whose shyness is slipping away
is another's woman. The bold (<s>pragalbhā</s>) woman's behavior is like that of a courtesan (<s>vāra-yoṣit</s>).
Through the sending of affectionate letters, through glances, through soft speech,
and through the dispatching of a female messenger (<s>dūtī</s>) — the expression of a woman's feelings (<s>bhāvas</s>) is desired.

children.text: dūtyaḥ sakhī naṭī dāsī dhātreyī prativeśinī // VisSd_3.128 //
children.translated_text: The messengers (<s>dūtīs</s>) are: a female friend (<s>sakhī</s>), an actress (<s>naṭī</s>), a maid-servant (<s>dāsī</s>), a foster-sister (<s>dhātreyī</s>), a neighbor (<s>prativeśinī</s>),

children.text: bālā pravrajitā kārūḥ śilpinyādyāḥ svayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: a young girl (<s>bālā</s>), a female ascetic (<s>pravrajitā</s>), a craftswoman (<s>kārū</s>), an artisan (<s>śilpinī</s>), and the like; or she herself.

children.text: kalā-kauśalam utsāho bhaktiś cittajñatā smṛtiḥ // VisSd_3.129 //
children.translated_text: Skill in the arts (<s>kalā-kauśala</s>), enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>), devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), knowledge of the mind (<s>cittajñatā</s>), good memory (<s>smṛti</s>),
sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), knowledge of humor (<s>narma-vijñāna</s>), and eloquence (<s>vāgmitā</s>) — these are her qualities.
These too, according to propriety, are classified as excellent, inferior, and middling.
The <s>dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast and haughty), the sinful, the debauched — [such is] the antagonist (<s>pratināyaka</s>).

children.text: uddīpana-vibhāvās te rasam uddīpayanti ye // VisSd_3.131 //
children.translated_text: The <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> (excitant determinants) are those that kindle the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment):
the gestures and the like of the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant), as well as place, time, and so forth.

children.text: udbuddhaṃ kāraṇaiḥ svaiḥ svari bahir bhāvaṃ prakāśayan // VisSd_3.132 //
children.translated_text: That which, being aroused by its own particular causes, manifests the inner emotional state (<s>bhāva</s>) externally —
that which in life takes the form of an effect — is called <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) in poetry and drama.

children.text: uktāḥ strīṇām alaṅkārā aṅgajāś ca svabhāvajāḥ // VisSd_3.133 //
children.translated_text: The ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) of women, both those born of the body and those born of nature, have been described.

children.text: tad-rūpāḥ sāttvikā bhāvās tathā ceṣṭāḥ parā api /
children.translated_text: Of that nature are the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary physical responses), and also the other gestures.
The changes born of <s>sattva</s> (the deepest emotional state) are called <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary).
Because they arise from <s>sattva</s> alone, they are distinct from [ordinary] <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents).

children.text: stambhaḥ svedo 'tha romāñcaḥ svara-bhaṅgo 'tha vepathuḥ // VisSd_3.135 //
children.translated_text: <s>Stambha</s> (paralysis), <s>sveda</s> (perspiration), <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation), <s>svara-bhaṅga</s> (voice-breaking), <s>vepathu</s> (trembling),

children.text: vaivarṇyam aśru-pralaya ity aṣṭau sāttvikāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>vaivarṇya</s> (change of color), <s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>pralaya</s> (fainting) — these eight are known as the <s>sāttvika</s> [bhāvas].
<s>Stambha</s> (paralysis) is the obstruction of [all] action, caused by fear, joy, illness, and the like.
<s>Sveda</s> (perspiration) is the emergence of moisture on the body, caused by passion, heat, exertion, and the like.
<s>Romāñca</s> (horripilation) is the bristling of body-hair, arising from joy, wonder, fear, and the like.
Stammering, i.e., <s>gadgada</s> (choked voice), caused by intoxication, delight, pain, and the like, is known as <s>vaisvaryam</s> (change of voice).
<s>Vepathu</s> (trembling) is the shaking of the body, caused by passion, hatred, exertion, and the like.
<s>Vaivarṇatā</s> (pallor/change of color) is the alteration of complexion, caused by despondency, intoxication, anger, and the like.
<s>Aśru</s> (tears) is the water arising from the eyes, born of anger, grief, and great joy.
<s>Pralaya</s> (fainting) is the cessation of action and consciousness, caused by [extreme] happiness or sorrow.
The <s>vyabhicāriṇaḥ</s> (transitory emotions), especially by their prominence,

children.text: sthāyiny unmagna-nirmagnās trayastriṃśac ca tad-bhidāḥ // VisSd_3.140 //
children.translated_text: surfacing and submerging in the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent sentiment) — their varieties are thirty-three.

children.text: nirvedāvega-dainya-śrama-mada-jaḍatā augrya-mohau vibodhaḥ svapnāpasmāra-garvā maraṇam alasatāmarṣa-nidrāvahitthāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>svapna</s> (dream), <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>maraṇa</s> (death), <s>alasatā</s> (sloth), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation),

children.text: autsukyonmāda-śaṅkāḥ smṛti-mati-sahitā vyādhi-satrāsa-lajjā harṣāsūyā-viṣādāḥ sadhṛti-capalatā glāni-cintā-vitarkāḥ // VisSd_3.141 //
children.translated_text: <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness), <s>unmāda</s> (madness), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>mati</s> (discernment), together with <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), <s>trāsa</s> (fright), <s>lajjā</s> (shame), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), together with <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), and <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture).
<s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation) is self-abasement arising from knowledge of truth, calamity, jealousy, and the like;
it produces wretchedness, anxiety, tears, sighs, pallor, heavy breathing, and the like.
<s>Āvega</s> (agitation) is perturbation. When caused by rain, it produces contraction of the body;
when caused by a portent, the limbs become slack; when caused by fire, smoke and the like cause disturbance.
When caused by the flight of a king and the like, there is the taking up of weapons, elephants, and the like;
when caused by an elephant and the like, there is paralysis, trembling, and the like; when caused by wind, there is disturbance from dust and the like.

children.text: iṣṭād dharṣāḥ śuco 'niṣṭāj jñeyāś cānye yathāyatham /
children.translated_text: From the desired [object] comes joy; from the undesired, grief — and the rest should be understood accordingly.
<s>Dainya</s> (wretchedness) is loss of energy arising from poverty and the like; it produces dirtiness and the like.
<s>Śrama</s> (fatigue) is weariness from lovemaking, journeying, walking, and the like; it produces heavy breathing, drowsiness, and the like.
<s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is born of the use of wine; it is a mixture of bewilderment and bliss.

children.text: amunā cottamaḥ śete madhyo hasati gāyati /
children.translated_text: Under its influence, a person of superior nature sleeps; a middling one laughs and sings;

children.text: adhama-prakṛtiś cāpi paruṣaṃ vakti roditi // VisSd_3.147 //
children.translated_text: and one of inferior nature speaks harshly and weeps.
<s>Jaḍatā</s> (stupor) is the absence of response, arising from the sight or hearing of the desired or undesired;
its [signs include] unblinking gazing, silence, and the like.
<s>Ugratā</s> (ferocity) arises from valor, offense, and the like;
its [signs include] perspiration, head-shaking, threatening, striking, and the like.
<s>Moha</s> (delusion) is mental confusion arising from fear, grief, agitation, and brooding;
it produces fainting, loss of consciousness, falling, roaming, and inability to see, and the like.
<s>Vibodha</s> (awakening) is the return of consciousness from the causes that dispel sleep;
it produces yawning, stretching of the limbs, closing and opening of the eyes, and surveying the body.

children.text: svapno nidrām upetasya viṣayānubhavas tu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Svapna</s> (dream) is the experience of sense-objects by one who has fallen asleep;
it causes anger, agitation, fear, languor, happiness, sorrow, and the like.
<s>Apasmāra</s> (epilepsy) is a derangement of the mind, born of possession by spirits and the like;
it causes falling on the ground, trembling, perspiration, foam, drooling, and the like.
<s>Garva</s> (pride) is intoxication born of power, beauty, learning, noble birth, and the like;
it causes contempt, displaying of limbs with grace, discourtesy, and the like.
<s>Maraṇa</s> (death) is the giving up of life, caused by arrows and the like; it produces falling of the body and the like.
<s>Ālasya</s> (sloth) is inertia born of fatigue, pregnancy, and the like; it produces yawning, listlessness, and the like.
<s>Amarṣa</s> (indignation) is intense preoccupation arising from reproach, abuse, dishonor, and the like;
it produces reddening of the eyes, head-shaking, frowning, menacing, and the like.
<s>Nidrā</s> (sleep) is the closing of the mind, born of fatigue, weariness, intoxication, and the like;
it causes yawning, closing of the eyes, heavy breathing, slackening of the body, and the like.
<s>Avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) is the concealment of the outward expression of joy and the like, arising from fear, respect, shame, and the like;
it causes engagement in other activities, speaking of other things, and looking elsewhere.
<s>Autsukya</s> (eagerness) is the impatience with the passage of time, arising from the non-attainment of what is desired;
it produces mental anguish, haste, perspiration, long sighs, and the like.
<s>Unmāda</s> (madness) is the confusion of the mind, arising from love, grief, fear, and the like;
it produces inappropriate laughter, weeping, singing, rambling speech, and the like.
<s>Śaṅkā</s> (apprehension) is the imagining of misfortune, arising from another's cruelty, one's own faults, and the like;
it produces pallor, trembling, change of voice, looking sideways, and dryness of the mouth.
<s>Smṛti</s> (recollection) is called the knowledge regarding previously experienced objects,
arising from similar cognition, thought, and the like; it produces the raising of the eyebrows and the like.
<s>Mati</s> (discernment) is the determination of meaning by following the path of reasoning and the like;

children.text: smeratā dhṛti-satoṣau bahu-mānaś ca tad-bhavāḥ // VisSd_3.163 //
children.translated_text: its expressions include a calm smile (<s>smeratā</s>), contentment (<s>dhṛti</s>), satisfaction (<s>santoṣa</s>), and high regard (<s>bahumāna</s>).
<s>Vyādhi</s> (sickness) is fever and the like, caused by <s>vāta</s> (wind) and the like; it produces [desire for] lying on the ground, writhing, and the like.
<s>Trāsa</s> (fright) is caused by thunder, lightning, meteors, and the like; it produces trembling and the like.
<s>Lajjā</s> (shame) is the absence of boldness (<s>dhārṣṭya</s>), arising from misconduct; it produces the lowering of the face and the like.
<s>Harṣa</s> (joy) is the cheerfulness of the mind, arising from the attainment of what is desired; it produces tears, choked voice, and the like.
<s>Asūyā</s> (envy) is the intolerance of others' prosperity, arising from arrogance;
it produces the proclamation of faults, frowning, contempt, anger, gesturing, and the like.
<s>Viṣāda</s> (despondency) is the diminution of one's spirit, born of the absence of means;
it produces sighs, heavy breathing, burning of the heart, and searching for help, and the like.
<s>Dhṛti</s> (steadfastness) is the state of being completely fulfilled in desire, arising from knowledge, the arrival of what is wished for, and the like;
it produces feelings of well-being, joyful speech, laughter, and quick-wittedness, and the like.
<s>Capalatā</s> (fickleness) is instability, arising from jealousy, hatred, passion, and the like;
its [signs include] reproach, harshness, and willful conduct, and the like.
<s>Glāni</s> (languor) arises from lovemaking, exertion, mental anguish, hunger, thirst, and the like;
it produces lifelessness, trembling, emaciation, and lack of enthusiasm, and the like.
<s>Cintā</s> (anxiety) is brooding, arising from the non-attainment of what is beneficial; it produces a vacant look, sighing, and burning.
<s>Vitarka</s> (conjecture) is deliberation, arising from doubt; it makes the eyebrows, head, and fingers dance.
<s>Rati</s> (love) and the like, when not fixed to a particular <s>rasa</s>, become <s>vyabhicāriṇaḥ</s> (transitory emotions).

children.text: śṛṅgāra-vīrayor hāso vīre krodhas tathā mataḥ // VisSd_3.172 //
children.translated_text: In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), laughter [appears]; in <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), anger (<s>krodha</s>) is likewise held.
In <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil), disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>) has been spoken of as a transitory emotion.

children.text: ity ādy-anyat samunnateyaṃ tathā bhāvita-buddhibhiḥ // VisSd_3.173 //
children.translated_text: Thus, other [combinations] of this kind should be worked out by those of cultivated understanding.

children.text: aviruddhā viruddhā vā yaṃ tirodhātum akṣamāḥ /
children.translated_text: That which — whether unopposed or opposed [transitory emotions] — are unable to obscure;
that which is the root-bulb (<s>kanda</s>) from which the sprout of relish (<s>āsvāda</s>) grows — that emotional state (<s>bhāva</s>) is accepted as the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent sentiment).

children.text: ratir hāsaś ca śokaś ca krodhotsāhau bhayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (mirth), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),

children.text: jugupsā vismayaś cettham aṣṭau proktāḥ śamo 'pi ca // VisSd_3.175 //
children.translated_text: <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) — thus eight are declared; and also <s>śama</s> (tranquility) [as the ninth].
<s>Rati</s> (love) is the inclination of the mind toward an object congenial to it.
<s>Hāsa</s> (mirth) is the expansion of the mind, manifested through changes of speech and the like.
<s>Śoka</s> (sorrow) is the perturbation of the mind, arising from the loss of what is desired and the like; it bears the name 'grief.'
<s>Krodha</s> (anger) is the apprehension of fierceness toward hostile things.
The steadfast enthusiasm in undertaking tasks is called <s>utsāha</s> (energy).

children.text: raudra-śaktyā tu janitaṃ citta-vaiklavyaṃ bhayam // VisSd_3.178 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaya</s> (fear) is the perturbation of the mind produced by a terrifying power.
<s>Jugupsā</s> (disgust) is censure arising from the perception of faults and the like; it gives rise to <s>vismaya</s> (wonder).
In various objects that transgress the limits of the ordinary world,

children.text: visphāraś cetaso yas tu sa vismaya udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: the expansion of the mind that occurs — that is called <s>vismaya</s> (wonder).
<s>Śama</s> (tranquility) is the happiness born of repose in one's own self, in a state of desirelessness.
Because they bring about (<s>bhāvayanti</s>) the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) through their connection with various modes of dramatic representation (<s>abhinaya</s>),

children.text: tasmād bhāvā amī proktāḥ sthāyi-sañcāri-sāttvikāḥ // VisSd_3.181 //
children.translated_text: therefore these — the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent), <s>sañcārin</s> (transitory), and <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary) — are called <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states).
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (the furious), <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible),

children.text: bībhatso 'dbhuta ity aṣṭau rasāḥ śāntas tathā mataḥ // VisSd_3.182 //
children.translated_text: <s>bībhatsa</s> (the odious), and <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous) — thus eight are the <s>rasas</s>; and <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil) is likewise accepted [as the ninth].
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment): '<s>Śṛṅga</s>' indeed is the sprouting of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love); that which causes its arising —
the <s>rasa</s> that is predominantly of a superior nature is accepted as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic).
Here, excluding the woman married to another and the courtesan who is not in love,

children.text: ālambanaṃ nāyikāḥ syur dakṣiṇādyāś ca nāyakam // VisSd_3.184 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nāyikās</s> (heroines) serve as the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant), and the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> and other types of heroes as the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero).
The moon, sandalwood, the humming of bees, and the like are considered the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant determinants).
The casting of the eyebrow, the sidelong glance, and the like are declared as the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents).
Excluding the transitory emotions of ferocity (<s>ugratā</s>), death (<s>maraṇa</s>), sloth (<s>ālasya</s>), and disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>) —
the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent sentiment) is <s>rati</s> (love); its color is dark (<s>śyāma</s>), and its presiding deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: vipralambho 'tha saṃbhoga ity eṣa dvividho mataḥ // VisSd_3.186 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vipralambha</s> (love in separation) and <s>saṃbhoga</s> (love in union) — thus this [śṛṅgāra] is held to be of two kinds.

children.text: yatra tu ratiḥ prakṛṣṭā nābhīṣṭam upaitai vipralambho 'sau /
children.translated_text: Where <s>rati</s> (love) is intense but the desired [union] is not attained — that is <s>vipralambha</s> (separation);

children.text: sa ca pūrva-rāga-māna-pravāsa-karuṇātmakaś caturdhā syāt // VisSd_3.187 //
children.translated_text: and it is of four kinds: <s>pūrvarāga</s> (prior love), <s>māna</s> (love-anger), <s>pravāsa</s> (love in absence), and <s>karuṇā</s> (love in compassion).
The special state that arises from hearing or seeing, between two whose passion has mutually grown,

children.text: daśā-viśeṣo yo 'prāptau pūrvarāgaḥ sa ucyate // VisSd_3.188 //
children.translated_text: when [union] has not yet been attained — that is called <s>pūrvarāga</s> (prior love/love before meeting).
Hearing about [the beloved] occurs there through the mouth of a messenger, a bard, or a female companion.

children.text: indrajāle ca citre ca sākṣāt svapne ca darśanam // VisSd_3.189 //
children.translated_text: And seeing [the beloved] occurs through magic, a painting, directly, or in a dream. // 3.189 //
Desire, anxiety, recollection, enumeration of qualities, agitation, delirium,

children.text: unmādo 'tha vyādhir jaḍatā mṛtir iti daśātra kāma-daśāḥ // VisSd_3.190 //
children.translated_text: madness, then illness, stupor, and death -- these are the ten stages of love (<s>kāma-daśā</s>) here. // 3.190 //
<s>Abhilāṣa</s> (desire) is longing; <s>cintā</s> (anxiety) is deliberation on the means of attainment and so forth.
<s>Unmāda</s> (madness) is the inability to distinguish between sentient and insentient things. // 3.191 //
Delirium (<s>pralāpa</s>) is incoherent speech arising from the intense wandering of the mind.
Illness (<s>vyādhi</s>) consists of long sighs, pallor, emaciation, and the like. // 3.192 //
Stupor (<s>jaḍatā</s>) is the diminished activity of the limbs and also of the mind.
Death (<s>maraṇa</s>) is never to be depicted, since it would cause a break in <s>rasa</s>. // 3.193 //

children.text: jāta-prāyaṃ tu tad vācyaṃ cetasākāṅkṣitaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: However, death that has nearly occurred may be described, as well as that which is wished for in the mind,

children.text: varṇyate 'pi yadi pratyuj-jīvanaṃ syād adūrataḥ // VisSd_3.194 //
children.translated_text: and even if depicted, revival should follow shortly after. // 3.194 //

children.text: ādau vācyaḥ striyā rāgaḥ puṃsaḥ paścāt tad-iṅgitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: First the woman's passion should be expressed, then the man's through her gestures. Prior love (<s>pūrva-rāga</s>) is also of three kinds: <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower), and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder).

children.text: nīlī kusumbhaṃ mañjiṣṭhā pūrvarāgo 'pi ca tridhā // VisSd_3.195 //
na cātiśobhate yan nāpaiti prema manogatam /
children.translated_text: That love which neither shines brilliantly nor departs from the mind

children.text: tan nīlī-rāgam ākhyātaṃ yathā śrī-rāma-sītayoḥ // VisSd_3.196 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>nīlī-rāga</s> (indigo-love), as in the case of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> and <s>Sītā</s>. // 3.196 //

children.text: kusumbha-rāgaṃ tat prāhur yad apaiti ca śobhate /
children.translated_text: That which departs yet shines is called <s>kusumbha-rāga</s> (safflower-love).

children.text: mañjiṣṭhā-rāgam āhus tad yan nāpaity atiśobhate // VisSd_3.197 //
children.translated_text: That which never departs and shines brilliantly is called <s>mañjiṣṭhā-rāga</s> (madder-love). // 3.197 //

children.text: mānaḥ kopaḥ sa tu dvedhā praṇayerṣyā-samudbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> (love-anger) is indignation; it is of two kinds: arising from affection (<s>praṇaya</s>) and from jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>).

children.text: dvayoḥ praṇayamānaḥ syāt pramode sumahaty api // VisSd_3.198 //
children.translated_text: Of the two, <s>praṇaya-māna</s> (affectionate anger) occurs even in the midst of great delight, // 3.198 //

children.text: premṇaḥ kuṭila-gāmitvāt kopo yaḥ kāraṇaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: being anger without cause, arising from the crooked course of love.
When the husband's association with another beloved is seen, inferred, or heard about, // 3.199 //

children.text: īrṣyāmāno bhavet strīṇāṃ tatratv anumitis tridhā /
children.translated_text: <s>īrṣyā-māna</s> (jealous anger) arises in women. The inference therein is of three kinds,
arising from talking in sleep, marks of enjoyment on the body, or slips of the tongue with another's name. // 3.200 //

children.text: sāma bhedo 'tha dānaṃ ca naty-upekṣe rasāntaram /
children.translated_text: Conciliation (<s>sāma</s>), dissension (<s>bheda</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), supplication (<s>nati</s>), disregard (<s>upekṣā</s>), and diversion to another sentiment (<s>rasāntara</s>) --

children.text: tad-bhaṅgāya patiḥ kuryāt ṣaḍ-upāyān iti kramāt // VisSd_3.201 //
children.translated_text: the husband should employ these six strategies in order to break her anger. // 3.201 //
Of these, <s>sāma</s> is affectionate speech; <s>bheda</s> is winning over her female companion.

children.text: dānaṃ vyājena bhūṣādeḥ pādayoḥ patanaṃ natiḥ // VisSd_3.202 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dāna</s> is giving ornaments and such under some pretext; <s>nati</s> is falling at her feet. // 3.202 //
When conciliation and the rest are exhausted, there should be <s>upekṣā</s> (disregard), which is indifference.
<s>Rasāntara</s> (diversion to another sentiment) is the breaking of anger through vehemence, fear, joy, and the like. // 3.203 //

children.text: pravāso bhinna-deśitvaṃ kāryāc chāpāc ca saṃbhramāt /
children.translated_text: Separation (<s>pravāsa</s>) is being in a different place, occurring due to duty, a curse, or an emergency.
In that state, there arise soiling of the body and garments, the head bearing a single braid, // 3.204 //
sighing, heavy breathing, weeping, falling on the ground, and so forth.

children.text: aṅgeṣv asauṣṭhavaṃ tāpaḥ pāṇḍutā kṛśatāruciḥ // VisSd_3.205 //
children.translated_text: The limbs lose their grace, there is burning, pallor, emaciation, and loss of appetite. // 3.205 //
There is loss of composure, absence of support, absorption in the beloved, madness, fainting,

children.text: mṛtiś ceti kramāj jñeyā daśa smara-daśā iha // VisSd_3.206 //
children.translated_text: and death -- these should be known as the ten stages of love-in-separation (<s>smara-daśā</s>) in sequence. // 3.206 //
Loss of grace (<s>asauṣṭhava</s>) is the onset of uncleanliness; burning (<s>tāpa</s>) is the fever of separation.
Loss of appetite (<s>aruci</s>) is disenchantment with all things; indifference to everything is <s>dhṛti</s> (composure). // 3.207 //
Absence of support (<s>anālambana</s>) is remembered as the emptiness of the mind.
Absorption in the beloved (<s>tan-maya</s>) is the manifestation of the beloved both externally and internally.

children.text: bhāvī bhavan bhūta iti tridhā syāt tatra kāryajaḥ // VisSd_3.208 //
children.translated_text: It is of three kinds based on the effect: relating to the future, the present, or the past. // 3.208 //

children.text: yūnor ekatarasmin gatavati lokāntaraṃ punar alabhye /
children.translated_text: When one of the two lovers has departed to another world and cannot be recovered,

children.text: vimanāyate yadaikas tato bhavet karuṇa-vipralambhākhyaḥ // VisSd_3.209 //
children.translated_text: and the other becomes sorrowful, then it is called <s>karuṇa-vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation of the pathetic type). // 3.209 //
Where two lovers, mutually attached, engage in gazing, touching, and the like,
that is declared to be <s>saṃbhoga</s> (love-in-union). // 3.210 //
Because of the innumerable varieties of kissing, embracing, and the like,

children.text: ayam eka eva dhīraiḥ kathitaḥ saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāraḥ // VisSd_3.211 //
children.translated_text: the learned have declared <s>saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment in union) to be of one kind only. // 3.211 //
In that context, the six seasons, the moon and the sun, rising and setting,
water-sports, forest excursions, dawn, drinking of wine, the night, and similar [settings are employed]. // 3.212 //

children.text: anulepana-bhūṣāḍyā vācyaṃ śuci medhyam anyac ca /
children.translated_text: Unguents, ornaments, and other [accessories] are to be described; everything should be pure and auspicious.

children.text: kathitaś caturvidho 'sāv ānantaryāt tu pūrva-rāgādeḥ // VisSd_3.213 //
children.translated_text: This [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] has been described as fourfold, following in sequence from <s>pūrva-rāga</s> (prior love) and the rest. // 3.213 //
From distorted appearance, speech, dress, gestures, and the like, the comic (<s>hāsya</s>) arises from absurdity (<s>kuhuka</s>).
<s>Hāsa</s> (laughter) is the <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s> (permanent emotion); its colour is white; its presiding deity is <s>Pramatha</s> (Śiva). // 3.214 //
One whose distorted appearance, speech, and gestures cause people to laugh

children.text: tam atrālambanaṃ prāhus tac-ceṣṭoddīpanaṃ matam // VisSd_3.215 //
children.translated_text: is called the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant object) here; such gestures are considered the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.215 //
The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) are contraction of the eyes, smiling of the face, and the like.
Drowsiness, laziness, dissimulation (<s>avahitthā</s>), and such are the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) here. // 3.216 //
For superior persons, there are <s>smita</s> (gentle smile) and <s>hasita</s> (smile); for middling persons, <s>vihasita</s> (laughter) and <s>avahasita</s> (ridiculing laughter);

children.text: nīcānām apahasitaṃ tathātihasitaṃ tad eṣa ṣaḍ-bhedaḥ // VisSd_3.217 //
children.translated_text: for the lowly, <s>apahasita</s> (derisive laughter) and <s>atihasita</s> (excessive laughter) -- thus it is of six varieties. // 3.217 //
<s>Smita</s> (gentle smile) has slightly blooming eyes and quivering lips.

children.text: kiñcil lakṣa-dvijaṃ tatra hasitaṃ kathitaṃ budhaiḥ // VisSd_3.218 //
children.translated_text: Where the teeth are slightly visible, that is called <s>hasita</s> (smile) by the learned. // 3.218 //
<s>Vihasita</s> (laughter) has a sweet sound; <s>avahasita</s> (ridiculing laughter) is accompanied by shaking of the shoulders and head.

children.text: apahasitaṃ sāsrākṣaṃ vikṣiptāṅgaṃ ca bhavaty atihasitam // VisSd_3.219 //
children.translated_text: <s>Apahasita</s> (derisive laughter) has tearful eyes; <s>atihasita</s> (excessive laughter) involves contortion of the limbs. // 3.219 //

children.text: yasya hāsaḥ sa cet kvāpi sākṣān naiva nibadhyate /
children.translated_text: Even if the one whose laughter it is does not appear directly anywhere [in the work],
nevertheless this [<s>rasa</s>] is apprehended through the power of the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the rest. // 3.220 //
Through non-difference, owing to the universality of the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest, it is experienced
by the spectators (<s>sāmājikas</s>) -- thus this <s>hāsya-rasa</s> (comic sentiment) is relished. // 3.221 //
From the loss of what is desired or the attainment of what is undesired, there arises the <s>rasa</s> called <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic).
The learned have declared its colour to be pigeon-grey (<s>kapota-varṇa</s>), and its presiding deity is <s>Yama</s>. // 3.222 //

children.text: śoko 'tra sthāyi-bhāvaḥ syāc chocyam ālambanaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śoka</s> (grief) is the <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s> (permanent emotion) here; the object of grief is considered the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant).

children.text: tasya dāhādikāvasthā bhaved uddīpanaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_3.223 //
children.translated_text: The burning and similar conditions of that [grief] constitute the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.223 //
The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) are blaming fate, falling on the ground, wailing, and the like,
as well as change of colour, heavy breathing, sighing, paralysis, and incoherent speech. // 3.224 //
<s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>apasmāra</s> (loss of memory), illness, languor, recollection, fatigue,
despondency, stupor, madness, anxiety, and others are the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions). // 3.225 //
This <s>rasa</s> differs from <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) in that <s>śoka</s> (grief) is the <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>.
In <s>vipralambha</s>, <s>rati</s> (love) is the <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>, directed toward reunion. // 3.226 //
<s>Raudra</s> (the furious) has <s>krodha</s> (anger) as its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>; its colour is red; its presiding deity is <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: ālambanam aris tasya tac ceṣṭoddīpanaṃ matam // VisSd_3.227 //
children.translated_text: The <s>ālambana</s> (determinant) is the enemy; the enemy's actions are considered the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.227 //
Through blows with the fist, striking down, mutilation, cutting, and tearing apart,
and through the tumult of battle and the like, its full arousal (<s>uddīpti</s>) occurs. // 3.228 //
The knitting of the brows, biting of the lips, clapping of the arms, and threatening gestures,
narrating one's own heroic deeds, and brandishing weapons -- // 3.229 //
these are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions), along with reproach, fierce glaring, and the like.
Ferocity, impetuosity, horripilation, perspiration, trembling, and intoxication, // 3.230 //
<s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), and others are the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) here.
Redness of the face and eyes distinguishes this [<s>raudra</s>] from heroism in battle (<s>yuddha-vīra</s>). // 3.231 //
The heroic (<s>vīra</s>) has a person of noble nature as its subject; <s>utsāha</s> (energy) is its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s> (permanent emotion).
Its presiding deity is <s>Mahendra</s> (Indra); its colour has been declared to be golden. // 3.232 //
The <s>ālambana-vibhāvas</s> (determinant causes) are considered to be those who are to be conquered and the like.
The actions of those to be conquered and such constitute the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitants).

children.text: anubhāvās tu tatra syuḥ sahāyānveṣaṇādayaḥ // VisSd_3.233 //
children.translated_text: The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) here are seeking allies and the like. // 3.233 //
The <s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) are fortitude, discernment, pride, recollection, reasoning, and horripilation.

children.text: sa ca dāna-dharma-yuddhair dayayā ca samanvitaś caturdhā syāt // VisSd_3.234 //
children.translated_text: And it is fourfold: through generosity (<s>dāna</s>), righteousness (<s>dharma</s>), battle (<s>yuddha</s>), and compassion (<s>dayā</s>). // 3.234 //
The terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>) has <s>bhaya</s> (fear) as its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>; its presiding deity is <s>Bhūta</s> (ghosts).
Its nature belongs to women and the lowly; its colour is black, as determined by those versed in the principles. // 3.235 //

children.text: yasmād utpadyate bhītis tad atrālambanaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: That from which terror arises is considered the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant) here.

children.text: ceṣṭā ghoratarās tasya bhaved uddīpanaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_3.236 //
children.translated_text: Its most terrible actions constitute the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.236 //
The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) here are change of colour, speaking in a choked voice,
fainting, perspiration, horripilation, trembling, looking in all directions, and the like. // 3.237 //
Disgust, agitation, bewilderment, terror, languor, wretchedness,
apprehension, loss of memory, confusion, death, and others are the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions). // 3.238 //
The <s>rasa</s> whose <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s> is <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust) is called <s>bībhatsa</s> (the odious).
Its colour is blue; its presiding deity is declared to be <s>Mahākāla</s>. // 3.239 //
Foul smells, flesh, blood, and fat are considered the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant).
The falling of worms and such upon them is cited as the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.240 //
Spitting, turning away of the face, contraction of the eyes, and the like

children.text: anubhāvās tatra matās tathā syur vyabhicāriṇaḥ // VisSd_3.241 //
children.translated_text: are considered the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) here; and the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) are: // 3.241 //
<s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>apasmāra</s> (loss of memory), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), illness, death, and others.
The marvellous (<s>adbhuta</s>) has <s>vismaya</s> (astonishment) as its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>; its presiding deity is <s>Gandharva</s>. // 3.242 //
Its colour is yellow; an object transcending the world is considered its <s>ālambana</s> (determinant).

children.text: guṇānāṃ tasya mahimā bhaved uddīpanaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_3.243 //
children.translated_text: The greatness of its qualities constitutes the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // 3.243 //
Paralysis, perspiration, horripilation, choking of the voice, and agitation,
as well as widening of the eyes and the like, are declared to be the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions). // 3.244 //
Conjecture, impetuosity, confusion, joy, and others are the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions).
The tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) has <s>śama</s> (tranquility) as its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s>; its subject is a person of noble nature. // 3.245 //
Its lustre is beautiful like jasmine and the moon; its presiding deity is <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>.
The essential worthlessness of all things, apprehended through impermanence and similar [insights], // 3.246 //
or the true nature of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) -- that is accepted as its <s>ālambana</s> (determinant).
Sacred hermitages, places of <s>Hari</s>, <s>tīrthas</s> (pilgrimage sites), delightful forests, and the like, // 3.247 //
and association with great souls and such, constitute its <s>uddīpana</s> (excitants).

children.text: romāñcādyāś cānubhāvās tathā syur vyabhicāriṇaḥ // VisSd_3.248 //
children.translated_text: Horripilation and the like are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions); and the <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) are: // 3.248 //
self-deprecation, joy, remembrance, transcendent compassion, and others.
Because of its nature being free from ego, this [<s>śānta</s>] is not [a sub-type of] compassionate heroism (<s>dayā-vīra</s>) and the like. // 3.249 //

children.text: yukta-viyukta-daśāyām avasthito yaḥ śamaḥ sa eva yataḥ /
