children.translated_text: Since the <s>śama</s> (tranquility) that exists in the state of union and separation is itself

children.text: rasatām eti tad asmin sañcāryādeḥ sthitiś ca na viśuddhā // VisSd_3.250 //
children.translated_text: what attains the status of <s>rasa</s>, the presence of <s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s> and the rest therein is not unmixed. // 3.250 //

children.text: sphuṭaṃ camatkāritayā vatsalaṃ ca rasaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: The learned also clearly recognize <s>vatsala</s> (the tender) as a <s>rasa</s>, on account of its capacity to produce <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder).

children.text: sthāyī vatsalatā snehaḥ putrādy-ālambanaṃ matam // VisSd_3.251 //
children.translated_text: Its <s>sthāyi-bhāva</s> is <s>vatsalatā</s> (tenderness), which is affection; the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant) is considered to be one's son and the like. // 3.251 //
The <s>uddīpanas</s> (excitants) are the child's actions, learning, valour, compassion, and the like.
Embracing, touching the body, kissing the head, and gazing [at the child] -- // 3.252 //
horripilation, tears of joy, and the like are declared to be the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions).
The <s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) are considered to be apprehension of misfortune, joy, pride, and others. // 3.253 //
Its colour is that of the inside of a lotus; its presiding deities are the Mothers of the World (<s>loka-mātaraḥ</s>).
The first [<s>śṛṅgāra</s>] stands in opposition to <s>karuṇa</s>, <s>bībhatsa</s>, <s>raudra</s>, <s>vīra</s>, and <s>bhayānaka</s>. // 3.254 //
<s>Hāsya</s> (the comic) is incompatible with <s>bhayānaka</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> as well.
<s>Karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) is likewise [incompatible] with <s>hāsya</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. // 3.255 //
<s>Raudra</s> (the furious) [is incompatible] with <s>hāsya</s>, <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, and <s>bhayānaka</s> as well.

children.text: bhayānakena śāntena tathā vīra-rasaḥ smṛtaḥ // VisSd_3.256 //
children.translated_text: And <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) is said [to be incompatible] with <s>bhayānaka</s> and <s>śānta</s>. // 3.256 //
<s>Bhayānaka</s> (the terrible) [is incompatible] with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>vīra</s>, <s>raudra</s>, <s>hāsya</s>, and <s>śānta</s>.
And <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil) [is incompatible] with <s>vīra</s>, <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>raudra</s>, <s>hāsya</s>, and <s>bhayānaka</s>. // 3.257 //

children.text: śṛṅgāreṇa tu bībhatsa ity ākhyātā virodhitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Bībhatsa</s> (the odious) [is incompatible] with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> -- thus the oppositions have been stated.

children.text: kuto 'pi kāraṇāt kvāpi sthiratām upayann api // VisSd_3.258 //
children.translated_text: Even though [a mental state] may attain stability due to some cause in some [literary] context,

children.text: unmādādir na tu sthāyī na pātre sthairyam eti yat /
children.translated_text: madness and the like are not <s>sthāyi-bhāvas</s> (permanent emotions), because they do not attain permanence in the [aesthetic] subject.
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state), the semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of each, the subsidence and arising of <s>bhāva</s>,

children.text: sandhiḥ śabalatā ceti sarve 'pi rasanād rasāḥ /
children.translated_text: conjunction (<s>sandhi</s>), and intermixture (<s>śabalatā</s>) — all of these are <s>rasas</s> because they are 'tasted' (<s>rasanāt</s>).
The transitory emotions (<s>sañcāriṇaḥ</s>) [are called <s>rasas</s>] by predominance; <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward gods and the like

children.text: udbuddha-mātraḥ sthāyī ca bhāva ity abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: when merely awakened, is called the <s>sthāyī</s> (permanent emotion) and <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state).
Just as in a potion (<s>prapāṇaka</s>) where pepper, sugar, and the rest are combined,

children.text: udrekaḥ kasyacit kvāpi tathā sañcāriṇo rase /
children.translated_text: one [ingredient] predominates somewhere — so too the transitory emotions in <s>rasa</s>.
When there is impropriety in [the depiction of rasa], it is the semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>.
When <s>rati</s> (love) is directed toward a subsidiary hero (<s>upanāyaka</s>), or toward the wife of a sage or guru,
or toward the hero [in inappropriate situations], or when it pertains to neither [of the two parties],
or when it pertains to the antagonist (<s>pratināyaka</s>), or when directed toward a low character, an animal, and the like —
there is impropriety in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment). In <s>raudra</s> (the furious sentiment), when anger is directed toward a guru and the like,

children.text: śānte ca hīna-niṣṭhe gurv-ādy ālambane hāsye /
children.translated_text: and in <s>śānta</s> (the peaceful sentiment) when it pertains to a low character; in <s>hāsya</s> (the comic sentiment) when the object (<s>ālambana</s>) is a guru and the like;
in <s>vīra</s> (the heroic sentiment) when directed toward a low character — [these are all semblances]; and when <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) is for brahmin-killing and the like,
in <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible sentiment) when directed toward a noble character — the same [principle] should be known elsewhere.

children.text: bhāvābhāso lajjādike tu veśyādi-viṣaye syāt // VisSd_3.266 //
children.translated_text: The semblance of <s>bhāva</s> (<s>bhāvābhāsa</s>) occurs in <s>lajjā</s> (modesty) and the like when directed toward a courtesan and similar [characters].
When a <s>bhāva</s> subsides and [another] arises, and when two are mixed — in sequence,

children.text: bhāvasya śāntir udayaḥ sandhiḥ śabalatā matā // VisSd_3.267 //
children.translated_text: the subsidence of <s>bhāva</s>, the arising [of bhāva], <s>sandhi</s> (junction), and <s>śabalatā</s> (intermixture) are recognized.

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe rasādi-nirūpaṇo nāma
tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, called 'The Examination of <s>Rasa</s> and Related Topics,' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(4) Fourth Chapter: The Determination of <s>Dhvani</s> (Suggestion).

children.text: kāvyaṃ dhvanir guṇībhūta-vyaṅgaṃ ceti dvidhā matā /
children.translated_text: Poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) is considered to be of two kinds: <s>dhvani</s> (suggestive poetry) and <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (poetry with subordinated suggestion).

children.text: vācyātiśayini vyaṅgyo dhvanis tat kāvyam uttamam // VisSd_4.1 //
children.translated_text: When the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) surpasses the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>), it is <s>dhvani</s> — that poetry is the highest.

children.text: bhedau dhvaner api dvāv udīritau lakṣaṇābhidhā-mūlau /
children.translated_text: Two varieties of <s>dhvani</s> are stated, based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) and <s>abhidhā</s> (primary signification) as their foundations:
one is <s>avivakṣita-vācya</s> (where the literal meaning is unintended), the other is <s>vivakṣitānyapara-vācya</s> (where the literal meaning is intended but another meaning is primary).
When the literal meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is transferred to another meaning, or when it is completely set aside —
<s>avivakṣita-vācya dhvani</s> too admits a twofold division.
<s>Vivakṣitābhidheya</s> (where the expressed meaning is intended) [<s>dhvani</s>] is first considered to be of two kinds:

children.text: asaṃlakṣya-kramo yatra vyaṅgyo lakṣya-kramas tathā // VisSd_4.4 //
children.translated_text: one where the process of suggestion is imperceptible (<s>asaṃlakṣya-krama</s>), and the other where it is perceptible (<s>lakṣya-krama</s>).
Footnote: of the nature based on primary signification
Of these, the first — consisting of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest — is counted as one alone here;

children.text: eko 'pi bhedo 'nantatvāt saṅkhyeyas tasya naiva yat // VisSd_4.5 //
children.translated_text: and even though [it is] one division, because of its infiniteness, its sub-varieties cannot be enumerated.
The suggested meaning arises from the power of word, meaning, or both — resembling an after-resonance (<s>anusvāna</s>);

children.text: dhvanir lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgyas trividhaḥ kathito budhaiḥ // VisSd_4.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>dhvani</s> with perceptible process of suggestion (<s>lakṣya-krama-vyaṅgya</s>) is said by the wise to be threefold.
That arising from the power of the word is twofold, since the suggested meaning takes the form of a thing (<s>vastu</s>) or an ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>);

children.text: vastu vālaṅkṛtir veti dvidhārthaḥ saṃbhavī svataḥ // VisSd_4.7 //
children.translated_text: the meaning-based is twofold as well — either a thing or an ornament — and is self-generated.

children.text: kaveḥ prauḍhokti-sikto vā tan nibaddhasya veti ṣaṭ /
children.translated_text: Or it may be saturated by the poet's bold expression (<s>prauḍhokti</s>), or it may be inherent in the composition — thus six [varieties].

children.text: ṣaḍbhis tair vyajyamānas tu vastv alaṅkāra-rūpakaḥ // VisSd_4.8 //
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning, expressed through those six, takes the form of a thing or an ornament —
the suggested meaning arising from the power of meaning reaches twelve varieties.

children.text: ekaḥ śabdārtha-śakty-utthe tad aṣṭadaśadhā dhvaniḥ // VisSd_4.9 //
children.translated_text: The one arising from both word and meaning-power — thus <s>dhvani</s> is of eighteen kinds.
In a sentence, that arising from word and meaning-power; the others [arise] from word, sentence,

children.text: prabandhe 'pi mato dhīrair artha-śakty-udbhavo dhvaniḥ // VisSd_4.10 //
children.translated_text: and in a composition (<s>prabandha</s>) as well — the wise consider <s>dhvani</s> arising from the power of meaning.
In word-parts, syllable-arrangements, and compositions — with imperceptible process [of suggestion] —

children.text: tad evam eka-pañcāśad bhedās tasya dhvaner matāḥ // VisSd_4.11 //
children.translated_text: thus fifty-one varieties of that <s>dhvani</s> are recognized.
Through threefold combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) or through blending (<s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>), in many ways —
[the numbers indicated by the code-words:] Veda (4), sky (0), ocean (4), arrows (5); arrows (5), missiles (5), fire (3), missiles (5).

children.text: aparaṃ tu guṇī-bhūta-vyaṅgyaṃ vācyād anuttame vyaṅgye /
children.translated_text: The other [kind] is <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> (poetry with subordinated suggestion) — when the suggested meaning does not surpass the expressed.

children.text: tatra syād itarāṅgaṃ kākvākṣiptaṃ ca vācya-siddha-vyaṅgyam // VisSd_4.13 //
children.translated_text: There, it may be subordinate to another [element], or implied by tone (<s>kākv-ākṣiptam</s>), or the suggestion may be established through the expressed meaning.
Doubtful predominance, equal predominance, indistinct [suggestion], non-hidden

children.text: vyaṅgyam asundaram evaṃ bhedās tasyoditā aṣṭau // VisSd_4.14 //
children.translated_text: suggestion, unattractive suggestion — thus eight varieties of it have been stated.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, called 'The Examination of the Division of Poetry into <s>Dhvani</s> and <s>Guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s>,' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(5) Fifth Chapter.
Of the [three] semantic functions — <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification), and the rest — beyond these,

children.text: aṅgīkāryā turyā vṛttir bodhe rasādīnām // VisSd_5.1 //
children.translated_text: a fourth function must be accepted for the apprehension of <s>rasa</s> and the rest.
Due to differences in the knower, [its own] nature, number, cause, effect, apprehension, time,
locus, object, and the rest — the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) differs from the expressed meaning (<s>abhidheya</s>).

children.text: prāg asattvād rasāder no bodhike lakṣaṇābhidhe /
children.translated_text: Since <s>rasa</s> and the rest did not exist before [poetic expression], <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and <s>abhidhā</s> are not capable of apprehending [them];

children.text: kiṃ ca mukhyārtha-bādhasya virahād api lakṣaṇā // VisSd_5.3 //
children.translated_text: moreover, because there is no obstruction of the primary meaning, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) [does not apply].
Nor is inference capable of apprehending <s>rasa</s> and the other suggested meanings,

children.text: ābhāsatvena hetūnāṃ smṛtir na ca rasādi-dhīḥ // VisSd_5.4 //
children.translated_text: because the 'reasons' [used] would be mere semblances; and memory is not the cognition of <s>rasa</s> and the like.

children.text: sā ceyaṃ vyañjanā-nāma vṛttir ity ucyate budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This very [function] is called <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) — thus say the wise;

children.text: rasa-vyaktau punar vṛttiṃ rasanākhyāṃ pare viduḥ // VisSd_5.5 //
children.translated_text: but in the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> specifically, others know the function as <s>rasanā</s> (tasting).

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe
vyañjanā-vyapāra-nirūpaṇo nāma
pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, called 'The Examination of the Function of <s>Vyañjanā</s> (Suggestion),' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(6) Sixth Chapter.
Poetry is again considered to be of two kinds, based on the distinction of being visible (<s>dṛśya</s>) and audible (<s>śravya</s>).

children.text: dṛśyaṃ tatrābhineyaṃ tad-rūpāropāt tu rūpakam // VisSd_6.1 //
children.translated_text: That which is visible is to be enacted (<s>abhineyam</s>); due to the superimposition of the form [of the character on the actor], it is called <s>rūpaka</s> (dramatic composition).
<s>Abhinaya</s> (dramatic representation) is the imitation of a state; it is fourfold:

children.text: āṅgiko vācikaś caivam āhāryaḥ sāttvikas tathā // VisSd_6.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>āṅgika</s> (bodily), <s>vācika</s> (verbal), <s>āhārya</s> (costume/makeup), and <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary emotional expressions).
<s>Nāṭaka</s>, <s>Prakaraṇa</s>, <s>Bhāṇa</s>, <s>Vyāyoga</s>, <s>Samavakāra</s>, <s>Ḍima</s>,

children.text: īhāmṛgāṅka-vīthyaḥ prahasanam iti rūpakāṇi daśa // VisSd_6.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Īhāmṛga</s>, <s>Aṅka</s>, <s>Vīthī</s>, and <s>Prahasana</s> — these are the ten [major] dramatic forms (<s>rūpakas</s>).
<s>Nāṭikā</s>, <s>Troṭaka</s>, <s>Goṣṭhī</s>, <s>Saṭṭaka</s>, <s>Nāṭya-rāsaka</s>,
<s>Prasthāna</s>, <s>Ullāpya</s>, <s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Preṅkhaṇa</s>, <s>Rāsaka</s> likewise,
<s>Saṃlāpaka</s>, <s>Śrī-gadita</s>, <s>Śilpaka</s>, and <s>Vilāsikā</s>,

children.text: durmallikā prakaraṇī hallīśako bhāṇiketi ca // VisSd_6.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Durmallikā</s>, <s>Prakaraṇī</s>, <s>Hallīśaka</s>, and <s>Bhāṇikā</s> —
the learned declare these eighteen to be the minor dramatic forms (<s>uparūpakas</s>).

children.text: vinā viśeṣaṃ sarveṣāṃ lakṣma nāṭakavan matam // VisSd_6.6 //
children.translated_text: Without distinction, the characteristics of all are considered to be like those of <s>nāṭaka</s>.
A <s>nāṭaka</s> should have a well-known plot (<s>khyāta-vṛtta</s>), be endowed with five junctures (<s>sandhi</s>),
possessing qualities of grace (<s>vilāsa</s>), prosperity (<s>ṛddhi</s>), and the rest, furnished with various splendors.
Abounding in various <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), with the arising of happiness and sorrow,
its acts (<s>aṅkas</s>) are declared to be from five to ten at most.
The hero should be of renowned lineage, a royal sage (<s>rājarṣi</s>), of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-steadfast) type, valorous,

children.text: divyo 'tha divyādivyo vā guṇavān nāyako mataḥ // VisSd_6.9 //
children.translated_text: either divine, or of mixed divine-and-human [nature], and endowed with virtues.

children.text: eka eva bhaved aṅgī śṛṅgāro vīra eva vā /
children.translated_text: There should be one predominant (<s>aṅgī</s>) [rasa] — either <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) or <s>vīra</s> (the heroic);

children.text: aṅgam anye rasāḥ sarve kāryo nirvahaṇe 'dbhutaḥ // VisSd_6.10 //
children.translated_text: all other <s>rasas</s> are subordinate (<s>aṅga</s>); <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous) should be employed in the denouement (<s>nirvahaṇa</s>).
There should be four or five principal characters engaged in the action.

children.text: gopucchāgra-samāgraṃ tu bandhanaṃ tasya kīrtitam // VisSd_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Its construction is described as gradually tapering like the tip of a cow's tail.
The action of the hero should be directly witnessed, resplendent with <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>,
with language that is not obscure, furnished with small metrical compositions (<s>cūrṇakas</s>).
With intervening sub-plots of a single purpose, somewhat connected by <s>bindus</s> (dots/links),

children.text: yukto na bahubhiḥ kāryair bīja-saṃhṛtimān na ca // VisSd_6.13 //
children.translated_text: not overburdened with many sub-plots, and not having [separate] seed and resolution.
Furnished with various arrangements, not excessively full of verses,
constructed without omitting any of the essential actions,
not employing a story that requires many days to unfold,

children.text: āsanna-nāyakaḥ pātrair yuktas tri-caturais tathā // VisSd_6.15 //
children.translated_text: with the hero readily accessible, and furnished with three or four characters.
Summoning from afar, killing, battle, the overthrow of a kingdom or country,

children.text: vivāho bhojanaṃ śāpotsargau mṛtyū rataṃ tathā // VisSd_6.16 //
children.translated_text: marriage, eating, pronouncing and lifting a curse, death, and lovemaking,

children.text: danta-cchedyaṃ nakha-cchedyam anyad vrīḍākaraṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: biting, scratching, and whatever else causes embarrassment,
sleeping, kissing the lips, and the like, and the siege of a city and the like —
a [nāṭaka] should be free from these and not excessively long.
With the queen, attendants, and the like, and ministers and merchants as well,
furnished with directly-witnessed, varied exploits arising from emotional states and <s>rasas</s>,
with all characters exiting at the end — this is declared to be an act (<s>aṅka</s>).
An act inserted within another act, featuring a stage-dancer's prologue and the like,

children.text: aṅko 'paraḥ sa garbhāṅkaḥ sa-bījaḥ phalavān api // VisSd_6.20 //
children.translated_text: is another act — that is called <s>garbhāṅka</s> (an embedded act); it too has a seed and a fruit.

children.text: tatra pūrvaṃ pūrva-raṅgaḥ sabhā-pūjā tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: There, first comes the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> (preliminary performance); then the greeting of the assembly;
then the mention of the poet's name and the like; and then the prologue (<s>āmukha</s>) of the <s>nāṭaka</s>.
That which the actors (<s>kuśīlavas</s>) perform before the dramatic action proper,

children.text: kuśīlavāḥ prakurvanti pūrva-raṅgaḥ sa ucyate // VisSd_6.22 //
children.translated_text: for the pacification of obstacles to the performance — that is called <s>pūrvaraṅga</s>.
Although its constituent parts such as <s>pratyāhāra</s> and the rest are numerous,

children.text: tathāpy avaśyaṃ kartavyā nāndī vighnopaśāntaye // VisSd_6.23 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, the <s>nāndī</s> (benedictory verse) must necessarily be performed for the pacification of obstacles.
Because a eulogy combined with words of blessing is performed
for gods, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, and the rest — therefore it is called <s>nāndī</s>.
Containing words suggestive of auspiciousness, conch-shells, the moon, lotuses, <s>koka</s> (ruddy geese), and night-lotuses,

children.text: padair yuktā dvādaśabhir aṣṭābhir vā padair uta // VisSd_6.25 //
children.translated_text: composed of twelve or else of eight <s>padas</s> (metrical feet).
Having performed the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s>, the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager) exits;

children.text: praviśya sthāpakas tadvat kāvyam āsthāpayet tataḥ // VisSd_6.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sthāpaka</s> (introducer), entering likewise, should then introduce the dramatic work.

children.text: divya-martye sa tad-rūpo miśram anyataras tayoḥ /
children.translated_text: He may be of divine or human type, or of mixed [nature] resembling either;

children.text: sūcayed vastu bījaṃ vā mukhaṃ pātram athāpi vā // VisSd_6.27 //
children.translated_text: he should hint at the subject matter (<s>vastu</s>), the seed (<s>bīja</s>), the prologue (<s>mukha</s>), or the character (<s>pātra</s>).
Having pleased the audience (<s>raṅga</s>) with sweet verses hinting at the meaning of the work,

children.text: rūpakasya kaver ākhyāṃ gotrādyāpi sa kīrtayet // VisSd_6.28 //
children.translated_text: he should proclaim the name, lineage, and the like of the poet of the <s>rūpaka</s> (dramatic composition).

children.text: ṛtuṃ ca kañcit prāyeṇa bhāratīṃ vṛttim āśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: And [he should mention] some season, generally resorting to the <s>Bhāratī</s> style of dramatic presentation.
<s>Bhāratī</s> is the verbal activity primarily in Sanskrit, having the actor as its basis.
Its [constituent parts] are: <s>prarocanā</s> (enticement), <s>vīthī</s> (lane), and the prologues of <s>prahasana</s> (farce).
Among these, <s>prarocanā</s> is the creation of interest through praise.

children.text: naṭī vidūṣāko vāpi pāripārśvika eva vā /
children.translated_text: The actress (<s>naṭī</s>), the jester (<s>vidūṣaka</s>), or the attendant (<s>pāripārśvika</s>),

children.text: sūtradhāreṇa sahitāḥ saṃlāpaṃ yatra kurvate // VisSd_6.31 //
children.translated_text: together with the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager), where they engage in dialogue —
through utterances arising from their own affairs that allude to the subject at hand, reciprocally,

children.text: āmukhaṃ tat tu vijñeyaṃ nāmnā prastāvanāpi sā // VisSd_6.32 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as the <s>āmukha</s> (introduction), which is also called <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue) by name.
<s>Uddhātyaka</s>, <s>kathodghāta</s>, <s>prayogātiśaya</s>,
<s>pravartakā</s>, and <s>avalagita</s> — these are the five types of <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue).
When words whose meaning has not been [fully] conveyed, in order to convey that meaning,

children.text: yojayanti padair anyaiḥ sa uddhātyaka ucyate // VisSd_6.34 //
children.translated_text: are connected with other words by people — that is called <s>uddhātyaka</s>.

children.text: sūtradhārasya vākyaṃ vā samādāyārtham asya vā /
children.translated_text: If a character enters by taking up the words of the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager) or [adopting] their meaning,

children.text: bhavet pātra-praveśaś cet kathodghātaḥ sa ucyate // VisSd_6.35 //
children.translated_text: and thereby a character's entrance occurs — that is called <s>kathodghāta</s>.
If during one performance, another performance is introduced,

children.text: tena pātra-praveśaś cet prayogātiśayas tadā // VisSd_6.36 //
children.translated_text: and through that a character enters — that is <s>prayogātiśaya</s>.

children.text: kālaṃ pravṛttam āśritya sūtra-dhṛg yatra varṇayet /
children.translated_text: When the <s>sūtradhāra</s>, referring to the current time or season, describes [something],

children.text: tad-āśrayaś ca pātrasya praveśas tat-pravartakam // VisSd_6.37 //
children.translated_text: and based on that a character enters — that is <s>pravartaka</s>.
When, by the merging of one [action] into another, a different purpose is accomplished

children.text: prayoge khalu taj jñeyaṃ nāmnāvalagitaṃ budhaiḥ // VisSd_6.38 //
children.translated_text: in the performance — that is to be known by the wise as <s>avalagita</s>.
The constituent elements of the <s>vīthī</s> and others may also be employed here as appropriate.

children.text: nepathoktaṃ śrutaṃ yatra tv ākāśa-vacanaṃ tathā // VisSd_6.39 //
children.translated_text: Where something spoken behind the curtain (<s>nepathya</s>) is heard — that is called <s>ākāśa-vacana</s> (voice from space);
based on that too, the <s>āmukha</s> (introduction) should be constructed in <s>nāṭakas</s> and the like.

children.text: eṣām āmukha-bhedānām ekaṃ kañcit prayojayet // VisSd_6.40 //
children.translated_text: Of these varieties of <s>āmukha</s>, one should employ any one.

children.text: tenārtham atha pātraṃ vā samākṣipyaiva sūtra-dhṛk /
children.translated_text: Having alluded to the subject or the character through it, the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager)

children.text: prastāvanānte nirgacchet tato vastu prayojayet // VisSd_6.41 //
children.translated_text: should exit at the end of the <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue); then the dramatic action should commence.

children.text: idaṃ punar vastu budhair dvividhaṃ parikalpyate /
children.translated_text: This subject matter (<s>vastu</s>) is again conceived as twofold by the learned:

children.text: ādhikārikam ekaṃ syāt prāsaṅgikam athāparam // VisSd_6.42 //
children.translated_text: one is <s>ādhikārika</s> (principal) and the other is <s>prāsaṅgika</s> (incidental). ||6.42||

children.text: adhikāraḥ phale svāmyam adhikārī ca tat-prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Adhikāra</s> (authority) is sovereignty over the fruit [of the plot]; the <s>adhikārin</s> (principal character) is its lord.
His story is called <s>ādhikārika</s> (the principal narrative) by poets. ||6.43||
That which serves to support it is regarded as <s>prāsaṅgika</s> (incidental).
The <s>patākāsthānaka</s> (episode-device) should be carefully applied to the subject matter here. ||6.44||
When, while one meaning is being contemplated, another bearing the mark of that [meaning] is employed

children.text: āgantukena bhāvena patākā-sthānakaṃ tu tat // VisSd_6.45 //
children.translated_text: through an adventitious sentiment — that is the <s>patākāsthānaka</s> (episode-device). ||6.45||
The sudden acquisition of meaning through a commendable figurative expression —
this is declared to be the first type of <s>patākāsthānaka</s>. ||6.46||
Speech that is exceedingly apt, well-connected, and based on various compositional structures —
this is declared to be the second type of <s>patākāsthānaka</s>. ||6.47||

children.text: arthopakṣepakaṃ yat tu līnaṃ sa-vinayaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: That which introduces a topic, is concealed, respectful,
and accompanied by an apt reply — this is said to be the third. ||6.48||
A double-meaninged arrangement of words, well-connected, employed in poetry,
that suggests another meaning alongside the main one — that is the supreme <s>patākāsthānaka</s>. ||6.49||

children.text: yat syād anucitaṃ vastu nāyakasya rasasya vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever subject matter would be inappropriate for the hero or the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment),

children.text: viruddhaṃ tat parityājyam anyathā vā prakalpayet // VisSd_6.50 //
children.translated_text: or contradictory — that should be abandoned or conceived otherwise. ||6.50||

children.text: aṅkeṣv adarśanīyā yā vaktavyaiva ca saṃmatā /
children.translated_text: That which should not be shown on stage but is agreed to be worth narrating,

children.text: yā ca syād varṣa-paryantaṃ kathā dina-dvayādijā // VisSd_6.51 //
children.translated_text: and a story extending up to a year but generated from two days or so — ||6.51||

children.text: anyā ca vistarā sūcyā sārthopakṣepair budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: and other extensive [matters] should be indicated by the learned through meaningful introductions (<s>arthopakṣepa</s>).

children.text: varṣād ūrdhvaṃ tu yad vastu tat syād varṣād adhobhavam // VisSd_6.52 //
children.translated_text: But subject matter beyond a year should be [presented as if it] occurred within a year. ||6.52||
What must happen at the end of a day, yet does not fit within the [stage-]day itself,

children.text: arthopakṣepakair vācyam aṅka-cchedaṃ vidhāya tat // VisSd_6.53 //
children.translated_text: should be narrated through <s>arthopakṣepakas</s> (introductory devices), having made a break between acts. ||6.53||
The <s>arthopakṣepakas</s> (introductory devices) are five: <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude) and <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance scene),

children.text: cūlikāṅkāvatāro 'tha syād aṅka-mukham ity api // VisSd_6.54 //
children.translated_text: <s>cūlikā</s> (behind-the-curtain scene), <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-transition), and <s>aṅkamukha</s> (act-opening). ||6.54||
That which indicates portions of the story — past and future —

children.text: saṅkṣiptārthas tu viṣkambha ādāv aṅkasya darśitaḥ // VisSd_6.55 //
children.translated_text: in summarized form is the <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude), shown at the beginning of an act. ||6.55||
Composed with middle[-ranking] or two middle-ranking characters,

children.text: śuddhaḥ syāt sa tu saṅkīrṇo nīca-madhyama-kalpitaḥ // VisSd_6.56 //
children.translated_text: it is called 'pure' (<s>śuddha</s>); but if composed with low and middle characters, it is 'mixed' (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>). ||6.56||
The <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance scene), with speech of low characters and employing low-ranking persons,

children.text: aṅka-dvayāntar vijñeyaḥ śeṣaṃ viṣkambhake yathā // VisSd_6.57 //
children.translated_text: should be understood as occurring between two acts; the rest is as in the <s>viṣkambhaka</s>. ||6.57||
The <s>cūlikā</s> (behind-the-curtain scene) indicates meaning through [characters] stationed behind the curtain,
at the end of an act, indicated by characters [speaking] without [visible] division of that act. ||6.58||
Where one act descends [into another] — that is known as the <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-transition).

children.text: yatra syād aṅka ekasminn aṅkānāṃ sūcanākhilā // VisSd_6.59 //
children.translated_text: Where, in a single act, all the acts are indicated — ||6.59||

children.text: tad-aṅka-mukham ity āhur bījārtha-khyāpakaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: that is called <s>aṅkamukha</s> (act-opening), and it also makes known the seed-meaning (<s>bījārtha</s>).
Or, the <s>aṅkāsya</s> (face of the act) [occurs] through characters at the end of an act, by indicating the meaning of an interrupted act. ||6.60||
Subject matter that is expected, [but] flavorless, and extensive — should be abandoned.

children.text: yadā sandarśayec cheṣam āmukhānantaraṃ tadā // VisSd_6.61 //
children.translated_text: When [the poet] shows the remainder [of the story] after the <s>āmukha</s> (prologue), then ||6.61||
a <s>viṣkambhaka</s> should be composed in the drama, with characters introduced by the prologue.

children.text: yadā tu sarasaṃ vastu mūlād eva pravartate // VisSd_6.62 //
children.translated_text: But when the flavorful subject matter proceeds directly from the root — ||6.62||
then the act should begin directly with the prologue-introduction.

children.text: viṣkambhakādyair api no vadho vācyo 'dhikāriṇaḥ // VisSd_6.63 //
children.translated_text: Even through <s>viṣkambhakas</s> and the like, the death of the principal character should not be described. ||6.63||
One [element] should not conceal another among the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) and subject matter.

children.text: bījaṃ binduḥ patākā ca prakarī kāryam eva ca // VisSd_6.64 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bīja</s> (seed), <s>bindu</s> (drop), <s>patākā</s> (episode), <s>prakarī</s> (sub-episode), and <s>kārya</s> (action) — ||6.64||
these five <s>arthaprakṛtis</s> (elements of the plot) should be known and employed according to rule.

children.text: alpa-mātraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ bahudhā yad visarpati // VisSd_6.65 //
children.translated_text: That which, though indicated in small measure, spreads extensively — ||6.65||

children.text: phalasya prathamo hetur bījaṃ tad abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: the first cause of the fruit [of the plot] — that is called <s>bīja</s> (the seed).
<s>Bindu</s> (the drop) is the cause of continuity when there is an interruption of the subsidiary meaning. ||6.66||
The pervasive incidental narrative is called <s>patākā</s> (the episode).

children.text: patākā-nāyakasya syān na svakīyaṃ phalāntaram // VisSd_6.67 //
children.translated_text: The hero of the <s>patākā</s> should not have a separate fruit of his own. ||6.67||

children.text: garbhe sandhau vimarśe vā virvāhas tasya jāyate /
children.translated_text: His resolution arises in the <s>garbha</s> (development) juncture or in the <s>vimarśa</s> (pause) juncture.

children.text: prāsaṅgikaṃ pradeśasthaṃ caritaṃ prakarī matā // VisSd_6.68 //
children.translated_text: An incidental narrative confined to a particular section is considered <s>prakarī</s> (the sub-episode). ||6.68||

children.text: prakarī nāyakasya syān na svakīyaṃ phalāntaram /
children.translated_text: The hero of the <s>prakarī</s> should not have a separate fruit of his own.

children.text: apekṣitaṃ tu yat sādhyam ārambho yan nibandhanaḥ // VisSd_6.69 //
children.translated_text: That which is the desired goal to be accomplished, on which the commencement is based, ||6.69||

children.text: samāpanaṃ tu yat-siddhyai tat kāryam iti saṃmatam /
children.translated_text: and for whose accomplishment [the plot reaches] conclusion — that is accepted as <s>kārya</s> (the action).

children.text: avasthāḥ pañca kāryasya prārabdhasya phalārthibhiḥ // VisSd_6.70 //
children.translated_text: There are five states of the action once undertaken by those seeking the fruit: ||6.70||
commencement (<s>ārambha</s>), effort (<s>yatna</s>), hope of attainment (<s>prāptyāśā</s>), certain attainment (<s>niyatāpti</s>), and arrival of the fruit (<s>phalāgama</s>).

children.text: bhaved ārabhya autsukyaṃ yan mukhya-phala-siddhaye // VisSd_6.71 //
children.translated_text: The eagerness that arises toward the accomplishment of the principal fruit is [the state of commencement]. ||6.71||
Effort (<s>prayatna</s>) is activity accompanied by great haste for the attainment of the fruit.
Through [considerations of] means and dangers, the hope of attainment (<s>prāptyāśā</s>) is the possibility of attainment. ||6.72||
Due to the absence of danger, the attainment is certain — that is <s>niyatāpti</s> (certain attainment).

children.text: sāvasthā phala-yogaḥ syād yaḥ samagra-phalodayaḥ // VisSd_6.73 //
children.translated_text: The state of union with the fruit, which is the complete arising of the [entire] fruit — [is <s>phalāgama</s>]. ||6.73||

children.text: yathā-saṅkhyam avasthābhir ābhir yogāt tu pañcabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: In correspondence with these five states, through their combination,

children.text: pañcadhaivetivṛttasya bhāgāḥ syuḥ pañca sandhayaḥ // VisSd_6.74 //
children.translated_text: the portions of the plot become fivefold — these are the five junctures (<s>sandhi</s>). ||6.74||
A juncture (<s>sandhi</s>) is the internal connection of a single purpose, when there is a conclusion.

children.text: mukhaṃ pratimukhaṃ garbho vimarśa upasaṃhṛtiḥ // VisSd_6.75 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mukha</s> (the opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (the progression), <s>garbha</s> (the development), <s>vimarśa</s> (the pause), and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> (the conclusion) — ||6.75||

children.text: iti pañcāsya bhedāḥ syuḥ kramāl lākṣaṇam ucyate /
children.translated_text: these are its five divisions; their characteristics are stated in order.
Where the seed (<s>bīja</s>) arises, giving birth to various meanings and <s>rasas</s> (sentiments), ||6.76||
combined with the commencement — that is declared as <s>mukha</s> (the opening).
Where the principal means toward the fruit, established in the opening juncture, ||6.77||

children.text: lakṣyālakṣya ivodbhedo yatra pratimukhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: breaks forth as if perceptibly or imperceptibly — that is the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression).
Where the principal means toward the fruit, previously broken forth, somewhat ||6.78||
[develops] — the <s>garbha</s> (development) is where there is a breaking forth accompanied by repeated search and laughter.
Where the principal means toward the fruit breaks forth even more than in the <s>garbha</s>, ||6.79||

children.text: śāpādyaiḥ sāntarāyaś ca sa vimarśa iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: and is accompanied by obstacles such as curses and the like — that is known as <s>vimarśa</s> (the pause).
Where the seed-bearing meanings of the opening and the rest, scattered as appropriate, ||6.80||

children.text: ekārtham upanīyante yatra nirvahaṇaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: are brought together to a single purpose — that is <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (the conclusion).
<s>Upakṣepa</s> (introduction), <s>parikara</s> (elaboration), <s>parinyāsa</s> (establishment), <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement), ||6.81||
<s>yukti</s> (reasoning), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (reflection),

children.text: udbhedaḥ karaṇaṃ bheda etāny aṅgāni vai mukhe // VisSd_6.82 //
children.translated_text: <s>udbheda</s> (sprouting), <s>karaṇa</s> (execution), and <s>bheda</s> (division) — these are the constituents of the <s>mukha</s> (opening). ||6.82||
The origination of the poetic meaning is known as <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction).
The abundance of meaning once originated should be known as <s>parikara</s> (elaboration). ||6.83||
Its completion is <s>parinyāsa</s> (establishment). The narration of qualities is <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement).

children.text: saṃpradhāraṇam arthānāṃ yuktiḥ prāptiḥ sukhāgamaḥ // VisSd_6.84 //
children.translated_text: The deliberation of meanings is <s>yukti</s> (reasoning). <s>Prāpti</s> (attainment) is the arrival of happiness. ||6.84||

children.text: bījasyāgamanaṃ yat tu tat samādhānam ucyate /
children.translated_text: The approach of the seed is called <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution).

children.text: sukha-duḥkha-kṛto yo 'rthas tad vidhānam iti smṛtam // VisSd_6.85 //
children.translated_text: The matter that produces happiness or sorrow is known as <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement). ||6.85||
Words that produce curiosity are called <s>paribhāvanā</s> (reflection).

children.text: bījārthasya prarohaḥ syād udbhedaḥ karaṇaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_6.86 //
children.translated_text: The sprouting of the seed-meaning is <s>udbheda</s> (sprouting). <s>Karaṇa</s> (execution) is ||6.86||
the commencement of the matter at hand. <s>Bheda</s> (division) is the breaking apart of what is joined.

children.text: vilāsaḥ parisarpaś ca vidhutaṃ tāpanaṃ tathā // VisSd_6.87 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vilāsa</s> (dalliance), <s>parisarpa</s> (pursuit), <s>vidhuta</s> (rejection), <s>tāpana</s> (torment), ||6.87||

children.text: narma narma-dyutiś caiva tathā pragamanaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>narma</s> (jest), <s>narmadyuti</s> (wit), and likewise <s>pragamana</s> (advance),

children.text: virodhaś ca pratimukhe tathā syāt paryupāsanam // VisSd_6.88 //
children.translated_text: <s>virodha</s> (conflict), and <s>paryupāsana</s> (conciliation) — these are [constituents] in the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression). ||6.88||

children.text: puṣpaṃ vajram upanyāso varṇa-saṃhāra ity api /
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpa</s> (flower), <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), <s>upanyāsa</s> (persuasion), <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (stratagem) — and also:

children.text: samīhā rati-bhogārthā vilāsa iti kathyate // VisSd_6.89 //
children.translated_text: A desire for amorous enjoyment is called <s>vilāsa</s> (dalliance). ||6.89||
The pursuit of something desired [but] lost is called <s>parisarpa</s> (pursuit).
The non-acceptance of a conciliation that was previously offered — that is <s>vidhuta</s> (rejection). ||6.90||

children.text: upāyādarśanaṃ yat tu tāpanaṃ nāma tad bhavet /
children.translated_text: The non-appearance of a means — that is called <s>tāpana</s> (torment).

children.text: parihāsa-vaco narma dhṛtis tu parihāsa-jā // VisSd_6.91 //
children.translated_text: Jesting speech is <s>narma</s> (jest). The composure born of jest ||6.91||
is <s>narmadyuti</s> (wit). <s>Pragamana</s> (advance) is speech that is one after another [i.e., escalating].
<s>Virodha</s> (conflict) is encountering calamity. The conciliation of one who is angry ||6.92||
is <s>paryupāsana</s> (conciliation). <s>Puṣpa</s> (flower) is considered to be distinguished speech.
<s>Vajra</s> (thunderbolt) is open harshness. <s>Upanyāsa</s> (persuasion) is propitiation. ||6.93||
The approach through the four methods [<s>sāma</s>, <s>dāna</s>, <s>bheda</s>, <s>daṇḍa</s>] is held to be <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (stratagem).
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> (false attribution), <s>mārga</s> (path), <s>rūpa</s> (semblance), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), <s>krama</s> (sequence), ||6.94||

children.text: saṅgrahaś cānumānaṃ ca prārthanā kṣiptir eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>saṅgraha</s> (collection), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>prārthanā</s> (supplication), <s>kṣipti</s> (dispatch),

children.text: troṭakādhibalodvegā garbhe syur vidravas tathā // VisSd_6.95 //
children.translated_text: <s>troṭaka</s> (break), <s>adhibala</s> (overpowering), <s>udvega</s> (alarm), and <s>vidrava</s> (flight) — these are [constituents] in the <s>garbha</s> (development). ||6.95||
Therein, a statement based on pretense is considered <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (false attribution).

children.text: tattvārtha-kathanaṃ mārgo rūpaṃ vākyaṃ vitarkavat // VisSd_6.96 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mārga</s> (path) is the narration of the true meaning. <s>Rūpa</s> (semblance) is a conjectural statement. ||6.96||
<s>Udāharaṇa</s> (illustration) is said to be a statement endowed with exaggeration.

children.text: bhāva-tattvopalabdhis tu kramaḥ syāt saṅgrahaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_6.97 //
children.translated_text: The ascertainment of the true nature of sentiments is <s>krama</s> (sequence). <s>Saṅgraha</s> (collection) is ||6.97||
that which is endowed with <s>sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>dāna</s> (gifts), and similar meanings. Inference from signs is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

children.text: rati-harṣotsavānāṃ tu prārthanaṃ prārthanā bhavet // VisSd_6.98 //
children.translated_text: The entreaty for love, joy, and festivity is <s>prārthanā</s> (supplication). ||6.98||

children.text: rahasyārthasya tad-bhedaḥ kṣiptiḥ syāt toṭakaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The disclosure of a secret matter — that is <s>kṣipti</s> (dispatch). <s>Troṭaka</s> (break) is
angry speech. <s>Adhibala</s> (overpowering) is [overpowering] through the stratagem of a compact. ||6.99||
Fear generated by a king and the like is declared to be <s>udvega</s> (alarm).
Confusion caused by doubt, fear, and terror is considered <s>vidrava</s> (flight). ||6.100||
<s>Apavāda</s> (censure), <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (confrontation), <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve), <s>drava</s> (agitation), <s>dyuti</s> (splendor),

children.text: śaktiḥ prasaṅgaḥ khedaś ca pratiṣedho virodhanam // VisSd_6.101 //
children.translated_text: <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>prasaṅga</s> (occasion), <s>kheda</s> (weariness), <s>pratiṣedha</s> (prohibition), and <s>virodha</s> (opposition) — ||6.101||

children.text: prarocanā vimarśe syād ādānaṃ chādanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>prarocanā</s> (inspiration) — these are [constituents] in the <s>vimarśa</s> (pause). <s>Ādāna</s> (appropriation) and <s>chādana</s> (concealment) likewise.
The proclamation of a fault is <s>apavāda</s> (censure). <s>Saṃpheṭa</s> (confrontation) is speech [born] of anger. ||6.102||
<s>Vyavasāya</s> (resolve) should be known as arising from assertion and reason.
<s>Drava</s> (agitation) is the transgression of a superior, arising from grief, excitement, and the like. ||6.103||

children.text: tarjanodvejane proktā dyutih śaktiḥ punar bhavet /
children.translated_text: Threatening and alarming are said to be <s>dyuti</s> (splendor). <s>Śakti</s> (power) is
the pacification of conflict. <s>Prasaṅga</s> (occasion) is the glorification of an elder. ||6.104||

children.text: manaś ceṣṭā-samutpannaḥ śramaḥ kheda iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kheda</s> (weariness) is known as the fatigue arising from the activities of the mind.
<s>Pratiṣedha</s> (prohibition) is held to be the obstruction of the desired goal. ||6.105||
<s>Virodhana</s> (opposition) is known as the approaching of a calamity regarding the action.
<s>Prarocanā</s> (inspiration) should be known as that which shows the purpose of the conclusion. ||6.106||

children.text: kārya-saṅgraha ādānaṃ tad āhuś chādanaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ādāna</s> (appropriation) is the gathering up of the action. And <s>chādana</s> (concealment) is said to be

children.text: kāryārtham apamānādeḥ sahanaṃ khalu yad bhavet // VisSd_6.107 //
children.translated_text: the endurance of insults and the like for the sake of the action. ||6.107||
<s>Sandhi</s> (reconciliation), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>grathana</s> (weaving), <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (narration),

children.text: kṛtiḥ prasāda ānandaḥ samayo 'py upagūhanam // VisSd_6.108 //
children.translated_text: <s>kṛti</s> (accomplishment), <s>prasāda</s> (grace), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>samaya</s> (agreement), and <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace), ||6.108||

children.text: bhāṣaṇaṃ pūrva-vākyaṃ ca kāvya-saṃhāra eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>bhāṣaṇa</s> (discourse), <s>pūrvavākya</s> (prior statement), <s>kāvyasaṃhāra</s> (poetic conclusion),

children.text: praśastir iti saṃhāre jñeyāny aṅgāni nāmataḥ // VisSd_6.109 //
children.translated_text: and <s>praśasti</s> (eulogy) — these are to be known by name as the constituents of the <s>saṃhāra</s> (conclusion). ||6.109||
The approach of the seed is <s>sandhi</s> (reconciliation). <s>Vibodha</s> (awakening) is the search for the action.

children.text: upanāyasas tu kāryāṇāṃ grathanaṃ nirṇayaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_6.110 //
children.translated_text: The weaving together of affairs is <s>grathana</s> (weaving). <s>Nirṇaya</s> (determination) is ||6.110||
the narration of experienced events, as they say. <s>Paribhāṣaṇa</s> (narration) is
speech made in reproach. The pacification of the attained result is <s>kṛti</s> (accomplishment). ||6.111||
<s>Prasāda</s> (grace) is devoted service and the like. <s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is the arrival of what was desired.

children.text: samayo duḥkha-niryāṇaṃ tad bhaved upagūhanam // VisSd_6.112 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samaya</s> (agreement) is the departure of sorrow. <s>Upagūhana</s> (embrace) would be ||6.112||
the attainment of something wonderful. <s>Bhāṣaṇa</s> (discourse) is [speech involving] conciliation, gifts, and the like.
<s>Pūrvavākya</s> (prior statement) should be known as the demonstration of meaning as stated before. ||6.113||
The attainment of the granting of a boon is held to be <s>kāvyasaṃhāra</s> (the poetic conclusion).
The pacification of a king, country, and the like is called <s>praśasti</s> (panegyric). ||6.114||

children.text: catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi-vidhaṃ hy etad aṅgaṃ proktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This limb [of plot] has been declared by the wise to be of sixty-four kinds.

children.text: kuryād aniyate tasya sandhāv api niveśanam // VisSd_6.115 //
children.translated_text: One should place it even in a <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) where it is not prescribed. ||6.115||
Observing conformity to <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), for <s>rasa</s> alone has primacy.
The attainment of the desired object, the wonder of the composition, and the expansion of the narrative — ||6.116||
the attainment of passion, the concealment of what is to be concealed in the performance,

children.text: prakāśanaṃ prakāśyānām aṅgānāṃ ṣaḍ-vidhaṃ phalam // VisSd_6.117 //
children.translated_text: and the revelation of what is to be revealed — these are the sixfold fruit of the limbs [of plot]. ||6.117||
Just as a person lacking limbs is not capable of undertaking [any task],

children.text: aṅga-hīnaṃ tathā kāvyaṃ na prayogāya yujyate // VisSd_6.118 //
children.translated_text: so too a poem lacking limbs is not suitable for dramatic performance. ||6.118||
The <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) and <s>pratināyaka</s> (antagonist) should accomplish the elements of the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture);
in their absence, the <s>patākā</s> characters and others; in their absence, yet others. ||6.119||
The arrangement of these limbs should be made with regard to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>,
not merely out of a desire to conform to the prescriptions of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise). ||6.120||
Even an episode that is not contradictory but conducive to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> and the like,

children.text: tad apy anyathayed dhīmān vaded vā kadācana // VisSd_6.121 //
children.translated_text: the wise [poet] may alter or sometimes omit. ||6.121||

children.text: śṛṅgāre kauśikī vīre sāttvaty ārabhaṭī punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) rasa, [the style is] <s>kauśikī</s>; in the <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>sātvatī</s>; and <s>ārabhaṭī</s>

children.text: rase raudre ca bībhatse vṛttiḥ sarvatra bhāratī // VisSd_6.122 //
children.translated_text: in the <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) rasas; the <s>bhāratī</s> style [is used] everywhere. ||6.122||

children.text: catasro vṛttayo hy etāḥ sarva-nāṭyasya mātṛkāḥ /
children.translated_text: These four <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) are the mothers of all dramatic art.
They are the particular activities of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) and others in <s>nāṭaka</s> and similar [dramatic forms]. ||6.123||
That [style] which is distinguished by refined costumes and varied [accessories], filled with women, abounding in dance and song,
endowed with the pleasures of love-enjoyment, and possessing charming playfulness — that is <s>kauśikī</s>. ||6.124||

children.text: narma ca narma-sphūrjo narma-sphoṭo 'tha narma-garbhaś ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Narma</s> (jest), <s>narma-sphūrja</s> (flash of jest), <s>narma-sphoṭa</s> (burst of jest), and <s>narma-garbha</s> (jest-concealing) —

children.text: catvāry aṅgāny asyā vaidagdhya-krīḍitaṃ narma // VisSd_6.125 //
children.translated_text: these are its four limbs; witty play is <s>narma</s>. ||6.125||
It serves to win over a beloved person, and is considered to be of three kinds:
composed of pure humor, and [also] mixed with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment). ||6.126||
<s>Narma-sphūrja</s> is a new union that begins with happiness and ends with fear.
<s>Narma-sphoṭa</s> is considered that in which a slight <s>rasa</s> is suggested through traces of <s>bhāva</s>. ||6.127||
<s>Narma-garbha</s> is the activity of the hero who acts in concealment.
The <s>sātvatī</s> [style] abounds in <s>sattva</s> (goodness), valor, generosity, compassion, and uprightness. ||6.128||
It has joy, minor erotic [elements], is free from sorrow, and possesses wonder.
<s>Utthāpaka</s> (instigation), <s>sāṅghātya</s> (confederacy-breaking), <s>saṃlāpa</s> (profound dialogue), and <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal) — ||6.129||
these four are declared as the varieties of <s>sātvatī</s>.
<s>Utthāpaka</s> is said to be verbal incitement of the enemy. ||6.130||
<s>Sāṅghātya</s> is the breaking of an alliance through strategy, destiny, supernatural power, and the like.
<s>Saṃlāpa</s> is profound speech that takes recourse to various <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions). ||6.131||
<s>Parivartaka</s> is the undertaking of tasks other than the one commenced.
Through magic, illusion, battle, fury, bewilderment, and similar actions, ||6.132||
combined with killing, imprisonment, and the like — the violent [style] is considered <s>ārabhaṭī</s>.
<s>Vastūtthāpana</s> (raising of a theme), <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (clash), <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (compression), and <s>avapātana</s> (catastrophe) — ||6.133||

children.text: iti bhedās tu catvāra ārabhaṭyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: these four are declared as the varieties of <s>ārabhaṭī</s>.
<s>Vastūtthāpana</s> is said to be the raising of a theme through magic and the like. ||6.134||
<s>Saṃpheṭa</s> is the clash between two who are angry and hasty.

children.text: saṅkṣiptā vastu-racanā śilpair itarathāpi vā // VisSd_6.135 //
children.translated_text: Compression of the plot through devices or otherwise ||6.135||

children.text: saṅkṣiptiḥ sthān nivṛttau ca netur netrantara-grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: is <s>saṃkṣipti</s>; and upon cessation, the hero's taking up of another [role].
Born of entry, fright, exit, joy, or flight — ||6.136||

children.text: avapātanam ity uktaṃ pūrvam uktaiva bhāratī /
children.translated_text: [that] is called <s>avapātana</s> (catastrophe). The <s>bhāratī</s> [style] has already been described.

children.text: aśrāvyaṃ khalu yad vastu tad iha svagataṃ matam // VisSd_6.137 //
children.translated_text: That subject matter which should not be heard [on stage] is considered <s>svagata</s> (aside). ||6.137||

children.text: sarva-śrāvyaṃ prakāśaṃ syāt tad bhaved apavāritam /
children.translated_text: What may be heard by all is <s>prakāśa</s> (public); that becomes <s>apavārita</s> (screened)

children.text: rahasyaṃ tu yad anyasya parāvṛtya prakāśyate // VisSd_6.138 //
children.translated_text: when something secret is revealed to another by turning aside. ||6.138||
Screening off others with a <s>tripatāka</s> hand [gesture], a conversation

children.text: anyonyāmantraṇaṃ yat syāt taj-janānte janāntikam // VisSd_6.139 //
children.translated_text: addressed to one another within the dialogue — that is <s>janāntika</s> (confidential aside). ||6.139||

children.text: kiṃ bravīṣīti yan-nāṭye vinā pātraṃ prayujyate /
children.translated_text: 'What do you say?' — when in drama [something] is enacted without a [visible] character,

children.text: śrutvevānuktam apy arthaṃ tat syād ākāśa-bhāṣitam // VisSd_6.140 //
children.translated_text: as if hearing an unspoken meaning — that is called <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech to the sky). ||6.140||

children.text: dattāṃ siddhāṃ ca senāṃ ca veśyānāṃ nāma darśayet /
children.translated_text: One should show the names of given and accomplished armies, and of courtesans;

children.text: datta-prāyāṇi vaṇijāṃ ceṭa-ceṭyos tathā punaḥ // VisSd_6.141 //
children.translated_text: also mostly the given [names] of merchants, and of male and female servants. ||6.141||

children.text: vasantādiṣu varṇyasya vastuno nāma yad bhavet /
children.translated_text: Whatever name belongs to the subject being described in [acts named after] spring and the like,
that should be made the name of the <s>nāṭaka</s>, revealing the hidden meaning. ||6.142||
In <s>prakaraṇa</s> and similar [forms], the title [comes] from the names of the heroine and hero.
In <s>nāṭikā</s>, <s>saṭṭaka</s>, and the like, the distinguishing [is done] by the heroines. ||6.143||

children.text: prāyeṇa ṇy-antakaḥ sādhir gameḥ sthāne prayujyate /
children.translated_text: Generally, a <s>ṇy</s>-ending derivative of the root <s>gam</s> is used for 'place.'

children.text: rājā svāmīti deveti bhṛtyair bhaṭṭeti cādhamaiḥ // VisSd_6.144 //
children.translated_text: By servants [the king is addressed as] 'lord' or 'master' or 'sire'; by lowly ones, '<s>bhaṭṭa</s>.' ||6.144||
By royal sages [he is called] 'friend,' and by the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) likewise.

children.text: rājann ity ṛṣibhir vācyaḥ so 'patya-pratyayena ca // VisSd_6.145 //
children.translated_text: By sages [he is addressed] 'O king'; he may also [be addressed] with a patronymic. ||6.145||

children.text: svecchayā nāmabhir viprair vipra āryeti cetaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [is addressed] by name at will by other <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and '<s>ārya</s>' (noble sir) by others.

children.text: vayasyety athavā nāmnā vācyo rājñā vidūṣakaḥ // VisSd_6.146 //
children.translated_text: The <s>vidūṣaka</s> is to be addressed by the king as 'friend' or by name. ||6.146||
The <s>naṭī</s> (actress) and <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager) address each other as '<s>ārya</s>' or by name.

children.text: sūtradhāraṃ vaded bhāva iti vai pāripārśvikaḥ // VisSd_6.147 //
children.translated_text: The <s>pāripārśvika</s> (attendant) should address the <s>sūtradhāra</s> as '<s>bhāva</s>' (sir). ||6.147||

children.text: sūtradhāro māriṣeti haṇḍe ity adhamaiḥ samāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> [addresses] equals [as] '<s>māriṣa</s>' (good sir); inferiors [as] '<s>haṇḍe</s>' (hey!).

children.text: vayasyety uttamair haṃho madhyair āryeti cāgrajaḥ // VisSd_6.148 //
children.translated_text: By superiors [the elder brother is addressed] 'friend'; by middling ones, '<s>haṃho</s>'; by [all], '<s>ārya</s>' [for] the elder. ||6.148||
Sages and ascetics should be addressed by all as '<s>bhagavan</s>' (venerable one).

children.text: vaded rājñīṃ ca ceṭīṃ ca bhavatīti vidūṣakaḥ // VisSd_6.149 //
children.translated_text: The <s>vidūṣaka</s> should address the queen and the maidservant as '<s>bhavatī</s>' (madam). ||6.149||

children.text: āyuṣman rathinaṃ sūto vṛddhaṃ tāteti cetaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The charioteer [addresses] the chariot-warrior [as] '<s>āyuṣman</s>' (long-lived one); an elder [as] 'father,' and others likewise.

children.text: vatsa-putraka-tāteti nāmnā gotreṇa vā sutaḥ // VisSd_6.150 //
children.translated_text: A son [is addressed as] '<s>vatsa</s>' (child), '<s>putraka</s>' (dear son), 'father,' or by name or family name. ||6.150||
A pupil and a younger [sibling] should also be so addressed; a minister [is called] '<s>ārya</s>' (noble) by inferiors,

children.text: viprair ayam amātyeti saciveti ca bhaṇyate // VisSd_6.151 //
children.translated_text: and 'this minister' by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and '<s>saciva</s>' (counselor) [by others]. ||6.151||

children.text: sādho iti tapasvī ca praśāntaś cocyate budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: An ascetic [is addressed] '<s>sādho</s>' (good one) and a tranquil person [likewise] by the wise.
A venerable person is addressed by pupils and others with his adopted title. ||6.152||
A teacher [is addressed] '<s>upādhyāya</s>' or '<s>ācārya</s>'; a king, '<s>mahārāja</s>';

children.text: svāmīti yuvarājas tu kumāro bhartṛ-dārakaḥ // VisSd_6.153 //
children.translated_text: a crown prince, '<s>svāmī</s>' (lord); a master's son, '<s>kumāra</s>' (prince). ||6.153||
'<s>Bhadra</s>' (good), '<s>saumya</s>-mukha' (gentle-faced), and such [terms are used] by inferiors; and [he is] '<s>kumāraka</s>' (young prince).

children.text: vācyā prakṛtibhī rājñaḥ kumārī bhartṛ-dārikā // VisSd_6.154 //
children.translated_text: The king's daughter, the master's daughter, should be addressed by subordinates [appropriately]. ||6.154||

children.text: patir yathā tathā vācyā jyeṣṭha-madhyādhamaiḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Women should be addressed by superiors, middling, and inferiors just as [they address] the husband.

children.text: haleti sadṛśī preṣyā hajje veśyājjukā tathā // VisSd_6.155 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Hala</s>!' [is used for] an equal servant; '<s>hajje</s>!' for a courtesan and actress. ||6.155||

children.text: kuṭṭiny ambety anugatiḥ pūjyā ca jaratī janaiḥ /
children.translated_text: A procuress [is addressed] '<s>amba</s>' (mother); a follower and an elder woman [are called reverently] by people.

children.text: āmantraṇaiś ca pāṣāṇḍā vācyāḥ svasamayāgataiḥ // VisSd_6.156 //
children.translated_text: Heretics should be addressed with the salutations proper to their own doctrines. ||6.156||
Buddhists and others should be addressed with names like '<s>Bhadra-datta</s>' and the like.

children.text: yasya yat karma śilpaṃ vā vidyā vā jātir eva vā // VisSd_6.157 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is one's occupation, craft, ||6.157||

children.text: tenaiva nāmnā vācyo 'sau jñeyāś cānye yathocitam /
children.translated_text: learning, or caste — by that very name should one be addressed; and others should be known as appropriate.

children.text: puruṣāṇām anīcānāṃ saṃskṛtaṃ syāt kṛtātmanām // VisSd_6.158 //
children.translated_text: For men of respectable classes who are cultured, Sanskrit should be employed; ||6.158||
<s>Śaurasenī</s> [Prakrit] should be used for women of such [classes].

children.text: āsām eva tu gāthāsu mahārāṣṭrīṃ prayojayet // VisSd_6.159 //
children.translated_text: For their songs, one should employ <s>Mahārāṣṭrī</s> [Prakrit]. ||6.159||
The <s>Māgadhī</s> language is prescribed here for those who move in the king's inner quarters.
<s>Ardha-Māgadhī</s> [is used] for servants, princes, and merchants. ||6.160||
<s>Prācyā</s> (Eastern) [is used] for the <s>vidūṣaka</s> and others; <s>Āvantijā</s> for rogues;
<s>Dākṣiṇātyā</s> (Southern) for warriors, townsfolk, and gamblers. ||6.161||
For <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, and the like, one should employ <s>Śābarī</s>;
<s>Drāviḍī</s> for <s>Drāviḍas</s> and others; [the same] for people of Bāhlīka and the northern regions. ||6.162||
<s>Ābhīrī</s> for <s>Ābhīras</s>; <s>Cāṇḍālī</s> for <s>Pukkasas</s> and the like;
also <s>Ābhīrī</s> and <s>Śābarī</s> for those who live by [selling] wooden vessels. ||6.163||
Likewise for charcoal-makers and the like; <s>Paiśācī</s> is the speech of <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls).

children.text: ceṭānām apy anīcānām api syāt saurasenikā // VisSd_6.164 //
children.translated_text: Even for lowly servants, <s>Śaurasenī</s> may be used. ||6.164||
For children, eunuchs, those possessed by lowly spirits,

children.text: unmattānām āturāṇāṃ saiva syāt saṃskṛtaṃ kvacit // VisSd_6.165 //
children.translated_text: the insane, and the afflicted — the same [Śaurasenī applies]; sometimes Sanskrit. ||6.165||
For one intoxicated with power, one afflicted by poverty,
and for mendicants, bark-wearers, and the like — Prakrit should be employed. ||6.166||
Sanskrit should be employed for female ascetics and noble women,
and by some it is also prescribed for queens, ministers' daughters, courtesans, and the like. ||6.167||
When the occasion demands, a reversal of language for superiors and others [may be made]. ||6.168||
For women's female friends, young courtesans, gamblers, and <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs),
Sanskrit should be given intermittently for the sake of displaying their wit. ||6.169||
Here [in drama there are] thirty-six distinguishing marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and likewise dramatic ornaments (<s>nāṭyālaṅkṛti</s>);
thirty-three [of these] are to be employed; thirteen are limbs of <s>vīthī</s> (one-act play); ||6.170||
ten are limbs of <s>lāsya</s> (feminine dance-drama), [to be used] as occasion arises, with regard to <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment), <s>akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination), <s>śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), ||6.171||
<s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>tulya-tarka</s> (analogical reasoning), <s>padoccaya</s> (word-accumulation),

children.text: nidarśanābhiprāyo ca prāptir vicāra eva ca // VisSd_6.172 //
children.translated_text: <s>nidarśana</s> (demonstration), <s>abhiprāya</s> (intent), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), and <s>vicāra</s> (deliberation); ||6.172||
<s>diṣṭa</s> (description) and <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction); <s>guṇātipāta</s> (transgression of virtue) and <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence);
<s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (specification) and <s>nirukti</s> (etymological explanation); <s>siddhi</s> (success), <s>bhraṃśa</s> (downfall), and <s>viparyaya</s> (reversal); ||6.173||
<s>dākṣiṇya</s> (courtesy) and <s>anunaya</s> (conciliation); <s>mālā</s> (garland), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), and <s>garhaṇa</s> (reproach);

children.text: pṛcchā prasiddhiḥ sārūpyaṃ saṃkṣepo guṇa-kīrtanam // VisSd_6.174 //
children.translated_text: <s>pṛcchā</s> (inquiry), <s>prasiddhi</s> (well-known fact), <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance), <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness), and <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of virtues); ||6.174||
<s>leśa</s> (hint), <s>manoratha</s> (heart's desire), <s>anukta-siddhi</s> (unspoken accomplishment), and <s>priya-vacas</s> (pleasant speech).

children.text: lakṣaṇāni guṇaiḥ sālaṅkārair yogas tu bhūṣaṇam // VisSd_6.175 //
children.translated_text: These are the distinguishing marks; their combination with <s>guṇas</s> (poetic qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) is <s>bhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment). ||6.175||
<s>Akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination) is the description with measured syllables of pictorial meaning;

children.text: siddhair arthaiḥ samaṃ yatrāprasiddho 'rthaḥ prakāśate // VisSd_6.176 //
children.translated_text: where, along with established meanings, an unusual meaning is revealed — ||6.176||
with closely joined distinguishing marks and pictorial meanings — that is called <s>śobhā</s> (splendor).
Where, through demonstration by means of a statement having an equivalent meaning, ||6.177||
the intended meaning is established — that is considered <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration).

children.text: hetur vākyaṃ samāsoktam iṣṭakṛd dhetu-darśanāt // VisSd_6.178 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hetu</s> (reason) is a statement made concisely that accomplishes the desired [end] through showing the cause. ||6.178||
<s>Saṃśaya</s> (doubt) is the uncertainty in a statement regarding a thing whose true nature is unknown.

children.text: dṛṣṭānto yas tu pakṣe 'rtha-sādhanāya nidarśanam // VisSd_6.179 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is a demonstration for establishing the meaning of a proposition. ||6.179||
<s>Tulya-tarka</s> (analogical reasoning) is reasoning by means of a meaning that follows from the nature [of the subject].

children.text: sañcayo 'rthānurūpo yaḥ padānāṃ sa padoccayaḥ // VisSd_6.180 //
children.translated_text: An accumulation of words conforming to the meaning is <s>padoccaya</s> (word-accumulation). ||6.180||
Where well-known facts are proclaimed
for the purpose of refuting the opponent's position — that is called <s>nidarśana</s> (demonstration). ||6.181||
<s>Abhiprāya</s> (intent) is the fabrication of an unreal thing on the basis of resemblance.

children.text: prāptiḥ kenacid aṃśena kiñcid yatrānumīyate // VisSd_6.182 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāpti</s> (attainment) is where something is inferred by some partial [evidence]. ||6.182||
<s>Vicāra</s> (deliberation) is the revelation of a non-evident meaning through statements of reasoning.
Description by means of place, time, and intrinsic nature is called <s>diṣṭa</s>. ||6.183||
<s>Upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction) is a pleasing statement made in accordance with <s>śāstra</s> (treatise).

children.text: guṇātipātaḥ kāryaṃ vad viparītaṃ guṇān prati // VisSd_6.184 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guṇātipāta</s> (transgression of virtue) is speaking what ought to be done in a manner contrary to the virtues. ||6.184||

children.text: yaḥ sāmān guṇodrekaḥ sa guṇātiśayo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: A superiority of virtues over those of equals — that is considered <s>guṇātiśaya</s> (excellence of virtue).

children.text: siddhān arthān bahūn uktvā viśeṣoktir viśeṣaṇam // VisSd_6.185 //
children.translated_text: Having stated many established facts, the specific statement is <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (specification). ||6.185||
The stating of a previously established meaning is called <s>nirukti</s> (etymological explanation).
The enumeration of many [things] is <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) — for the attainment of the intended purpose.

children.text: dṛptādīnāṃ bhavad bhraṃśo vācyād anyatarad vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fall of the arrogant and the like — speech that is different from the stated [meaning] — <s>viparyaya</s> (reversal) is the otherwise-ness of deliberation, from doubt.
is <s>viparyaya</s> (reversal), arising from doubt.
<s>Dākṣiṇya</s> (courtesy) is the conforming to another's mind through gesture and speech.

children.text: vākyaiḥ snigdhair anunayo bhaved arthasya sādhanam // VisSd_6.188 //
children.translated_text: <s>Anunaya</s> (conciliation) is the accomplishment of a purpose through gentle words.
<s>Mālā</s> (garland) is the presentation of more than one meaning for a desired purpose.
<s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is when another meaning is understood from the statement of a different meaning.

children.text: dūṣaṇodghoṣaṇāyāṃ tu bhartsanā garhaṇaṃ tu tat /
children.translated_text: <s>Garhaṇa</s> (censure) is the proclamation of faults — that is <s>bhartsanā</s> (reproach).
<s>Pṛcchā</s> (inquiry) is regarded as the investigation of a matter through beseeching words.
<s>Prasiddhi</s> (establishment) is the accomplishment of a purpose through well-known and exalted matters.
<s>Sārūpya</s> (resemblance) is the increase of agitation through the resemblance of something similar.

children.text: saṅkṣepo yat tu saṅkṣepād ātmāny arthe prayujyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṅkṣepa</s> (condensation) is that which is briefly applied to one's own purpose.

children.text: guṇānāṃ kīrtanaṃ yat tu tad eva guṇa-kīrtanam // VisSd_6.192 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guṇakīrtana</s> (praise of virtues) is indeed the enumeration of virtues.

children.text: sa leśo bhaṇyate vākyaṃ yat sādṛśya-puraḥsaram /
children.translated_text: That speech which is preceded by comparison is called <s>leśa</s> (trace).

children.text: manorathas tv abhiprāyasyoktir bhaṅgyantareṇa yat // VisSd_6.193 //
children.translated_text: <s>Manoratha</s> (heart's desire) is the expression of one's intention by an indirect means.
The elaboration of a special meaning in an implicative manner is called <s>anuktasiddhi</s> (establishment of the unstated).

children.text: syāt prayāṇayituṃ pūjyaṃ priyoktir harṣa-bhāṣaṇam // VisSd_6.194 //
children.translated_text: <s>Priyokti</s> (pleasant speech) is joyful speech intended to gratify one who is venerable.
<s>Āśīḥ</s> (benediction), <s>ākranda</s> (lamentation), <s>kapaṭa</s> (deception), <s>akṣamā</s> (intolerance), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>udyama</s> (endeavor), <s>āśraya</s> (recourse),
<s>utprāsana</s> (mockery), <s>spṛhā</s> (longing), <s>kṣobha</s> (agitation), <s>paścāttāpa</s> (remorse), <s>upapatti</s> (reasoning) —
<s>āśaṃsā</s> (hope) and <s>adhyavasāya</s> (resolve) are called <s>visarpa</s> (spreading) and <s>ullekha</s> (delineation).
<s>Uttejana</s> (provocation), <s>parīvāda</s> (reproach), <s>nīti</s> (policy), <s>arthaviśeṣaṇa</s> (specification of meaning),
<s>protsāhana</s> (encouragement), <s>sāhāyya</s> (assistance), <s>abhimāna</s> (self-regard), <s>anuvartana</s> (compliance),

children.text: utkīrtanaṃ yathā yācñā parihāro nivedanam // VisSd_6.197 //
children.translated_text: <s>utkīrtana</s> (recounting), <s>yācñā</s> (entreaty), <s>parihāra</s> (expiation), <s>nivedana</s> (submission),
<s>pravartana</s> (instigation), <s>ākhyāna</s> (narration), <s>yukti</s> (reasoning), <s>praharṣa</s> (delight), and <s>upadeśana</s> (instruction) —
these are the <s>nāṭyālaṅkṛtis</s> (dramatic ornaments), the causes of embellishment in drama.
<s>Āśīḥ</s> (benediction) is the expression of good wishes for a beloved person. <s>Ākranda</s> (lamentation) is lamenting in grief.

children.text: kapaṭaṃ māyayā yatra rūpam anyad vibhāvyate // VisSd_6.199 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kapaṭa</s> (deception) is where, through illusion, a different appearance is made manifest.

children.text: akṣamā sā paribhavaḥ svalpo 'pi na viṣahyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣamā</s> (intolerance) is that in which even a small insult is not tolerated.
Speech born of pride and arrogance is <s>garva</s> (pride). <s>Udyama</s> (endeavor) is the commencement of an undertaking.
The meritorious grasping of the cause of an action is called <s>āśraya</s> (recourse).
<s>Utprāsana</s> (mockery) is ridicule directed at a wicked person who considers himself good.

children.text: ākāṅkṣā ramaṇīyatvāḍ vastuno yā spṛhā tu sā /
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛhā</s> (longing) is the desire for an object because of its attractiveness.

children.text: adhikṣepa-vacaḥ-kārī kṣobhaḥ proktaḥ sa eva tu // VisSd_6.202 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣobha</s> (agitation) is that very [state] which produces words of reproach.
<s>Paścāttāpa</s> (remorse) is that very [feeling] regarding a matter disregarded through delusion.
<s>Upapatti</s> (reasoning) is regarded as the presentation of a reason for the establishment of a purpose.
<s>Āśaṃsā</s> (hope) is expectation; <s>adhyavasāya</s> (resolve) is a firm vow.
<s>Visarpa</s> (spreading) is an undertaking that produces an undesired result.
<s>Ullekha</s> (delineation) is the grasping of the task; <s>uttejana</s> (provocation) —
is harsh speech for inciting another, for the accomplishment of one's own purpose.

children.text: bhartsanā tu parīvādo nītiḥ śāstreṇa vartanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Parīvāda</s> (reproach) is the same as <s>bhartsanā</s> (censure). <s>Nīti</s> (policy) is conduct according to the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises).

children.text: uktasyārthasya yat tu syād utkīrtanam anekadhā // VisSd_6.206 //
children.translated_text: <s>Utkīrtana</s> (recounting) is the manifold [repetition] of what has been stated.
<s>Arthaviśeṣaṇa</s> (specification of meaning) is [effected] through a particular kind of reproach.

children.text: protsāhnaṃ syād utsāha-girā kasyāpi yojanam // VisSd_6.207 //
children.translated_text: <s>Protsāhana</s> (encouragement) is the joining of someone with words of enthusiasm.

children.text: sāhāyyaṃ saṅkaṭe yat syāt sānukūlyaṃ parasya ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Sāhāyya</s> (assistance) is favorable [action] toward another in distress.

children.text: abhimānaḥ sa eva syāt praśrayād anuvartanam // VisSd_6.208 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhimāna</s> (self-regard) is that same [state]; <s>anuvartana</s> (compliance) is following out of deference.
<s>Anuvṛtti</s> (compliance) is [also called] <s>utkīrtana</s> (recounting), regarded as the narration of past events.

children.text: yācñā tu kvāpi yācñā yā svayaṃ dūta-mukhena vā // VisSd_6.209 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yācñā</s> (entreaty) is whatever entreaty [is made], whether by oneself or through a messenger.
<s>Parihāra</s> (expiation) is called the cleansing of what has been improperly done.
<s>Nivedana</s> (submission) is the declaration of what ought to be done [but was] disregarded.

children.text: pravartanaṃ tu kāryasya yat syāt sādhu-pravartanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pravartana</s> (instigation) is the proper initiation of an undertaking.
<s>Ākhyāna</s> (narration) is the statement of past events. <s>Yukti</s> (reasoning) is the determination of a matter.
<s>Praharṣa</s> (delight) is an excess of joy. <s>Upadeśana</s> (instruction) is teaching.
<s>Geya-pada</s> (sung verse), <s>sthita-pāṭhya</s> (standing recitation), <s>āsīna</s> (seated [performance]), <s>puṣpa-gaṇḍikā</s> (flower-game),
<s>pracchedaka</s> (severance-song), <s>trigūḍha</s> (thrice-concealed), <s>saindhava</s> (the Sindhi), <s>dvigūḍha</s> (twice-concealed),
<s>uttamottamaka</s> (the most excellent), and <s>ukta-pratyukta</s> (dialogue) —

children.text: lāsye daśavidhaṃ hy etad-aṅgam uktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: these are declared by the wise as the tenfold limbs of <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance-drama).
When one sits before [the audience], with a stringed instrument placed before [them],

children.text: śuddhaṃ gānaṃ geya-padaṃ sthita-pāṭhyaṃ tad ucyate /
children.translated_text: pure singing is <s>geya-pada</s> (sung verse). <s>Sthita-pāṭhya</s> (standing recitation) is said to be

children.text: madanottāpitā yatra paṭhati prākṛtaṃ sthitā // VisSd_6.215 //
children.translated_text: when a woman tormented by love recites <s>Prākṛta</s> (vernacular verse) while standing.
A young woman afflicted with grief and anxiety, completely devoid of musical instruments,

children.text: aprasādhita-gātraṃ yad āsīnāsīnam eva tat // VisSd_6.216 //
children.translated_text: with body unadorned — that which is [performed] while seated is <s>āsīna</s> (seated [performance]).
Singing mixed with instrumental music, various meters,
and the playful reversal of male and female roles is <s>puṣpa-gaṇḍikā</s> (flower-game).
Considering her husband to be attached to another woman, with the anger born of love's breach,

children.text: vīṇā-puraḥ-saraṃ gānaṃ striyāḥ pracchedako mataḥ // VisSd_6.218 //
children.translated_text: a woman's singing preceded by the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) is regarded as <s>pracchedaka</s> (severance-song).
<s>Trigūḍhaka</s> (thrice-concealed) is the delicate dramatic performance of men wearing women's dress.
Someone who has missed his rendezvous, endowed with clearly performed actions,

children.text: prākṛtaṃ vacanaṃ vakti yatra tat saindhavaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: speaks words in <s>Prākṛta</s> (vernacular) — that is regarded as <s>saindhava</s> (the Sindhi).
<s>Dvigūḍha</s> (twice-concealed) is a song with well-formed verses, possessing the <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>pratimukha</s> (counter-opening) [elements],
rich in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and <s>bhāva</s> (emotional states). <s>Uttamottamaka</s> (the most excellent)
is born of anger and appeasement, containing reproach, and excelling in <s>rasa</s>,
endowed with <s>hāva</s> (flirtation) and <s>helā</s> (playfulness), with captivating arrangement of varied verses.
<s>Ukta-pratyukta</s> (dialogue) is that which contains speech and counter-speech, with reproach, as if false,
with the meaning of song accompanied by <s>vilāsa</s> (charm) — this is called <s>ukta-pratyukta</s> (dialogue).

children.text: etad eva yadā sarvaiḥ patākā-sthānakair yutam // VisSd_6.223 //
children.translated_text: When this very [form] is endowed with all the <s>patākā-sthānakas</s> (banner-positions)

children.text: aṅkaiś ca daśabhir dhīrā mahānāṭakam ūcire /
children.translated_text: and with ten acts — the learned call it <s>mahānāṭaka</s> (great drama).

children.text: bhavet prakaraṇe vṛttaṃ laukikaṃ kavi-kalpitam // VisSd_6.224 //
children.translated_text: In a <s>prakaraṇa</s> (social drama), the plot is worldly, devised by the poet;
<s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) is the principal <s>rasa</s>; the hero is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a minister, or a merchant,
who is devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>artha</s> (wealth), along with their attendant dangers — of the <s>dhīra-praśānta</s> (steadfast and tranquil) type.

children.text: nāyikā kulajā kvāpi veśyā kvāpi dvayaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: The heroine is sometimes a woman of good family, sometimes a courtesan, and sometimes both;

children.text: tena bhedās trayas tasya tatra bhedas tṛtīyakaḥ // VisSd_6.226 //
children.translated_text: hence its three varieties; and the third type [where both appear] has [further] divisions.
The <s>bhāṇa</s> (monologue) is replete with gamblers, gaming, rogue companions, and servants;
it is the account of a rascal, consisting of various situations.

children.text: ekāṅka eka evātra nipuṇaḥ paṇḍito viṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: It has a single act; there is only one [character] here — a clever, learned rogue,

children.text: raṅge prakāśayet svenānubhūtam itareṇa vā // VisSd_6.228 //
children.translated_text: who displays on the stage what is experienced by himself or by another.
He makes address, speech, and reply through <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech directed at an unseen interlocutor).
He should suggest the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiments through descriptions of valor and good fortune.
The plot therein is invented; the style (<s>vṛtti</s>) is predominantly <s>bhāratī</s> (verbal).

children.text: mukha-nirvahaṇe sandhī lāsyāṅgāni daśāpi ca // VisSd_6.230 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) are <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion); and also the ten <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (components of lāsya).
The <s>vyāyoga</s> (military drama) has a well-known plot, with few female characters,

children.text: hīno garbha-vimarśābhyāṃ narair bahubhir āśritaḥ // VisSd_6.231 //
children.translated_text: lacking <s>garbha</s> (embryo) and <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation) [junctures], having many male characters,
a single act, and a celestial being alone should be the hero here — though others say not so.
It is devoid of the <s>kaiśikī-vṛtti</s> (graceful style); the hero therein is renowned,

children.text: rājarṣir atha divyo vā bhaved dhīroddhataś ca saḥ /
