children.translated_text: being either a royal sage or a divine being; he should be of the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast and haughty) type.
The principal <s>rasas</s> therein are those other than <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), and <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil).
In the <s>samavakāra</s> (mixed drama), the plot is well-known, based on gods and demons.

children.text: sandhayo nirvimarśās tu trayo 'ṅkās tatra cādime // VisSd_6.234 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) are without <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation); there are three acts, and in the first [acts],

children.text: sandhī dvāv antyayos tadvad eka eko bhavet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: two <s>sandhis</s> in the last [acts], and one each in the others.
The heroes are twelve, exalted, well-known gods and men.

children.text: phalaṃ pṛthak pṛthak teṣāṃ vīra-mukhyo 'khilo rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruits are different for each of them; <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) is the principal <s>rasa</s>, and all [other] <s>rasas</s> [appear].
The styles (<s>vṛttis</s>) are <s>kaiśikī</s> (graceful) sparingly; there are no <s>bindu</s> (drop-scene) or <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene) here.

children.text: vīthy-aṅgāni ca tatra syur yathālābhaṃ trayodaśa /
children.translated_text: The <s>vīthyaṅgas</s> (components of the vīthī) therein should be thirteen, as available.

children.text: gāyatry-uṣṇiṅ-mukhāny atra cchandāṃsi vividhāni ca // VisSd_6.237 //
children.translated_text: The meters therein include <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Uṣṇik</s>, and various others.
It should have three types of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), three types of <s>kapaṭa</s> (deception), and three types of sound.
The plot of the first act is to be accomplished through twelve <s>nāḍīs</s> (tubes/channels [of time]),
in the second act through four, and in the third act through two.

children.text: dharmārtha-kāmais trividhaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ kapaṭaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_6.239 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) is threefold through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire). <s>Kapaṭa</s> (deception) again

children.text: svābhāvikaḥ kṛtrimaś ca daivajo vidravaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: is natural, artificial, and divinely caused. <s>Vidrava</s> (panic) again

children.text: acetanaiś cetanaiś ca cetanācetanaiḥ kṛtaḥ // VisSd_6.240 //
children.translated_text: is caused by inanimate [things], animate [beings], and by both animate and inanimate [combined].
Through <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>indrajāla</s> (magic), battle, and actions of fury and bewilderment,

children.text: aparāgaiś ca bhūyiṣṭho ḍimaḥ khyātetivṛttakaḥ // VisSd_6.241 //
children.translated_text: and with much <s>aparāga</s> (disaffection) — the <s>ḍima</s> (spectacle drama) has a well-known plot.

children.text: aṅgī raudra-rasas tatra sarve 'ṅgāni rasāḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The principal <s>rasa</s> therein is <s>raudra</s> (the furious); all other <s>rasas</s> are subordinate.
Four acts are held; there are no <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude) or <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene) here.
The heroes are gods, <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature-spirits), <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents),
<s>bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>pretas</s> (spirits), <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), and the like — sixteen, all extremely haughty.
The styles (<s>vṛttis</s>) are devoid of <s>kaiśikī</s> (graceful); the <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) are without <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation).
The <s>rasas</s> should be <s>dīpta</s> (blazing) — the six [rasas] excluding <s>śānta</s> (tranquil), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic).
The <s>īhāmṛga</s> (hunt-drama) is of mixed style (<s>vṛtti</s>) and has four acts.

children.text: mukha-pratimukhe sandhī tatra nirvahaṇaṃ tathā // VisSd_6.245 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) therein are <s>mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (counter-opening), and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion).
The hero and antagonist are [respectively] a celestial-earthly pair;

children.text: khyātau dhīroddhatāv anyo gūḍha-bhāvād ayukta-kṛt // VisSd_6.246 //
children.translated_text: both are well-known, of the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast and haughty) type; the other [antagonist], acting improperly due to concealed motives,
is a celestial being who carries away by night one who does not wish [to go], through abduction and the like.

children.text: śṛṅgārābhāsam apy asya kiñcit kiñcit pradarśayet // VisSd_6.247 //
children.translated_text: Some semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) belonging to him should also be shown, to some slight degree.
The subsidiary heroes are celestial or mortal, ten in number, all haughty.

children.text: yuddham ānīya saṃrambhaṃ paraṃ vyājān nivartate // VisSd_6.248 //
children.translated_text: Having brought about a battle and great fury, [the antagonist] is turned back through a stratagem.

children.text: mahātmāno vadha-prāptā api vadhyāḥ syur atra no /
children.translated_text: Even great souls who deserve death are not to be slain herein.

children.text: ekāṅko deva evātra netety āhuḥ pare punaḥ // VisSd_6.249 //
children.translated_text: There is only one act; the hero should be a god alone — though others say otherwise.
The battle is on account of a celestial woman; the heroes are six — so say others.

children.text: utsṛṣṭikāṅka ekāṅko netāraḥ prākṛtā narāḥ // VisSd_6.250 //
children.translated_text: The <s>utsṛṣṭikāṅka</s> (released-act drama) has a single act; the heroes are ordinary men.
The <s>rasa</s> therein is <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic); the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent sentiment) is much lamentation by women.

children.text: prakhyātam itivṛttaṃ ca kavir buddhyā prapañcayet // VisSd_6.251 //
children.translated_text: The plot is well-known; and the poet should elaborate it with his own imagination.
As in the <s>bhāṇa</s> (monologue), the <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), styles (<s>vṛttis</s>), and limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) [are applied]; victory and defeat [both appear],

children.text: yuddhaṃ ca vācā kartavyaṃ nirveda-vacanaṃ bahu // VisSd_6.252 //
children.translated_text: and battle should be conveyed through words; there is much speech of self-deprecation (<s>nirveda</s>).

children.text: vīthyām eko bhaved aṅkaḥ kaścid eko 'tra kalpyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>vīthī</s> (sketch) has a single act; some one [character] is conceived therein,

children.text: ākāśa-bhāṣitair uktaiś citrāṃ pratyuktim āśritaḥ // VisSd_6.253 //
children.translated_text: who, adopting varied replies through <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech addressed to the unseen),

children.text: sūcayed bhūri śṛṅgāraṃ kiñcid anyān rasān prati /
children.translated_text: should suggest <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) abundantly and the other <s>rasas</s> to some extent.
The <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) are <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion); all the <s>artha-prakṛtis</s> (elements of the plot) [are present].
The wise prescribe thirteen limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) for this [form].
<s>Uddhātyaka</s> (the boisterous), <s>avalagita</s> (the suspended), <s>prapañca</s> (the elaborate), <s>trigata</s> (the triple), <s>chala</s> (the trick),
<s>vākkeli</s> (verbal play), <s>adhibala</s> (the overpowering), <s>gaṇḍa</s> (the knot), <s>avasyandita</s> (the flowing), <s>nālikā</s> (the hollow tube),
<s>asatpralāpa</s> (incoherent talk), <s>vyāhāra</s> (discourse), and <s>mārdava</s> (gentleness) — these are they.

children.text: mitho vākyam asadbhūtaṃ prapañco hāsya-kṛn mataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prapañca</s> (the elaborate) is a mutually false utterance, held to produce laughter.
<s>Trigata</s> (the triple) is the joining of multiple meanings, through the ambiguity of the hearing.
Through apparently pleasing but actually displeasing words, by the deception of enticement — that is <s>chala</s> (the trick).

children.text: anye tvāhuś chalaṃ kiñcit kāryam uddiśya kasyacit // VisSd_6.258 //
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that <s>chala</s> (deception) is a statement uttered with some purpose in mind, directed at someone, ||6.258||
which, being spoken, produces deceit, laughter, or anger.
<s>Vāk-keli</s> (verbal sport) is connected with humor and consists of two or three retorts. ||6.259||
The mutual assertion of superiority in speech through rivalry is considered <s>adhibala</s> (overpowering).

children.text: gaṇḍaṃ prastuta-saṃbandhi bhinnārthaṃ satvaraṃ vacaḥ // VisSd_6.260 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇḍa</s> (impediment) is a hasty speech related to the subject at hand but having a different meaning. ||6.260||
<s>Vyākhyāna</s> (explanation) is something stated spontaneously that is then interpreted otherwise.

children.text: prahelikaiva hāsyena yuktā bhavati nālikā // VisSd_6.261 //
children.translated_text: A <s>prahelikā</s> (riddle) when combined with humor becomes <s>nālikā</s> (tube/jest). ||6.261||
<s>Asat-pralāpa</s> (nonsensical babble) is speech that is incoherent, as well as an [equally incoherent] reply;

children.text: agṛhṇato 'pi mūrkhasya puro yac ca hitaṃ vacaḥ // VisSd_6.262 //
children.translated_text: and also beneficial words spoken in the presence of a fool who does not grasp them. ||6.262||
<s>Vyāhāra</s> (utterance) is speech that causes laughter or agitation regarding another's purpose.

children.text: doṣā guṇā guṇā doṣā yatra syur mṛdavaṃ hi tat // VisSd_6.263 //
children.translated_text: Where faults become virtues and virtues become faults — that is <s>mṛdava</s> (the mild). ||6.263||
Like a <s>bhāṇa</s>, constructed with <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), <s>sandhy-aṅgas</s> (juncture-elements), <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (dance-elements), and acts,

children.text: bhavet prahasanaṃ vṛttaṃ nindyānāṃ kavi-kalpitam // VisSd_6.264 //
children.translated_text: the <s>prahasana</s> (farce) is a composition with a plot invented by the poet concerning despicable characters. ||6.264||
Herein there is no <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (violent style), nor <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (introductory interlude) or <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance scene).

children.text: aṅgī hāsya-rasas tatra vīthy-aṅgānāṃ sthitir na vā // VisSd_6.265 //
children.translated_text: The predominant <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) therein is <s>hāsya</s> (comic); the <s>vīthī</s>-elements may or may not be present. ||6.265||
The hero therein is from among ascetics, venerable ones, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and the like.

children.text: eko yatra bhaved dhṛṣṭo hāsyaṃ tac chuddham ucyate /
children.translated_text: Where there is a single bold [character], that is called 'pure' (<s>śuddha</s>) [farce];

children.text: āśritya kañcana janaṃ saṅkīrṇam iti tad viduḥ // VisSd_6.266 //
children.translated_text: when it relies upon some [low-class] person, that is known as 'mixed' (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>). ||6.266||

children.text: vṛttaṃ bahūnāṃ dhṛṣṭānāṃ saṅkīrṇaṃ kecid ūcire /
children.translated_text: Some say that [a farce] with a plot of many bold characters is 'mixed' (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>);

children.text: tat punar bhavati dvy-aṅgkam athavaikāṅka-nirmitam // VisSd_6.267 //
children.translated_text: it may further be composed of two acts or of a single act. ||6.267||
That in which there are eunuchs, chamberlains, and ascetics is known as 'distorted' (<s>vikṛta</s>),
endowed with the costumes and speech of libertines, <s>cāraṇas</s> (bards), warriors, and the like. ||6.268||
A <s>nāṭikā</s> (short play) has a well-known plot, predominantly features women, and has four acts.

children.text: prakhyāto dhīra-lalitas tatra syān nāyako nṛpaḥ // VisSd_6.269 //
children.translated_text: The hero therein should be a king, noble and gallant (<s>dhīra-lalita</s>), well-known. ||6.269||
It should be connected with the inner apartments [of the palace] or concerned with music.
The heroine therein is a maiden of fresh love, born of a royal family. ||6.270||
The hero should act in it fearful and anxious because of the queen's jealousy.

children.text: devī bhavet punar jyeṣṭhā pragalbhā nṛpa-vaṃśajā // VisSd_6.271 //
children.translated_text: The queen, for her part, should be the senior wife, bold (<s>pragalbhā</s>), born of a royal family. ||6.271||

children.text: pade pade mānavatī tad-vaśaḥ saṅgamo dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: At every step she displays pride (<s>māna</s>); subject to her, the union of the two [occurs].

children.text: vṛttiḥ syāt kaiśikī svalpa-vimarśāḥ sandhayaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_6.272 //
children.translated_text: The style should be <s>kaiśikī</s> (graceful); the junctures (<s>sandhis</s>) should have minimal deliberation (<s>vimarśa</s>). ||6.272||
Having seven, eight, nine, or five acts, relying on divine and human [themes],

children.text: troṭakaṃ nāma tat prāhuḥ pratyaṅkaṃ saṃvidūṣaṇam // VisSd_6.273 //
children.translated_text: that which is called <s>troṭaka</s> has a <s>saṃvidūṣaṇa</s> (plot-corruption) in each act. ||6.273||

children.text: prākṛtair navabhiḥ pumbhir daśabhir vāpy alaṅkṛtā /
children.translated_text: Adorned by nine or even ten Prakrit-speaking male [characters],
having no elevated speech, the <s>goṣṭhī</s> (assembly piece) is endowed with the <s>kaiśikī</s> style. ||6.274||
Lacking <s>garbha</s> (development) and <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation), accompanied by five or six women,
connected with love and the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment, it should be composed as a single act. ||6.275||
The <s>saṭṭaka</s> has its entire recitation in Prakrit; it has no <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance scene),

children.text: na ca viṣkambhako 'py atra pracuraś cādbhuto rasaḥ // VisSd_6.276 //
children.translated_text: nor any <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude) herein; and the <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) <s>rasa</s> is abundant. ||6.276||

children.text: aṅkā javanikākhyāḥ syuḥ syād anyan nāṭikāsamam /
children.translated_text: The acts are called <s>javanikā</s> (curtain[-raisings]); in other respects it is like a <s>nāṭikā</s>.
The <s>nāṭya-rāsaka</s> (dramatic circle-dance) is a single act with abundant rhythm and tempo. ||6.277||
It has a noble hero, and likewise a <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (companion) as sub-hero.

children.text: hāsyo 'ṅgy atra sa-śṛṅgāro nārī vāsaka-sajjikā // VisSd_6.278 //
children.translated_text: The predominant <s>rasa</s> herein is <s>hāsya</s> (comic) with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic); the heroine is one adorned for her lover's arrival (<s>vāsaka-sajjikā</s>). ||6.278||
The junctures are <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion), and there are also the ten <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (dance-elements).

children.text: kecit pratimukhaṃ sandhim iha necchanti kevalam // VisSd_6.279 //
children.translated_text: Some do not admit the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression) juncture herein alone. ||6.279||

children.text: prasthāne nāyako dāso hīnaḥ syād upanāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>prasthāna</s> (departure piece), the hero is a servant; the sub-hero is of lower [rank];

children.text: dāsī ca nāyikā vṛttiḥ kaiśikī bhāratī tathā // VisSd_6.280 //
children.translated_text: and the heroine is a maidservant; the styles are <s>kaiśikī</s> (graceful) and <s>bhāratī</s> (verbal). ||6.280||
The resolution of the stated theme occurs through the occasion of wine-drinking.

children.text: aṅkau dvau laya-tālādir vilāso bahulas tathā // VisSd_6.281 //
children.translated_text: It has two acts; rhythm, tempo, and the like are abundant; likewise, <s>vilāsa</s> (playful grace) is plentiful. ||6.281||
Having a noble hero, a divine plot, adorned with a single act,
endowed with the elements of the <s>śilpaka</s>, with <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) rasas — ||6.282||
the <s>ullāpya</s> (the exclamatory piece) has many battles and is charming with weapons and songs.

children.text: catasro nāyikās tatra trayo 'ṅkā iti kecana // VisSd_6.283 //
children.translated_text: Therein are four heroines and three acts, according to some. ||6.283||
A composition lacking the <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (violent) style, consisting of a single act, filled with <s>hāsya</s> (humor),
adorned with <s>khaṇḍa</s> metres alone, with <s>vipadikā</s> (two-footed) and <s>abhagna</s> (unbroken) rhythms, ||6.284||
consisting of <s>varṇa</s> metres and <s>chaddaṇikā</s> [pieces], with speech characterized by <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) —

children.text: netā strī cāpy udāttātra sandhī ādyau tathāntimaḥ // VisSd_6.285 //
children.translated_text: the hero and heroine herein are noble; the junctures are the first, [the second,] and the last. ||6.285||
The <s>preṅkhaṇa</s> (swing-play) is devoid of <s>garbha</s> (development) and <s>avamarśa</s> (reflection), has a low-born hero,
has no <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager), consists of a single act, and is without <s>viṣkambhaka</s> and <s>praveśaka</s>. ||6.286||
It includes wrestling (<s>niyuddha</s>) and clashing (<s>saṃpheṭa</s>), and relies on all the styles.

children.text: nepathye gīyate nāndī tathā tatra prarocanā // VisSd_6.287 //
children.translated_text: The <s>nāndī</s> (benediction) is sung behind the curtain, and likewise the <s>prarocanā</s> (captivation) therein. ||6.287||
The <s>rāsaka</s> (circle-dance play) has five characters; it has [only] the <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) junctures.
It is predominantly in <s>bhāṣā</s> (standard language) and <s>vibhāṣā</s> (dialects); endowed with the <s>bhāratī</s> and <s>kaiśikī</s> styles. ||6.288||
Having no <s>sūtradhāra</s>, consisting of a single act, with <s>vīthī</s>-elements, and accompanied by artistry (<s>kalā</s>),
having an integrated <s>nāndī</s>, with a well-known heroine or a foolish hero, ||6.289||
relying on noble emotional arrangements and [exchanges of] <s>uttarottara</s> (successive retorts) —

children.text: iha pratimukhaṃ sandhim api kecit pracakṣate // VisSd_6.290 //
children.translated_text: herein some also designate the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression) juncture [as being present]. ||6.290||

children.text: saṃlāpike 'ṅkāś catvāras trayo vā nāyakaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>saṃlāpikā</s> (dialogue piece) there are four or three acts; the hero

children.text: pāṣaṇḍaḥ syād rasas tatra śṛṅgāra-karuṇottaraḥ // VisSd_6.291 //
children.translated_text: should be a heretic (<s>pāṣaṇḍa</s>); the <s>rasa</s> therein is primarily <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic). ||6.291||
There may be siege of a city, stratagem, battle, and rout.

children.text: na tatra vṛttir bhavati bhāratī na ca kaiśikī // VisSd_6.292 //
children.translated_text: There is no <s>bhāratī</s> style therein, nor <s>kaiśikī</s>. ||6.292||
Having a well-known plot, a single act, a well-known noble hero,
a famous heroine, devoid of <s>garbha</s> (development) and <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation), ||6.293||
abundant in the <s>bhāratī</s> (verbal) style, filled with auspicious words (<s>śrīti-śabda</s>) —

children.text: mataṃ śrī-gaditaṃ nāma vidvadbhir uparūpakam // VisSd_6.294 //
children.translated_text: this is considered by the learned to be the minor dramatic form (<s>uparūpaka</s>) called <s>śrī-gadita</s> (auspicious narration). ||6.294||

children.text: śrīr āsīnā śrī-gadite gāyet kiṃcit paṭhed api /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) sits in the <s>śrī-gadita</s>, sings something, and also recites;

children.text: ekāṅko bhāratī-prāya iti kecit pracakṣate // VisSd_6.295 //
children.translated_text: some describe it as a single act predominantly in the <s>bhāratī</s> style. ||6.295||

children.text: catvāraḥ śilpake 'ṅkāḥ syuś catasro vṛttayas tathā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>śilpaka</s> (the artisan-play) there are four acts and four styles;

children.text: aśānta-hāsyāś ca rasā nāyako brāhmaṇo mataḥ // VisSd_6.296 //
children.translated_text: all <s>rasas</s> except <s>śānta</s> (peace) and <s>hāsya</s> (humor) [are present]; the hero is considered to be a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. ||6.296||
There is description of cremation grounds and the like; the sub-hero should be of low rank.

children.text: saptaviṃśatir aṅgāni bhavanty etasya tāni tu // VisSd_6.297 //
children.translated_text: Its elements number twenty-seven; they are: ||6.297||
hope (<s>āśaṃsā</s>), conjecture (<s>tarka</s>), doubt (<s>sandeha</s>), torment (<s>tāpa</s>), agitation (<s>udvega</s>), attachment (<s>prasakti</s>),
effort (<s>prayatna</s>), complication (<s>grathana</s>), longing (<s>utkaṇṭhā</s>), dissimulation (<s>avahitthā</s>), understanding (<s>pratipatti</s>), ||6.298||
grace (<s>vilāsa</s>), languor (<s>ālasya</s>), tears (<s>bāṣpa</s>), delight (<s>praharṣa</s>), relief (<s>āśvāsa</s>), bewilderment (<s>mūḍhatā</s>),
accomplishment (<s>sādhana</s>), pursuit (<s>anugama</s>), sigh (<s>ucchvāsa</s>), wonder (<s>vismaya</s>), attainment (<s>prāpti</s>), and likewise ||6.299||
gain (<s>lābha</s>), forgetfulness (<s>vismṛti</s>), clashing (<s>saṃpheṭa</s>), expertise (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), awakening (<s>prabodhana</s>),

children.text: camatkṛtiś cety amīṣāṃ spaṣṭatvāl lakṣma nocyate // VisSd_6.300 //
children.translated_text: and astonishment (<s>camatkṛti</s>) — their definitions are not given because of their self-evidence. ||6.300||
Predominantly <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), consisting of a single act, endowed with the ten <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (dance-elements),
adorned by a <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester), a <s>viṭa</s> (libertine), and a <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (companion), ||6.301||
lacking <s>garbha</s> (development) and <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation) and two junctures, with a low-born hero,

children.text: svalpavattā sunepathyā vikhyātā sā vilāsikā // VisSd_6.302 //
children.translated_text: brief in extent, with fine costumes — that well-known form is the <s>vilāsikā</s> (the graceful play). ||6.302||
The <s>durmallī</s> has four acts and is endowed with the <s>kaiśikī</s> and <s>bhāratī</s> styles,
lacking <s>garbha</s> (development), with urbane male characters, adorned with a low-born hero. ||6.303||
In it, the first act consists of three <s>nālis</s> (time-units) and is filled with the sport of the <s>viṭa</s> (libertine);
the second act is of five <s>nālis</s> and features the playfulness of the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester). ||6.304||
The third act is of six <s>nālis</s> and features the playfulness of the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (companion);

children.text: caturtho daśanāliḥ syād aṅkaḥ krīḍita-nāgaraḥ // VisSd_6.305 //
children.translated_text: the fourth act should be of ten <s>nālis</s> and features the sport of the urbane hero. ||6.305||
The <s>prakaraṇī</s> (short invented play) is like a <s>nāṭikā</s> but with a caravan leader or similar person as hero,

children.text: samāna-vaṃśajā netur bhaved yatra ca nāyikā // VisSd_6.306 //
children.translated_text: and where the heroine is born of the same class as the hero. ||6.306||

children.text: hallīśa eka evāṅkaḥ saptāṣṭau daśa vā striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>hallīśa</s> (group dance) has a single act, with seven, eight, or ten women,
a single male character of elevated speech, the <s>kaiśikī</s> style, brilliance,
the <s>mukha</s> (opening) and final junctures, and abundant rhythm and tempo. ||6.307||
The <s>bhāṇikā</s> (short monologue) has refined costumes, possesses the <s>mukha</s> and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> junctures,
is endowed with the <s>kaiśikī</s> and <s>bhāratī</s> styles, and is composed as a single act. ||6.308||
The heroine is noble, the hero is mild; herein there are seven elements:

children.text: upanyāso 'tha vinyāso virodhaḥ sādhvasaṃ tathā // VisSd_6.309 //
children.translated_text: <s>upanyāsa</s> (introduction), then <s>vinyāsa</s> (arrangement), <s>virodha</s> (conflict), <s>sādhvasa</s> (alarm), ||6.309||

children.text: samarpaṇaṃ nivṛttiś ca saṃhāra iti saptamaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>samarpaṇa</s> (entrustment), <s>nivṛtti</s> (cessation), and the seventh, <s>saṃhāra</s> (conclusion).

children.text: upanyāsaḥ prasaṅgena bhavet kāryasya kīrtanam // VisSd_6.310 //
children.translated_text: <s>Upanyāsa</s> (introduction) is the incidental mention of the purpose. ||6.310||
The articulation of words of disillusionment is remembered as <s>vinyāsa</s> (arrangement).

children.text: bhrānti-nāśo vibodhaḥ syān mithyākhyānaṃ tu sādhvasam // VisSd_6.311 //
children.translated_text: The removal of delusion is <s>vibodha</s> (enlightenment); false narration is <s>sādhvasa</s> (alarm). ||6.311||
Words of reproach along with the torment of anger constitute <s>samarpaṇa</s> (entrustment) herein.
The presentation of an illustration is called <s>nivṛtti</s> (cessation). ||6.312||

children.text: saṃhāra iti ca prāhur yat-kāryasya samāpanam /
children.translated_text: The completion of the purpose is called <s>saṃhāra</s> (conclusion).
<s>Śravya</s> (auditory literature) is that which is merely to be heard; it is twofold: consisting of verse and prose. ||6.313||
Verse (<s>padya</s>) is that whose words are bound by metre; a free-standing [verse] is a <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse).

children.text: dvābhyāṃ tu yugmakaṃ sāndānitakaṃ tribhir iṣyate // VisSd_6.314 //
children.translated_text: A <s>yugmaka</s> (couplet) consists of two [verses]; a <s>sāndānitaka</s> (linked set) is composed of three. ||6.314||

children.text: kalāpakaṃ caturbhiś ca pañcabhiḥ kulakaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: A <s>kalāpaka</s> (cluster) consists of four; a <s>kulaka</s> (group) is considered to consist of five.

children.text: sarga-bandho mahā-kāvyaṃ tatraiko nāyakaḥ suraḥ // VisSd_6.315 //
children.translated_text: A <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem) is a composition bound into cantos; therein the single hero is a god, ||6.315||
of a noble family, or a <s>kṣatriya</s>, endowed with the qualities of a <s>dhīrodātta</s> (the noble and steadfast) [type].

children.text: eka-vaṃśa-bhavā bhūpāḥ kulajā bahavo 'pi vā // VisSd_6.316 //
children.translated_text: There may be many kings born of a single dynasty, or [multiple kings] of good family. ||6.316||
One of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), or <s>śānta</s> (peaceful) is the predominant <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: aṅgāni sarve 'pi rasāḥ sarve nāṭaka-sandhayaḥ // VisSd_6.317 //
children.translated_text: All [other] <s>rasas</s> are subordinate; all the junctures of a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) [are present]. ||6.317||
The plot is derived from <s>itihāsa</s> (epic history) or another [source] that shelters noble persons.

children.text: catvāras tasya vargāḥ syus teṣv ekaṃ ca phalaṃ bhavet // VisSd_6.318 //
children.translated_text: Its [goals encompass the] four human aims (<s>puruṣārthas</s>); among them, one should be the fruit. ||6.318||

children.text: ādau namaskriyāśīr vā vastu-nirdeśa eva vā /
children.translated_text: At the beginning there should be an obeisance, a benediction, or a statement of the subject matter;

children.text: kvacin nindā khalādīnāṃ satāṃ ca guṇa-kīrtanam // VisSd_6.319 //
children.translated_text: sometimes censure of the wicked and the like, and praise of the virtues of the good. ||6.319||
With verses in a single metre [throughout each canto], and different metres at the end;

children.text: nātisvalpā nātidīrghāḥ sargā aṣṭādhikā iha // VisSd_6.320 //
children.translated_text: the cantos (<s>sargas</s>) are neither too short nor too long, and number more than eight. ||6.320||
Sometimes a canto composed of various metres is also seen.

children.text: sargānte bhāvi-sargasya kathāyāḥ sūcanaṃ bhavet // VisSd_6.321 //
children.translated_text: At the end of a canto there should be an indication of the story of the coming canto. ||6.321||
Twilight, the sun, the moon, night, early evening, darkness, day,
morning, midday, hunting, mountains, seasons, forests, oceans, ||6.322||
union and separation [in love], sages, heaven, cities, sacrifices,
battle, military expeditions, marriage, counsel, the birth of a son, and so forth — ||6.323||
these are to be described as appropriate, with all their parts and sub-parts.

children.text: kaver vṛttasya vā nāmnā nāyakasyetarasya vā // VisSd_6.324 //
children.translated_text: The name of [the poem] is derived from the poet, the story, the hero, or another [element]; ||6.324||
the name of the canto is from the principal story of that canto.

children.text: asminn ārṣe punaḥ sargā bhavanty ākhyāna-saṃjñakāḥ // VisSd_6.325 //
children.translated_text: In a [poem] of the <s>ārṣa</s> (ancient/Vedic) type, the cantos are designated as <s>ākhyānas</s> (narrations). ||6.325||
In one composed in Prakrit, the cantos are designated as <s>āśvāsas</s> (assurances);

children.text: chandasā skandhakenaitat kvacid galitakair api // VisSd_6.326 //
children.translated_text: in one composed in [Prakrit] metre or <s>skandhaka</s> [form], sometimes also with <s>galitaka</s> [verses]. ||6.326||
In one composed in <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, the cantos are called <s>kuḍavakas</s>.
And likewise, various metres suitable for <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> [are employed]. ||6.327||
A poem that is free from the restriction of standard language and dialects, lacking canto-divisions,
with verses directed toward a single meaning, devoid of the full apparatus of junctures — ||6.328||
that is a <s>khaṇḍa-kāvya</s> (short poem), and it follows only one part of a [full] poem.

children.text: koṣaḥ śloka-samūhas tu syād anyonyānapekṣakaḥ // VisSd_6.329 //
children.translated_text: A <s>koṣa</s> (treasury) is a collection of verses that are mutually independent. ||6.329||
When composed in the sequence of a journey, that very [koṣa] is exceedingly delightful.

children.text: vṛtta-gandhojjhitaṃ gadyaṃ muktakaṃ vṛtta-gandhi ca // VisSd_6.330 //
children.translated_text: Prose devoid of any trace of verse is <s>muktaka</s> (free prose); that which has a trace of verse ||6.330||
is mostly <s>utkalikā</s>-type; and <s>cūrṇaka</s> (ground prose) is of four kinds.

children.text: ādyaṃ samāsa-rahitaṃ vṛtta-bhāg ayutaṃ param // VisSd_6.331 //
children.translated_text: The first is free from compounds; the second contains verse portions but is unconnected; ||6.331||
another is rich in long compounds; and the fourth has few compounds.

children.text: kathāyāṃ sarasaṃ vastu gadyair eva vinirmitam // VisSd_6.332 //
children.translated_text: In a <s>kathā</s> (narrative), an entertaining subject is composed entirely in prose. ||6.332||

children.text: kvacid atra bhaved āryā kvacid vaktrāpavaktrake /
children.translated_text: Here and there an <s>āryā</s> [meter] may occur, and occasionally <s>vaktra</s> and <s>apavaktra</s> [meters].

children.text: ādau padyair namaskāraḥ khalāder vṛtta-kīrtanam // VisSd_6.333 //
children.translated_text: At the beginning, salutation is in verse; the narration of the wicked one's [deeds is also in verse]. ||6.333||
An <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (prose romance) is like a <s>kathā</s>, [but] with the recounting of the poet's lineage.

children.text: asyām anya-kavīnāṃ ca vṛttaṃ padyaṃ kvacit kvacit // VisSd_6.334 //
children.translated_text: In it, and also of other poets, there are verses here and there. ||6.334||
The division of the narrative sections is bound [together] as an <s>āśvāsa</s> (chapter).
With the meter of <s>āryā</s>, <s>vaktra</s>, and <s>apavaktra</s>, or with any [other] meter, ||6.335||
at the beginning of each <s>āśvāsa</s>, there is a foreshadowing of future events through indirect suggestion.

children.text: gadya-padya-mayaṃ kāvyaṃ campūr ity abhidhīyate // VisSd_6.336 //
children.translated_text: A composition (<s>kāvya</s>) made of both prose and verse is called <s>campū</s>. ||6.336||
A royal eulogy in prose and verse is called <s>viruda</s> (panegyric).

children.text: karambhakaṃ tu bhāṣābhir vividhābhir vinirmitam // VisSd_6.337 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karambhaka</s> (medley) is composed in various languages. ||6.337||

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe
dṛśya-śravya-kāvya-nirūpaṇo nāma
ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, entitled 'Examination of Visual and Auditory Poetry,' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(7) Seventh Chapter: Determination of Faults (<s>Doṣa</s>)

children.text: rasāpakarṣakā doṣās te punaḥ pañcadhā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Faults are those that diminish <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment); they are considered to be of five kinds:

children.text: pade tad-aṃśe vākye 'rthe saṃbhavanti rase 'pi yat // VisSd_7.1 //
children.translated_text: they occur in a word, in a part of a word, in a sentence, in meaning, and also in <s>rasa</s>. ||7.1||
<s>Duḥśrava</s> (cacophony) is of three kinds: indecency, inappropriateness of meaning, and improper usage.
<s>Grāmya</s> (vulgarity), obscure meaning, ambiguous meaning, meaning requiring inference, and annihilated meaning — ||7.2||
inexpressiveness, contortedness, contradiction, and excessive length,
and unexamined predicate — [these are faults] of words and sentences. ||7.3||

children.text: kecid doṣā bhavanty eṣu padāṃśe 'pi pade 'paraṃ /
children.translated_text: Some of these faults occur in a part of a word; others in the [whole] word.
Meaninglessness, inability [to convey meaning], and defective grammar; ||7.4||
harshness of phonemes, and elided, damaged, or [improperly placed] <s>visarga</s>;
excess, deficiency, or misstatement of words; and broken meter — ||7.5||
falling excellence in <s>sandhi</s> (euphonic combination); disjunction, indecency, and awkwardness;
a single word [split] across half-verses; completion and resumption — ||7.6||
non-existence, relational incoherence, disorder, unacceptedness, and dependence on another's meaning;
and non-expression of what is intended, and broken sequence — ||7.7||
abandonment of the well-known [usage]; misplacement of words and compounds;

children.text: saṅkīrṇatā garbhitatā doṣāḥ syur vākya-mātragāḥ // VisSd_7.8 //
children.translated_text: confusion and embedding — these are faults belonging to the sentence alone. ||7.8||
Unsupported [meaning], poor sequence, vulgarity, contradiction, indecency, and awkwardness;
unrevised [meaning], causelessness, explicitness [of what should be implied], and inconsistency; ||7.9||
ambiguity and redundancy; contradiction with well-known [facts] and with [established] knowledge;
incompleteness, contradiction with concomitants, disjunction, and misplacement; ||7.10||
specification where there is no distinction, and restriction where there is none;
the reverse of those two; and the errors of injunction and restatement; ||7.11||
and redundancy that has been [falsely] cleared — these are declared as major faults.
The naming of <s>rasa</s> by its own word, and likewise of the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (dominant emotion) and <s>sañcāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion); ||7.12||
the manifestation [of rasa] being contrived with difficulty through <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) and <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant);

children.text: akāṇḍe prathana-cchedau tathā dīptiḥ punaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_7.13 //
children.translated_text: untimely expansion and cutting short; and repeated intensification; ||7.13||

children.text: {[*2] The following line from VisSd is missing here: paripanthir asāṅgasya vibhāvādeḥ parigrahaḥ}
children.translated_text: [Note: The following line from the Sāhityadarpaṇa is missing here: 'the obstruction of what is unconnected, the inclusion of vibhāva and the like.']
the non-pursuit of the principal [rasa], and the mention of what is not a limb [of rasa];
excessive expansion of a limb [of rasa]; and reversal of the natural dispositions; ||7.14||

children.text: arthānaucityam anye ca doṣā rasa-gatā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: impropriety of meaning, and others — these are considered faults pertaining to <s>rasa</s>.
Apart from these, faults of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figures of speech) have no [separate] existence. ||7.15||
When the speaker is filled with anger, or when the subject matter is elevated,

children.text: raudrādau ca rase 'tyantaṃ duḥśravatvaṃ guṇo bhavet // VisSd_7.16 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>raudra</s> (furious) and similar <s>rasas</s> — extreme cacophony becomes a virtue. ||7.16||
Indecency likewise, in the context of the commencement of lovemaking, assemblies, and the like.
In <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) and the like, annihilated meaning and improper usage would be non-faults. ||7.17||

children.text: guṇaḥ syād apratītatvaṃ jñatvaṃ ced vaktṛ-vācyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Obscurity of meaning becomes a virtue when it is [intended to show] the knowledge of the speaker or the addressee.

children.text: svayaṃ vāpi parāmṛśe kathitaṃ ca padaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_7.18 //
children.translated_text: Even a word already stated, when reconsidered by oneself, ||7.18||
when restating what has been prescribed, in sorrow, astonishment, anger,
in distress, in <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with changed meaning), in compassion, in appeasement, ||7.19||
when the addressee has shifted to another topic, in joy, in emphasis —
and when ambiguity culminates in ironic praise — ||7.20||
[is not a fault]. And when the subject being taught is primarily grammatical, or when the speaker [requires it],

children.text: kaṣṭatvaṃ duḥśravatvaṃ vā grāmyatvam adhamoktiṣu // VisSd_7.21 //
children.translated_text: awkwardness or cacophony [is not a fault]; nor is vulgarity in the speech of lowly [characters]. ||7.21||

children.text: nirhetutā tu khyāte 'rthe doṣatāṃ naiva gacchati /
children.translated_text: Causelessness in a well-known matter does not become a fault.

children.text: kavīnāṃ samaye khyāte guṇaḥ khyāta-viruddhatā // VisSd_7.22 //
children.translated_text: When poetic convention is well-established, contradiction with the well-known becomes a virtue. ||7.22||

children.text: mālinyaṃ vyomni pāpe yaśasi dhavalatā varṇyate hāsa-kīrtyoḥ raktau ca krodha-rāgau sarid udadhi-gataṃ paṅkajendīvarādi /
children.translated_text: Darkness is described in the sky and in sin; whiteness in fame; in laughter and renown, redness in anger and passion; the lotus and blue lotus are [said to be] in rivers and oceans;

children.text: toyādhāre 'khile 'pi prasarati ca marālādikaḥ pakṣi-saṅgho jyotsnā preyā cakorair jaladhara-samaye mānasaṃ yānti haṃsāḥ // VisSd_7.23 //
children.translated_text: the flock of swans and such birds spreads across all reservoirs of water; moonlight is beloved of <s>cakora</s> birds; in the rainy season, the swans depart for <s>Mānasa</s> [lake]. ||7.23||

children.text: pādāghātād aśokā vikasati bakulo yoṣitām āsyam adyair yūnām aṅgeṣu hārāḥ sphuṭati ca hṛdayaṃ viprayogasya tāpaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>aśoka</s> blossoms from the kick of a [woman's] foot; the <s>bakula</s> from the mouthfuls of women; garlands [expand] on the limbs of young men; the heart bursts from the heat of separation.

children.text: maurvī-rolamba-mālā dhanur atha viśikhāḥ kausumāḥ puṣpa-ketor bhinnaṃ syād asya vāṇair yuvajana-hṛdayaṃ strī-kaṭākṣeṇa tadvat // VisSd_7.24 //
children.translated_text: The bowstring is a garland of bees; the bow, and the arrows of the flower-bannered [<s>Kāma</s>] are made of flowers; the hearts of young people are pierced by his arrows, and similarly by the sidelong glances of women. ||7.24||

children.text: ahny-ambhojaṃ niśāyāṃ vikasati kumudaṃ candrikā śukla-pakṣe megha-dhvāneṣu nṛtyaṃ bhavati ca śikhināṃ nāpy aśoke phalaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: The day-lotus [blooms by] day; the night-lily blooms at night; the moonlight [shines] in the bright fortnight; peacocks dance at the sound of thunder; the <s>aśoka</s> should have no fruit;

children.text: na syāj jātī vasante na ca kusuma-phale gandha-sāra-drumāṇām ity ādy unneyam anyat kavi-samaya-gataṃ sat-kavīnāṃ prabandhe // VisSd_7.25 //
children.translated_text: the <s>jātī</s> [should bloom] only in spring; the sandal trees should not have [fragrant] fruit — and so forth. Other poetic conventions should be inferred [and employed] in the compositions of good poets. ||7.25||

children.text: dhanur jyādiṣu śabdeṣu śabdās tu dhanur-ādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For [the word] 'bow,' the words for bowstring and the like [are used]; and for bowstring and the like, the word 'bow' [stands].
These established [metonymies] are to be employed to convey such notions as mounting [a chariot] and the like. ||7.26||
In the speech of one submerged in bliss and the like, deficiency of words becomes a virtue.

children.text: kvacin na doṣo na guṇo guṇaḥ kvāpy adhikaṃ padam // VisSd_7.27 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes [a fault] is neither a fault nor a virtue; sometimes an extra word is a virtue. ||7.27||

children.text: samāpta-punar-āttatvaṃ na doṣo na guṇaḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Completion and resumption is sometimes neither a fault nor a virtue.

children.text: garbhitatvaṃ guṇaḥ kvāpi patat-prakarṣatā tathā // VisSd_7.28 //
children.translated_text: Embedding is sometimes a virtue; and so is falling excellence. ||7.28||

children.text: kvacid uktau sva-śabdena na doṣo vyabhicāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sometimes the naming of a <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion) by its own word is not a fault.
Where composition through <s>anubhāva</s> and <s>vibhāva</s> is not appropriate, ||7.29||
the speech that overrides a contradictory <s>sañcāri</s> and the like becomes a virtue;

children.text: virodhino 'pi smaraṇe sāmyena vacane tathā // VisSd_7.30 //
children.translated_text: also in the recollection of something contradictory, and in speech [showing] similarity. ||7.30||

children.text: bhaved virodho nānyonyam aṅginy aṅgatvam āptayoḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no contradiction when two [rasas] that have attained [their full form] stand as principal and subordinate to each other.

children.text: anukāre ca sarveṣāṃ doṣāṇāṃ naiva doṣatā // VisSd_7.31 //
children.translated_text: And in imitation [of another's speech], none of the faults are [actually] faults. ||7.31||

children.text: anyeṣām api doṣāṇām ity aucityān manīṣibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of other faults as well, the wise [recognize that] through propriety (<s>aucitya</s>),

children.text: adoṣatā ca guṇatā jñeyā cānubhayātmatā // VisSd_7.32 //
children.translated_text: both non-faultiness and virtuousness should be known, as well as the state of being neither. ||7.32||
Thus ends the seventh chapter, the Exposition of Faults, in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(8) Eighth Chapter: Determination of Qualities (<s>Guṇa</s>)
Just as valor and such are the attributes of a noble person, [so too] the qualities that belong to <s>rasa</s> as its principal [element]

children.text: guṇāḥ mādhuryam ojo 'tha prasāda iti te tridhā // VisSd_8.1 //
children.translated_text: are of three kinds: <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), and <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). ||8.1||
The delight that consists in the melting of the heart is called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).

children.text: saṃbhoge karuṇe vipralambhe śānte 'dhikaṃ kramāt // VisSd_8.2 //
children.translated_text: It predominates progressively in <s>saṃbhoga</s> (union), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos), <s>vipralambha</s> (separation), and <s>śānta</s> (tranquility). ||8.2||

children.text: mūrdhni vargāsty avarṇena yuktāṣ ṭa-ṭha-da-ḍhān vinā /
children.translated_text: The head consonants of the [five] classes combined with the vowel 'a,' excluding ṭa, ṭha, da, and ḍha,

children.text: raṇau laghū ca tad-vyaktau varṇāḥ kāraṇatāṃ gatāḥ // VisSd_8.3 //
children.translated_text: and the [consonants] ra and ṇa, and short [syllables] — these phonemes have become causes for its manifestation. ||8.3||

children.text: avṛttir alpa-vṛttir vā madhurā racanā tathā /
children.translated_text: A composition with no compounds or few compounds is sweet.

children.text: ojaś cittasya vistāra-rūpaṃ dīptatvam ucyate // VisSd_8.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is the expansion of the mind; it is called brilliance. ||8.4||
It predominates progressively in the <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), and <s>raudra</s> (furious) [rasas].
The phonemes combined with the first and third [consonants] of each class, and the last two of each [class], ||8.5||

children.text: upary adho dvayor vā sarephau ṭa-ṭha-ḍa-ḍhaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: above and below, or of both, with 'r' and 'eph' [i.e., ra and pha], together with ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, and ḍha,

children.text: śa-kāraś ca ṣa-kāraś ca tasya vyañjakatāṃ gatāḥ // VisSd_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and the letters śa and ṣa — these have become suggestive of it. ||8.6||
Likewise, a composition abundant in compounds and possessing an elevated arrangement.

children.text: śleṣaḥ samādhir audāryaṃ prasāda iti ye punaḥ // VisSd_8.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>audārya</s> (grandeur) — as for <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), some say ||8.7||

children.text: guṇāś cirantanair uktā ojasy antarbhavanti te /
children.translated_text: that the qualities declared by the ancients are subsumed within <s>ojas</s>.
Through the avoidance of vulgarity and cacophony, [the quality of] <s>kānti</s> (grace) and <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy) [arise]. ||8.8||
Sometimes equanimity (<s>samatā</s>), which has the nature of non-distinction of style, is a fault.
Its subsumption under the differently stated qualities is [to be understood] as appropriate. ||8.9||
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy), and <s>udāratā</s> (nobility) —

children.text: tad-abhāvasya doṣatvāt svīkṛtā anugā guṇāḥ // VisSd_8.10 //
children.translated_text: since the absence of these is a fault, they are accepted as accompanying qualities. ||8.10||
The clarity of meaning through natural description (<s>svabhāvokti</s>) and <s>alaṅkāra</s>, and likewise
of <s>rasa-dhvani</s>, <s>guṇībhūta-vyaṅgya</s> — [this quality] is named <s>kānti</s> (grace). ||8.11||
<s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion) is mere variety; non-fault is just equanimity.

children.text: na guṇatvaṃ samādheś ca tena nārtha-guṇāḥ pṛthak // VisSd_8.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) is not [a separate] quality either; therefore, qualities of meaning are not separate. ||8.12||

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe guṇa-vivecano nāma
aṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter, entitled 'Examination of Qualities,' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(9) Ninth Chapter: Determination of Style (<s>Rīti</s>)
<s>Rīti</s> (style) is the arrangement of words, like the particular configuration of limbs [in a body],

children.text: upakartrī rasādīnāṃ sā punaḥ syāc caturvidhā // VisSd_9.1 //
children.translated_text: serving as auxiliary to <s>rasa</s> and the rest; it is of four kinds: ||9.1||

children.text: vaidarbhī cātha gauḍī ca pāñcālī lāṭikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, <s>Pāñcālī</s>, and <s>Lāṭikā</s>.
A composition that is graceful in nature, with phonemes that suggest <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), ||9.2||

children.text: avṛttir alpa-vṛttir vā vaidarbhī rītir iṣyate /
children.translated_text: with no compounds or few compounds — that is regarded as the <s>Vaidarbhī</s> style.

children.text: ojaḥ prakāśakair varṇair bandha āḍambaraḥ punaḥ // VisSd_9.3 //
children.translated_text: A construction that is pompous, with phonemes that manifest <s>ojas</s> (vigor), ||9.3||

children.text: samāsa-bahulā gauḍī varṇaiḥ śeṣaiḥ punar dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: abundant in compounds — that is <s>Gauḍī</s>. With the remaining phonemes, in both [styles],
a construction having five or six words in a compound is considered <s>Pāñcālī</s>. ||9.4||

children.text: lāṭī tu rītir vaidarbhī-pāñcālyor antare sthitā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Lāṭī</s> style is situated between <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and <s>Pāñcālī</s>.

children.text: kvacit tu vaktrādyaucityād anyathā racanādayaḥ // VisSd_9.5 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes, however, due to the propriety of the speaker and the like, the composition and other [features] may differ. ||9.5||

children.text:
iti sāhitya-darpaṇe rīti-vivecano nāma
navamaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, entitled 'Examination of Style,' in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>.
(10) Tenth Chapter: The Essence of Figures of Speech (<s>Alaṅkāra</s>)
Those non-permanent properties of word and meaning that enhance beauty
and serve <s>rasa</s> and the rest — those are <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech), like armlets and the like. ||10.1||
Figures of Sound
When a meaning is apparently expressed with redundancy at first glance,

children.text: punar uktavad ābhāsaḥ sa bhinnākāra-śabdagaḥ // VisSd_10.2 //
children.translated_text: [but is actually not redundant,] that is <s>punaruktavad ābhāsa</s> (semblance of tautology); it involves words of different forms. ||10.2||
<s>Anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is the similarity of sounds even when the vowels differ.

children.text: cheko vyañjana-saṅghasya sakṛt sāmyam anekadhā // VisSd_10.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cheka</s> [anuprāsa] is the single occurrence of similarity of a group of consonants in multiple [ways]; ||10.3||
the similarity of many [consonants] in one way, or of many in multiple ways repeatedly,

children.text: ekasya sakṛd apy eṣa vṛtty-anuprāsa iṣyate // VisSd_10.4 //
children.translated_text: or of one [consonant] occurring once — this is regarded as <s>vṛtti-anuprāsa</s> (recurrent alliteration). ||10.4||
When a consonant, being pronounced in one place [of articulation] — palate, cerebral, and the like —
shows similarity [with another consonant of the same place], that is regarded as <s>śruty-anuprāsa</s> (phonic alliteration). ||10.5||

children.text: vyañjanaṃ ced yathāvasthaṃ sahāyena svareṇa tu /
children.translated_text: When a consonant in its original form, together with its accompanying vowel,
is repeated, being joined at the end [of a metrical foot] — that is <s>antya-anuprāsa</s> (end-rhyme). ||10.6||
When there is repetition of words and meanings only in purport [but not literally],

children.text: lāṭānuprāsa ity ukto 'nuprāsaḥ pañcadhā mataḥ // VisSd_10.7 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (Lāṭa-alliteration); thus <s>anuprāsa</s> is considered to be fivefold. ||10.7||
When the meaning is real, a sequence of vowels and consonants having a different meaning
is repeated in the same order — that is declared to be <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia). ||10.8||
If someone construes another's statement, which has a different meaning, in a different way,

children.text: anyaḥ śleṣeṇa kākvā vā sā vakroktis tato dvidhā // VisSd_10.9 //
children.translated_text: through <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) or <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice) — that is <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), and it is thus twofold. ||10.9||

children.text: śabdair eka-vidhair eva bhāṣāsu vividhāsv api /
children.translated_text: Where a sentence is composed using words of a single form across various languages —

children.text: vākyaṃ yatra bhavet so 'yaṃ bhāṣā-sama itīṣyate // VisSd_10.10 //
children.translated_text: that is considered <s>bhāṣā-sama</s> (linguistic equivalence). ||10.10||
<s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is said to be the expression of multiple meanings through words that are joined together;
[it arises] from letters, suffixes, genders, stems, and words. ||10.11||
Through <s>śleṣa</s> of case-endings, number, and language, it is eightfold.

children.text: punas tridhā sabhaṅgo 'bhaṅgas tad ubhayātmakaḥ // VisSd_10.12 //
children.translated_text: Again it is threefold: with word-break (<s>sabhaṅga</s>), without word-break (<s>abhaṅga</s>), and having both natures. ||10.12||
<s>Citra</s> (pictorial verse) is when letters serve as the cause of the visual form of a verse and so forth.
<s>Prahelikā</s> (riddle) is not a [true] ornament, since it obstructs <s>rasa</s>. ||10.13||
It is merely verbal ingenuity, [consisting of] dropped letters, supplied letters, and the like.

children.text: sāmyaṃ vācyam avaidharmye vākyaikye upamā dvayoḥ // VisSd_10.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> (simile) is the stated similarity between two things that are different, in a single sentence. ||10.14||

children.text: sā pūrṇā yadi sāmānya-dharma aupamya-vāci ca /
children.translated_text: It is complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>) if the common property, the word expressing comparison,

children.text: upamānaṃ copameyaṃ bhaved vācyam iyaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_10.15 //
children.translated_text: the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), and the object compared (<s>upameya</s>) are all stated. Furthermore, ||10.15||

children.text: śrautī yathevāvā-śabdā ivārtho vā vatir yadi /
children.translated_text: it is verbal (<s>śrautī</s>) when [using particles like] <s>yathā</s>, <s>iva</s>, <s>āvā</s>, or when <s>vati</s> [suffix] has the sense of <s>iva</s>;

children.text: ārthī tulya-samānādyās tulyārtho yatra vā vatiḥ // VisSd_10.16 //
children.translated_text: it is semantic (<s>ārthī</s>) when [using words like] <s>tulya</s>, <s>samāna</s>, and the like, or when <s>vati</s> has a synonymous meaning. ||10.16||

children.text: dve tad-dhite samāse 'pi vākye pūrṇā ṣaḍ eva tat /
children.translated_text: Both [verbal and semantic] occur in secondary derivatives (<s>taddhita</s>) and compounds — thus the complete simile is sixfold.

children.text: luptā sāmānya-dharmāder ekasya yadi vā dvayoḥ // VisSd_10.17 //
children.translated_text: The elliptical (<s>luptā</s>) [simile] is when one or two of the common property and other [elements] are omitted, ||10.17||

children.text: trayāṇāṃ vānupādāne śrauty ārthī sāpi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: or when all three are absent; it too is verbal or semantic, as before.

children.text: pūrṇāvad dharma-lope sā vinā śrautīṃ tu tad-dhite // VisSd_10.18 //
children.translated_text: Like the complete [simile], when the property is omitted, without the verbal type, in a secondary derivative — ||10.18||
in the two types prescribed for locus (<s>ādhāra</s>) and object (<s>karma</s>), [namely] <s>kyac</s> and <s>kyaṅ</s>,

children.text: karma-kartror ṇamuli casyād evaṃ pañcadhā punaḥ // VisSd_10.19 //
children.translated_text: and <s>ṇamul</s> for object and agent — thus it is again fivefold. ||10.19||
When the standard of comparison is omitted, it is twofold: in sentence and in compound.

children.text: aupamya-vācino lope samāse kvipi ca dvidhā // VisSd_10.20 //
children.translated_text: When the word expressing comparison is omitted, it is twofold: in compound and with <s>kvip</s> [suffix]. ||10.20||

children.text: dvidhā samāse vākye ca lope dharmopamānayoḥ /
children.translated_text: It is twofold in compound and in sentence when both property and standard are omitted.
That occurring in <s>kvip</s>-compound is twofold: with omission of property, <s>iva</s>-particle, and so on. ||10.21||

children.text: upameyasya lope tu syād eka pratyaye kyaci /
children.translated_text: When the object of comparison is omitted, there is one [type] with the <s>kyac</s> suffix.
Another [type] when both property and object are omitted; and one in compound when all three are omitted. ||10.22||
Therefore the varieties of <s>upamā</s> (simile) amount to twenty-seven in number.

children.text: eka-rūpaḥ kvacit kvāpi bhinnaḥ sādhāraṇo guṇaḥ // VisSd_10.23 //
children.translated_text: The common property may sometimes be uniform, sometimes different. ||10.23||
When different, there is a relation of image and reflection, or the difference is merely verbal.
<s>Eka-deśa-vivartinī upamā</s> (partially transformed simile) is [either] stated or implied. ||10.24||
Where the tasting of similarity is expressed — that is <s>rasanā upamā</s> (simile of relishing).

children.text: yathordhvam upameyasya yadi syād upamānatā // VisSd_10.25 //
children.translated_text: When the object compared itself successively becomes the standard of comparison — ||10.25||
that is <s>mālā upamā</s> (garland simile). Where many standards of comparison are seen for one [object],
and the same thing serves as both standard and object — that is <s>ananvaya</s> (non-sequential simile). ||10.26||
When two things alternately [serve as standard and object] — that is considered <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile).
The recollection of a thing through an experience of similarity is called <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance). ||10.27||
<s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is the superimposition of form on a subject without denial —

children.text: tat paraṃparitaṃ sāṅgaṃ niraṅgam iti ca tridhā // VisSd_10.28 //
children.translated_text: it is threefold: <s>paraṃparita</s> (successive), <s>sāṅga</s> (with parts), and <s>niraṅga</s> (without parts). ||10.28||
Where the superimposition of one thing is the cause of another superimposition —
that is called <s>paraṃparita</s> (successive), [and it has] connected (<s>śliṣṭa</s>) and disconnected (<s>aśliṣṭa</s>) forms. ||10.29||
It is fourfold: individual (<s>pratyeka</s>), simple (<s>kevala</s>), and garland (<s>mālā</s>) metaphor.

children.text: aṅgino yadi sāṅgasya rūpaṇaṃ sāṅgam eva tat // VisSd_10.30 //
children.translated_text: When the principal entity along with its parts is metaphorically identified — that is <s>sāṅga</s> (metaphor with parts). ||10.30||
It may pertain to the entire subject or be partially transformed (<s>eka-deśa-vivarti</s>).

children.text: āropyāṇām aśeṣāṇāṃ śābdatve prathamaṃ matam // VisSd_10.31 //
children.translated_text: When all the superimposed elements are verbal, the first [type, i.e., complete] is recognized. ||10.31||
When some [element] is semantic — that is the partially transformed (<s>eka-deśa-vivarti</s>) type.

children.text: niraṅgaṃ kevalasyaiva rūpaṇaṃ tad api dvidhā // VisSd_10.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Niraṅga</s> (without parts) is the metaphorical identification of [the principal] alone; it too is twofold — ||10.32||
being of garland and simple form — thus the varieties of <s>rūpaka</s> are eight.

children.text: dṛśyante kvacid āropyāḥ śliṣṭāḥ saṅge 'pi rūpake // VisSd_10.33 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes the superimposed elements are seen as connected (<s>śliṣṭa</s>) even in the <s>sāṅga</s> metaphor. ||10.33||

children.text: adhikārūḍha-vaiśiṣṭyaṃ rūpakaṃ yat tad eva tat /
children.translated_text: A <s>rūpaka</s> in which the superimposed element has a dominant established identity is precisely that [same metaphor].
When the superimposed [element] serves as the meaning of the subject and is useful for the topic at hand — ||10.34||
<s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) arises; it is twofold: equated (<s>tulya</s>) and co-referential (<s>tulya-adhikaraṇa</s>).
<s>Sandeha</s> (doubt) is the uncertainty regarding a real thing, arising from [perceived] similarity; ||10.35||
it is threefold: pure (<s>śuddha</s>), with embedded certainty (<s>niścaya-garbha</s>), and ending in certainty (<s>niścayānta</s>).

children.text: sāmyād atasmiṃs tad-buddhir bhrāntimān pratibhotthitā // VisSd_10.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhrāntimān</s> (delusion) is the cognition of one thing as another due to similarity, arising from [direct] perception. ||10.36||

children.text: kvacid bhedād gṛhītṛṇāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ tathā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Sometimes from the difference of perceivers, sometimes of objects perceived —

children.text: ekasyānekadhollekho yaḥ sa ullekha ucyate // VisSd_10.37 //
children.translated_text: the manifold appearance of one thing in various ways is called <s>ullekha</s> (delineation). ||10.37||
<s>Apahnutti</s> (concealment) is the denial of the real and the substitution of something else.

children.text: gopanīyaṃ kam apy arthaṃ dyotayitvā kathañcana // VisSd_10.38 //
children.translated_text: When some meaning that should be concealed is somehow revealed, ||10.38||
and then altered through <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) or otherwise — that too is <s>apahnutti</s>.

children.text: anyan niṣidhya prakṛta-sthāpanaṃ niścayaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_10.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Niścaya</s> (ascertainment) is the denial of the other and the establishment of the real. ||10.39||
<s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) is the imaginative identification of the real with something else.

children.text: vācyā pratīyamānā sā prathamaṃ dvividhā matā // VisSd_10.40 //
children.translated_text: It is primarily twofold: stated (<s>vācyā</s>) and implied (<s>pratīyamānā</s>). ||10.40||

children.text: vācye vādeḥ prayoge syād aprayoge parā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the stated [type], there is use of [particles like] <s>vā</s> and so forth; when they are absent, it is the other [implied type].

children.text: jātir guṇaḥ kriyā dravyaṃ yad utprekṣyaṃ dvayor api // VisSd_10.41 //
children.translated_text: The imagined [element] of both [types may be]: genus (<s>jāti</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>kriyā</s>), or substance (<s>dravya</s>). ||10.41||
Each becomes eightfold through the conception of existence and non-existence.

children.text: guṇa-kriyā-svarūpatvān nimittasya punaś ca tāḥ // VisSd_10.42 //
children.translated_text: And again, since the basis (<s>nimitta</s>) can be of the nature of quality, action, or essence, ||10.42||
they become thirty-two-fold. Among these, the stated varieties further,

children.text: vinā dravyaṃ tridhā sarvāḥ svarūpa-phala-hetugāḥ // VisSd_10.43 //
children.translated_text: excluding substance, are each threefold: pertaining to essence, result, and cause. ||10.43||
Those pertaining to essence are twofold: with or without statement of the basis.

children.text: pratīyamānā bhedāś ca pratyekaṃ phala-hetugāḥ // VisSd_10.44 //
children.translated_text: The implied varieties also are each [divided into] those pertaining to result and cause, ||10.44||

children.text: ukty-anuktyoḥ prastutasya pratyekaṃ tā api dvidhā /
children.translated_text: and each of those is again twofold according to whether the subject is stated or unstated.

children.text: alaṅkārāntarotthā sā vaicitryam adhikaṃ bhajet // VisSd_10.45 //
children.translated_text: When [<s>utprekṣā</s>] arises from within another ornament, it possesses additional charm. ||10.45||
<s>Atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is said to be when the imaginative assertion is treated as established fact.
[It involves:] identity where there is difference, disconnection where there is connection, and their reverses; ||10.46||
and a [reversal of] temporal sequence between cause and effect — thus it is considered fivefold.

children.text: padārthānāṃ prastutānām anyeṣāṃ vā yadā bhavet // VisSd_10.47 //
children.translated_text: When there occurs a connection through a single property ||10.47||
among things — whether those under discussion or others — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction).
When the relevant and irrelevant are [joined together], that is called <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator). ||10.48||

children.text: atha kārakam ekaṃ syād anekāsu kriyāsu cet /
children.translated_text: Now, when a single agent is [involved] in multiple actions —

children.text: prativastūpamā sā syād vākyayor gamya-sāmyayoḥ // VisSd_10.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile) is when two sentences have an implied similarity. ||10.49||

children.text: eko 'pi dharmaḥ sāmānyo yatra nirdiśyate pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Where a single common property is stated separately [in each clause] —

children.text: dṛṣṭāntas tu sadharmasyāpi vastunaḥ pratibimbanaḥ // VisSd_10.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is the reflection of a thing that also possesses the same property. ||10.50||
Whether the connection between things is possible or impossible somewhere —

children.text: yatra bimbānubimbatvaṃ bodhayets sā nidarśanā // VisSd_10.51 //
children.translated_text: where it conveys the relation of image and reflection, that is <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration). ||10.51||
The superiority of the object compared over the standard of comparison, or [its] inferiority —

children.text: vyatireka eka ukte 'nukte hetau punas tridhā // VisSd_10.52 //
children.translated_text: <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is threefold: when one [element] is stated, when unstated, and again when the reason [is given]. ||10.52||
Each of these four [types] is also [extended] through conveying similarity verbally or semantically,

children.text: ākṣepāc ca dvādaśadhā śleṣe 'pīti triraṣṭadhā // VisSd_10.53 //
children.translated_text: or through objection — becoming twelvefold; with <s>śleṣa</s> as well, three times eightfold [= twenty-four]. ||10.53||
Each [may be] individual or combined — thus forty-eight varieties again.

children.text: sahārthasya balād ekaṃ yatra syād vācakaṃ dvayoḥ // VisSd_10.54 //
children.translated_text: Where, by the force of concomitant meaning, one [word] expresses two [things] — ||10.54||
that is <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression). When the underlying [figure] is hyperbole,

children.text: vinoktir yad vinānyena nāsādhv anyad asādhu vā // VisSd_10.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence) is [the statement that] without one thing, the other is not good or is deficient. ||10.55||
<s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) is where, through qualifiers applicable equally [to two subjects],
the conventional usage of one thing is superimposed on the subject at hand. ||10.56||
When the stated qualifiers are purposeful [with a hidden intent], that is considered <s>parikara</s> (attendant).
The expression of multiple meanings through words that naturally [belong to] a single meaning is <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre). ||10.57||

children.text: kvacid viśeṣaḥ sāmānyāt sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Sometimes the particular [is inferred] from the general, or the general from the particular;

children.text: kāryān nimittaṃ kāryaṃ ca hetor atha samāt samam // VisSd_10.58 //
children.translated_text: the cause from the effect, the effect from the cause; or the equal from the equal — ||10.58||

children.text: aprastutāt prastutaṃ ced gamyate pañcadhā tataḥ /
children.translated_text: if through the irrelevant the relevant is understood — fivefold thus,

children.text: aprastuta-praśaṃsā syād uktā vyāja-stutiḥ punaḥ // VisSd_10.59 //
children.translated_text: that would be <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant). Then <s>vyāja-stuti</s> (ironic praise) is defined as: ||10.59||
when through stated blame or praise, praise or blame [respectively] is understood.

children.text: paryāyoktaṃ yadā bhaṅgyā gamyam evābhidhīyate // VisSd_10.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) is when the intended meaning is expressed indirectly. ||10.60||

children.text: sāmānyaṃ vā viśeṣeṇa viśeṣas tena vā yadi /
children.translated_text: If the general is established by the particular, or the particular by the general;

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇenedaṃ kāryeṇa ca samarthyate // VisSd_10.61 //
children.translated_text: and an effect is established by a cause, or [a cause] by an effect — ||10.61||
through similarity or through contrast — <s>arthāntara-nyāsa</s> (corroboration) is thus eightfold.
<s>Kāvya-liṅga</s> (poetic reason) is said to be when the reason has the nature of a sentence or word. ||10.62||

children.text: anumānaṃ tu vicchityā jñānaṃ sādhyasya sādhanāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the knowledge of what is to be proved from the means of proof, with poetic charm.
Through non-difference, a cause of expression of the reason together with what possesses the reason — ||10.63||
if [it states] what is favorable, what is unfavorable, or what produces the favorable,
for the purpose of specifically understanding the thing one wishes to state — ||10.64||
<s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) is an apparent prohibition; it is twofold: referring to what will be said or what has been said.

children.text: aniṣṭasya tathārthasya vidhyābhāsaḥ paro mataḥ // VisSd_10.65 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, an apparent injunction regarding an undesirable thing is considered the other [type]. ||10.65||

children.text: vibhāvanā vinā hetuṃ kāryotpattir yad ucyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhāvanā</s> (causelessness) is when the production of an effect without a cause is stated.
It is declared twofold: with stated or unstated reason. ||10.66||

children.text: sati hetau phalābhāve viśeṣoktis tathā dvidhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśeṣokti</s> (specification) is when there is absence of effect despite the presence of a cause; it too is twofold.

children.text: jātiś caturbhir jātādyair guṇo guṇādibhis tribhiḥ // VisSd_10.67 //
children.translated_text: Genus [is contradicted] by four things beginning with genus; quality by three beginning with quality; ||10.67||

children.text: kriyā ca kriyādravyābhyāṃ dravyaṃ dravyeṇa vā mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: action by action and substance; and substance mutually by substance —

children.text: viruddham iva bhāseta virodho 'sau daśākṛtiḥ // VisSd_10.68 //
children.translated_text: when they appear as if contradictory, that is <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), having ten forms. ||10.68||
<s>Asaṅgati</s> (incongruity) is when cause and effect are in different places.

children.text: guṇau kriye vā yat syātāṃ viruddhe hetu-kāryayoḥ // VisSd_10.69 //
children.translated_text: When two qualities or two actions are contradictory as cause and effect, ||10.69||

children.text: yad vārabdhasya vaiphalyam anarthasya ca saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: or when what is begun proves futile, or misfortune arises,

children.text: virūpayoḥ saṃghaṭanā yā ca tad viṣamaṃ matam // VisSd_10.70 //
children.translated_text: or there is a conjunction of incongruous things — that is considered <s>viṣama</s> (discordance). ||10.70||

children.text: samaṃ syād ānurūpyeṇa ślāghā yogyasya vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sama</s> (concordance) is the fitting praise of a worthy thing.

children.text: vicitraṃ yad viruddhasya kṛtir iṣṭa-phalāptaye // VisSd_10.71 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vicitra</s> (the marvellous) is the accomplishment of a contradictory thing for achieving a desired result. ||10.71||
When one of container and contained is superior, that is called <s>adhika</s> (the excessive).

children.text: anyonyam ubhayor eka-kriyāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ mithaḥ // VisSd_10.72 //
children.translated_text: When two things are mutually the cause of a single action — [that is <s>mithas</s> (reciprocity)]. ||10.72||
When the contained has no container, and one thing has multiple domains;

children.text: kiñcit prakurvataḥ kāryam aśakyasyetarasya vā // VisSd_10.73 //
children.translated_text: when something accomplishes an impossible task, or [accomplishes the task] of something else — ||10.73||

children.text: kāryasya karaṇaṃ daivād viśeṣas trividhas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: the accomplishment of a task by fate — <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) is thus threefold.

children.text: vyāghātaḥ sa tu kenāpi vastu yena yathākṛtam // VisSd_10.74 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāghāta</s> (obstruction) is when by some means a thing was made a certain way,

children.text: tenaiva ced upāyena kurute 'nyas tad anyathā /
children.translated_text: and by that very means another makes it otherwise.

children.text: saukāryeṇa ca kāryasya viruddhaṃ kriyate yadi // VisSd_10.75 //
children.translated_text: And if with ease the opposite of [what was intended] is accomplished — ||10.75||

children.text: paraṃ paraṃ prati yadi pūrva-pūrvasya hetutā /
children.translated_text: when each successive [element] is the cause of the one before it,

children.text: tadā kāraṇa-māla syāt tan mālā-dīpakaṃ punaḥ // VisSd_10.76 //
children.translated_text: then it is <s>kāraṇa-mālā</s> (chain of causes). <s>Mālā-dīpaka</s> (garland illuminator) is: ||10.76||
when [multiple] substrates are connected by a single property; and then successively,

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ prati viśeṣaṇatvena paraṃ param // VisSd_10.77 //
children.translated_text: each subsequent [element] serves as a qualifier of each preceding one — ||10.77||

children.text: sthāpyate 'pohate vā cet syāt tadaikāvalī dvidhā /
children.translated_text: if it establishes or negates, that is <s>ekāvalī</s> (single strand), twofold.

children.text: uttarottaram utkarṣo vastunaḥ sāra ucyate // VisSd_10.78 //
children.translated_text: Successive increase of excellence in a thing is called <s>sāra</s> (essence). ||10.78||
<s>Yathāsāṅkhya</s> (enumeration in order) is when listed items are [explained] in the same sequence.

children.text: kvacid ekam anekasmin ekaṃ caikaśaḥ kramāt // VisSd_10.79 //
children.translated_text: Sometimes one [action applies] to many, and one to each in turn — ||10.79||

children.text: bhavati kriyate vā cet tadā paryāya iṣyate /
children.translated_text: if it happens or is done [in rotation], then it is considered <s>paryāya</s> (alternation).
<s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is a mutual exchange with equals, inferiors, or superiors. ||10.80||

children.text: praśnād apraśnato vāpi kathitād vastuno bhavet /
children.translated_text: Whether from a question or without one, from a stated thing there arises

children.text: tādṛg anya-vyāpohaś cec chābda ārtho 'thavā tadā // VisSd_10.81 //
children.translated_text: the exclusion of something else of that kind — if verbal, it is <s>śābda</s>; if based on meaning, it is <s>ārtha</s>. ||10.81||
<s>Parisaṅkhyā</s> (enumeration) — if from the answer to a question there is an elevation (<s>unnaya</s>);

children.text: yac cāsakṛd asaṃbhāvyaṃ saty api praśna uttaram // VisSd_10.82 //
children.translated_text: and that which is repeatedly inconceivable, even when there is a question, [constitutes] the answer. ||10.82||
By the maxim of the stick and the cake (<s>daṇḍāpūpikā</s>), the arrival at another meaning is accepted as <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).
<s>Vikalpa</s> (alternative) is when two things of equal force are in contradiction due to an intervening obstacle. ||10.83||
<s>Samuccaya</s> (aggregation) is this: when one thing, being present, accomplishes the effect,
by the maxim of the hawk and the pigeon (<s>khalekapotikā-nyāya</s>), another that is devoted to it also [contributes]. ||10.84||

children.text: guṇau kriye vā yugapat syātāṃ yad vā guṇa-kriye /
children.translated_text: Two qualities or two actions may occur simultaneously, or a quality and an action [together].

children.text: samādhiḥ sukare kārye daivād vastv antarāgamāt // VisSd_10.85 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> (resolution) is when, in an easily accomplished task, through fate, an intervening object appears. ||10.85||
<s>Pratyanīka</s> (opposition) is when one who is unable to retaliate against an enemy
disparages something belonging to [the enemy], [thereby] establishing [the enemy's] superiority. ||10.86||
The imagining of a well-known standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) as the thing compared (<s>upameya</s>),

children.text: niṣphalatvābhidhānaṃ vā pratīpam iti kathyate // VisSd_10.87 //
children.translated_text: or the statement of [the comparison's] fruitlessness — that is called <s>pratīpa</s> (the reverse). ||10.87||
Having stated the extreme excellence of a supremely excellent thing,

children.text: kalpite 'py upamānatve pratīpaṃ kecid ūcire // VisSd_10.88 //
children.translated_text: even when [the thing] is imagined as a standard of comparison — some have called this <s>pratīpa</s> as well. ||10.88||
<s>Mīlita</s> (concealment) is the hiding of a thing by something having similar characteristics.
<s>Sāmānya</s> (generality) is the identity of the subject with another through similar qualities. ||10.89||
<s>Tadguṇa</s> (having its quality) is the abandonment of one's own qualities and the adoption of the qualities of something supremely excellent.

children.text: tad-rūpānahāras tu hetau saty apy atadguṇaḥ // VisSd_10.90 //
children.translated_text: But the non-adoption of [the other's] form, even when there is a cause [for adoption], is <s>atadguṇa</s> (not having its quality). ||10.90||
That which is recognized — a subtle meaning through a gesture, a hint,

children.text: kayāpi sūcyate bhaṅgyā yatra sūkṣmaṃ tad ucyate // VisSd_10.91 //
children.translated_text: or indicated by some oblique expression — is called <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle). ||10.91||

children.text: vyājoktir gopanaṃ vyājād udbhinnasya tu vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyājakti</s> (feigned speech) is the concealing by pretext of a thing that has become manifest.
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is the description of the intrinsic nature of actions and forms, the meaning of which is difficult to fathom. ||10.92||
When a wonderful thing of the past or future

children.text: yat pratyakṣāyamānatvaṃ tad bhāvikam udāhṛtam // VisSd_10.93 //
children.translated_text: is made to appear as if directly present — that is called <s>bhāvika</s> (the vivid). ||10.93||
An extraordinary wealth surpassing the world — that is called <s>udātta</s> (the exalted).

children.text: yad vāpi prastutasyāṅgaṃ mahatāṃ caritaṃ bhavet // VisSd_10.94 //
children.translated_text: Or even that which is the conduct of great ones, serving as a limb of the subject [being described]. ||10.94||
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>), as well as the cessation (<s>praśama</s>) of an emotion,
when they become subordinate [to the ornament] — then they are [themselves] <s>alaṅkṛtis</s> (figures of speech). ||10.95||

children.text: rasavat preya ūrjasvi samāhitam iti kramāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasavat</s> (possessing rasa), <s>preyas</s> (the pleasant), <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous), and <s>samāhita</s> (the composed) — in that order,

children.text: bhāvasya codaye sandhau miśratve ca tad-ākhyakāḥ // VisSd_10.96 //
children.translated_text: in the arising, the conjunction, the mixture [of emotion], and in its naming — they bear those designations. ||10.96||
If these very <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) are combined with one another,

children.text: tadā pṛthag-alaṅkārau saṃsṛṣṭiḥ saṅkaras tathā // VisSd_10.97 //
children.translated_text: then two separate figures [arise]: <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (blending) and <s>saṅkara</s> (intermixture). ||10.97||
When [figures] have an ancillary-principal relationship, and likewise when they share a single substratum,

children.text: sandigdhatve ca bhavati saṅkaras trividhaḥ punaḥ // VisSd_10.98 //
children.translated_text: and when there is doubt [as to which figure is present] — <s>saṅkara</s> (intermixture) is again of three kinds. ||10.98||
This composition, the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>, made by <s>Śrī Viśvanātha Kavirāja</s>, son of <s>Śrī Candrasekhara Mahākavi</s> —

children.text: sāhitya-darpaṇam amuṃ sudhiyo vilokya sāhitya-tattvam akhilaṃ sukham eva vitta // VisSd_10.99 //
children.translated_text: may the wise, having examined it, easily comprehend the entire essence of <s>sāhitya</s> (literary art). ||10.99||
As long as <s>Śrī</s> (Goddess Lakṣmī), whose face resembles the serene moon, adorns the lap of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: tāvan manaḥ saṃmadayan kavīnām eṣa prabandhaḥ prathito 'stu loke // VisSd_10.100 //
children.translated_text: so long may this composition, delighting the minds of poets, remain renowned in the world. ||10.100||
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Śrī Viśvanātha Kavirāja</s>, the emperor among rhetoricians, the great minister of war and peace.
